    the **asymptote**, not just the sign: sweep the candidate cause to the edge of its
    plausible range and ask whether it *can* reach the target, before crediting it with
    the gap. (Fact 603.)

308. **A parameter that changes the count of primitives, not their size, changes the
    asymptotic cost of code that has only ever run at one scale.** M25's power-law
    occluder drew ~55,000 discs where the control drew ~50, through a generator that ran
    a full 4176x4176 `np.maximum` per disc -- about 1e12 element-operations, and it
    presented as a hang, not as an error. It had always been fast because it had always
    been called with one scale. **Time one instance before committing to a long run**,
    and treat any parameter that multiplies primitive count as a cost change until shown
    otherwise. (Fact 606, M25 §11.8.)

309. **A detail metric built from a single statistic will fail on this sensor; the
    working one is a product of two.** Correlation statistics (FRC, FSC) measure
    recoverable information per ring and are **blind by construction** to any linear
    post-filter, because it scales common and uncommon power identically. Absolute-power
    statistics measure delivered energy and cannot tell signal from noise. Their
    **product** measures delivered signal. **Before proposing a new detail metric, state
    which of those two quantities it estimates**; if the answer is "one of them", it is
    already refuted by fact 617 or fact 618 and need not be run. (Facts 617-619.)

310. **Measure a region's rule-10 detector before calling it featureless.** A genuinely
    featureless ROI reads about 1.0; anything above roughly 2 has content, and a metric
    that fires there is detecting a real loss rather than raising a false alarm. Fact
    477's flat readings were correct detections misread as failures for a whole
    milestone, and the check that settles it costs one line. (Fact 615.)

311. **A false-alarm control needs a source that is both featureless and perturbable, and
    on a sensor with fixed-pattern noise no such source exists.** Removing the scene does
    not remove the structure. Do not write an acceptance bar that requires one -- use a
    **within-source contrast at matched cost**, which needs no featureless source. An
    agent that proves a bar unsatisfiable has done the job; failing against an ill-posed
    bar teaches nothing. (Fact 616.)

312. **When a negative control returns the same value as the live arm, ask what is
    common-mode between the two halves before blaming the estimator.** Two independent
    captures 76 s apart failed to decorrelate a flat ROI because FPN is common to the
    **sensor**, not to the stack -- and the FRC came out *higher*, not lower. The same
    mechanism kept the 0.4961 censoring alive across four windows and a pre-filter.
    (Facts 609, 612, 613.)

313. **Pair a statistic to remove a nuisance, never to create sensitivity.** Conditioning
    a detail reading on a flat reading made every incumbent metric worse -- `mean_grad`
    0.233 to 0.018 -- because the denominator moves with the numerator. A ratio cannot
    manufacture separation that neither term possesses. Only a statistic that already
    separates gains from being paired. (Fact 622.)

314. **Prefer a control that can return a wrong answer over one that cannot.**
315. **A measurement against a sensor model must record the commit it was taken at.** Fact 324's numbers were invalidated **twice in one day** -- by `2a4f5c5` at 09:41 and `f95f6f4` at 11:17 -- and nothing in the fact row, the report, or the shipped CLI text said which model produced them. Cite the commit or the number is not reproducible. (M52)
316. **A regression test that hard-codes measured data tests the code that consumes the data, never the claim.** `the_solved_gate_spans_the_range_fact_324_claims` passes today while two of its three assertions are false of the current pipeline. This is rule 35's disease in a form the rule does not name: not a constant asserted against itself, but a subject and object that are *both* frozen copies of one stale measurement. If a test exists to defend a fact it must recompute the fact, or be labelled as defending only the interpolator. (M52)
317. **When a ratio is formed between two measured arms, pair them per seed against a measured reference rather than dividing each by a published constant.** Fact 510 spent its entire verdict on an offset that paired ratios remove: +0.47% -> +/-0.018%. (M52)
318. **A homogeneity or invariance test whose correct answer is exactly 1 must be run on a *shared* realisation, not on independent draws per arm.** M52's step 06 read 1.068x for an operator whose true answer is 1.000000; step 07, on a shared realisation, read 1.000000 with deviation 0.00e+00. The 6.8% was the draw, not the operator. (M52)
319. **Before asserting that a measured effect is a defect in some code, read that code.** M52 was about to report a real, correctly measured, 64x homogeneity effect as a bug in a crate that already handled it correctly. The measurement was right and the accusation would have been wrong. (M52)
320. **A statistic assembled from two helpers written at different times must be re-derived as one expression before it is specified.** `sigpow` was an interpolated correlation times a nearest-ring power taken from one of two images; writing the product on a single ring collapsed it to `Re<A.conj(B)>` -- symmetric, exact, and stronger in every separation test. The defect was invisible in Python because both halves were obviously right on their own. (M46 App.A)
321. **When specifying for another language, enumerate the library defaults the source language chose for you, and measure what each one costs.** `numpy.hanning` is symmetric where DSP convention is periodic; `numpy.fft` is unnormalised forward; `float32` is silently upcast to `complex128`. The Hann convention alone is worth 1.5e-3, 146x the test tolerance. (M46 App.A)
322. **Set a test tolerance by bracketing it between a measured floor and a measured ceiling, and record both.** The floor is the largest difference a correct implementation may legitimately show; the ceiling is the smallest real defect. **A tolerance with no measured ceiling is not a test** -- it cannot be shown to have power. (M46 App.A)
323. **Golden vectors must include a case where the data structure, not the arithmetic, is wrong.** G7 drops 61 of 64 rings and is the only vector of eight that catches an index built from the uncompacted edge list. Every comfortable middle case passes with that bug present. (M46 App.A)
324. **Before shipping a derived quantity, measure the cost of what it actually repeats rather than what it appears to repeat.** Two half-merges look like 2x a merge; measured, they are 1.439x, and against a pipeline that is 98% decode the whole verification is 0.4%. A cost assumed rather than measured came within one decision of making a metric opt-in that should be default. (M46 App.A)
325. **A constant measured against a synthetic plant must say so at the constant, in the words "this does not depend on the camera profile".** `FOCUS_NOISE_SD` is correct and well-tested, yet a careful reader commissioned a change to it because its doc comment does not exclude the sensor. The cost of the missing sentence was a whole milestone of somebody's attention. (M48)
326. **Never quote a noise-model ratio without stating the signal level it was evaluated at.** A read-noise error of +18.6% at S = 0 is +0.345% at the median pixel of a real frame. **Dark-frame ratios flatter every read-noise argument by one to two orders of magnitude**, and did so twice in one milestone to the same author. (M48)
327. **A negative control that is bit-identical is what licenses reading a small delta as signal.** The 0.24% shift on `coffee-bubbles` would have been indistinguishable from run-to-run jitter had the ISO-50 placebo not come back identical in all four gates and all four columns. (M48)
328. **Read a fact's provenance column, not its headline, before deciding whether a change reaches it.** Facts 436 and 437 read like synthetic-plane results and are real-stack results. A blast-radius audit that skims headlines will clear facts it has not actually checked. (M48)
    `oracle_fsc` holds ground truth and is still worthless, because `FSC(H.L, L) = 1` for
    any real positive `H` -- its truth channel is degenerate. It was caught only because
    it returned an absurd +144 to +222 rather than a plausible 0.95. **A matched-cost
    design must also state which direction of the matching is feasible and report the
    infeasible one**; that the detail ROI's entire noise budget is worth less than a
    0.125 px blur is a stronger result than the bisection that failed to find it.
    (Facts 614, 621.)

329. **A noise fraction is a property of a sensor AT A SIGNAL LEVEL, and must be quoted with one.** `rho` = 0.3094 and `rho` = 0.0671 are both correct for this body at ISO 500 and differ by 4.6x because one is at S = 271 DN and the other at S = 0. **A fraction whose denominator moves with exposure is not a sensor constant**, and storing it as one hides an operating point inside a scalar. (M48b, fact 663)
330. **When an estimator's bias has the same shape as the effect under test, use a two-sample cross-statistic instead of correcting the bias.** Temporal noise leaking into a mean image is white, and the question was whether the fixed pattern is white; a subtracted pedestal would have left the answer resting on the accuracy of the subtraction, while a cross-spectrum between disjoint halves has no pedestal to subtract. (M48b, facts 664 and 675)
331. **Estimate precision from a second independent realisation, not from subdividing one.** Tiles of one plane gave +/-0.0002; the second green plane gave +/-0.016. **Only the latter can see a systematic that the whole plane shares.** (M48b, fact 665)
332. **A library object that hands back a view into a foreign buffer must be copied at the boundary, and the copy must be visible in the code.** `.astype()` copies and looks like a conversion; plain assignment does not copy and looks identical. Of two scripts carrying the same defect, one crashed and one published numbers. (M48b, fact 677)
333. **Check whether a pre-registered statistic is structurally zero over most of its population before you trust its verdict.** `deficit = winner - merged` is identically zero wherever `n_eff = 1`, which was 97.7% of the population it was chosen to decide. It still decided the stated question correctly; it was simply blind to the real defect, which had to be found outside it. (M54, fact 688)
334. **A statistic and the flag it is compared against must share a domain.** Counting a defect on luma while flagging it per-plane inflated a 0.0004-0.0028% population to 35%. Three milestones have now produced the same shape of error in three different quantities: frequency (fact 637), degree (fact 633) and now domain. (M54, fact 689)
335. **Price a proposed fix by its collateral ratio -- pixels changed per pixel it was meant to address -- before implementing it.** 29.6x to 238x, with 82-99% of the moved pixels never clipped at all, is a regression regardless of the sign of the intended effect. Prefer a repair whose blast radius is bounded by the population it addresses. (M54, facts 684 and 687)
336. **A rule that is inert exactly where its own stated mechanism already operates is redundant, not conservative.** Fact 203's prescription moves 0 pixels above half the support pinned, which is precisely where the argmax already flees on its own. (M54, fact 686)
337. **Print the constant the harness actually linked, not the one it was assumed to link.** M54's re-take under a changed calibration constant was bit-identical, and the reason was visible only because the harness echoed `sigma(0)`: it had already been building against the new value. Without that line the null result would have been indistinguishable from a stale binary. (M54, fact 690)
338. **A separation score whose denominator is a null residual is not a statistic.** `S = abs(d_signal)/(abs(d_signal)+abs(d_null))` looks like a normalised contrast and behaves like a random number when `d_null` is consistent with zero: 0.770 to 0.980 on one plant with only the repetition count varying. **Report the signal and the null separately, with the null's standard error, and let the reader form the ratio if it is defensible.** M55's corollary, which the corpus has not applied: **every separation number in this corpus quoted to three figures is over-precise** -- it names 0.937, 0.917, 0.990, 0.931, 0.973, 0.995, 0.994, 0.936, 0.982 and its own 0.523 and 0.464. (M55, fact 695; question 182)
339. **An identity verified numerically on one realisation is not an identity.** The way to test one is to vary the structure the derivation depends on -- parity of `n`, realness of the input, the FFT normalisation, the window -- not to re-run the same shape with new noise. Doing so here found a real unstated precondition that the numerical check could never have found. (M55, fact 699)
340. **A plant that holds the latent fixed cannot validate a metric whose largest real-data confound is latent drift.** Every plant in `m46lib` shares one latent object, which makes the asymmetry exactly 1 and the drift exactly 0 -- both by construction. This is rule 34's disease in a form rule 34 does not cover: the shared thing is an *object*, not a constant. (M55, fact 705; the shared-latent mechanism is M55's own and is folded nowhere else)
341. **Before trusting a metric, price its largest nuisance against its signal.** Here the split choice carries 50x the leverage of the effect under test and 1751x the leverage of the noise term, and the two cannot be varied independently on real data. **A metric is not realisable when a nuisance dominates, however well it separates on a plant.** (M55, fact 705)
342. **Golden vectors pin values; they do not pin properties.** A frozen spec with eight golden vectors and no monotonicity, homogeneity or sign-branch test cannot see an inverted decision rule, a degree-2 gain sensitivity or an undefined negative branch -- and did not. **Test the properties the decision rule depends on, not only the numbers it returns.** (M55, fact 711)
343. **A citation audit that checks number validity and a citation audit that checks content support are different instruments, and passing the first says nothing about the second.** M49 found every cited number resolved; M56 found 11 content defects among the same citations, 5 user-visible. **Resolving is not supporting.** (M56, fact 713)
344. **Line numbers in a fact row rot silently.** Two of the corpus's own line-number citations were wrong on the day they were checked (`profile.rs` `:25,:40,:45` -> `:72,:87,:92,:112`; `LADDERS` `:1833` -> `:1934`). **Cite by symbol name or by quoted content; treat a line number as a decaying hint.** (M56, facts 719 and 721)
345. **A prohibition written into the row it prohibits does not reach the code that quotes the row.** Fact 505 says its figure must not be quoted; it is quoted at five sites, one of them a `println!` in the example that measured the refutation. **If a number must not be quoted, the enforcement has to live where quoting happens.** (M56, fact 715)
346. **When you park a defect pending a verification, record what unparks it.** Fact 580 parked five sites pending M52. M52 landed and the park stayed, reading as a decision rather than a wait. **Name the unblocking event in the row.** (M56, fact 716)
347. **Two numbers that are individually correct can be wrong when paired.** `reference.rs` pairs one operator's gate with another operator's pixel fraction; both trace to real rows, both re-measure exactly, and the sentence is false. **This is the class of defect a number-validity check is structurally unable to see.** (M56, fact 722)
348. **Fixing a citation forces you to read the sentence around it, and that is where the second defect usually is.** Four label fixes surfaced two content errors that no audit had asked for, one of them the fixing agent's own, written in the same commit as the other. **Treat a wrong citation as a signpost, not as an isolated typo.** (M48, fact 727)
349. **Ask whether a citation is the BEST source, not merely a correct one.** A superseded-but-true row passes every check the corpus has, including the content audit of facts 713-723. Only fact 585, which adjudicates the constant by name, actually licenses it. (M48, fact 729)
350. **A process rule that hard-codes one tool's output string forbids every tool that prints a different one.** Rule 33 demanded a `Compiling` line; `cargo clippy` and `cargo check` emit `Checking`, so the rule was unsatisfiable for half the commands it governed and cost four invocations before anyone checked. **State the property, then enumerate the strings each tool uses to express it.** (M48, fact 730)
351. **A red exit code is not evidence of the red you wanted.** A power probe that expects an assertion to fail must confirm the failure is *the assertion*. `cargo test` exiting 101 with the output filtered away was one step from being logged as a passing probe; the real cause was a `const HP_TOL: f32` against `f64` operands. **Re-run unfiltered and read the failure text.** (Fact 741's sibling; rule 33 in the power-probe direction.)
352. **Test a candidate bound against both epochs, not just today's.** A threshold set from the current measurement is encoding today's data no matter how one-sided it is. Run it against the numbers on the far side of a known calibration change: **a bound that passes both is encoding the claim** (facts 747, 748). This is the cheapest discriminator the corpus has found and it caught a defect the author was actively removing.
353. **A claim of the form "X is large" is asserted as a one-sided bound**, set from where the claim stops meaning anything rather than from the measurement. Two-sided bands around a measured value go false at the next recalibration and take the claim down with them; the one-sided form has now survived two (fact 747).
354. **A verbal caveat in a report is not a caveat on the artifact.** The committed log outlives the report and is read without it. If a script's output carries a confound, the *script* prints the warning (fact 744).
355. **When a constant is corrected, grep for its CLAIMS, not just its value.** Three independent instances of one failure -- a correction landing in one artifact and not its siblings -- were found by hand at high cost (fact 743). The value-grep passes every time; the sentences around it are where the staleness lives.
356. **Encode a refutation in the type, not in a comment.** `FlatReference` has no single-frame accessor, so fact 441's defect is unrepresentable rather than discouraged (fact 736). Prefer this to a warning block whenever the API allows it.
357. **Locate a refutation at the derivation, not at the nearest constant.** A refuted ratio does not implicate its inputs; changing the constant to fix the printed quotient can break every other consumer of that constant (fact 753). And **substituting a corrected number into a refuted inference leaves the inference refuted** (fact 754).
358. **Separate the quantity under test from the quantity that labels the test.** A plant may use a calibrated constant to set its size, provided the statistic being validated does not divide by that same constant (facts 738, 740). If it must, say so in the report instead of reporting a clean pass.
359. **Before reporting that data is not on this machine, check every corpus root.** `D:\personal\macro` holds 15 stacks; `C:\dev\macro\test` holds three. A search that stops at the first root produces a false 'cannot verify' (fact 756).
360. **Amend the sentence a reader hits first.** An amendment applied to the cell you happened to be reading, leaving the row's headline asserting the opposite, is worse than no amendment -- the row now looks checked (fact 761). After any amendment, re-read the whole row and ask whether its first sentence is still true.
361. **A refutation applies to its own target, not only to the target's dependents.** A sweep framed as "what leans on this?" structurally excludes the thing being leaned on (fact 760). Amend the refuted row first, then sweep.
362. **A row that states a count must be checked against its own enumeration**, in the same reading. Fact 725 said seven and listed eight in the next sentence (fact 759).
363. **A substring match on a citation is not a citation check.** `M25 fact 200` matches `M25 fact 200a`, which is a different claim with a different resolution. Match to a word boundary and read the site (facts 726, 763).
364. **Fidelity to a source and correctness are different properties, and folding optimises only the first.** Re-derive any arithmetic a source states about its own table, especially decorative counts that no conclusion depends on -- those are exactly the ones nobody checks (fact 762).
365. **A site list is not a defect list.** An audit that enumerates by string match returns a superset in one direction and a subset in the other, simultaneously (facts 768, 770). Before fixing N sites, read what each sentence needs: two sites quoting the same number may need different numbers, and one of them may already be right.
366. **Exit codes are evidence of neither outcome.** Not of the success you wanted (fact 776: a restore failed silently while its block returned 0) and not of the failure you wanted (discipline 351: a type error read as a passing power probe). **Read the content back.**
367. **Check whether a number is unmeasured before instructing anyone to caveat it as unmeasured** (fact 769). `1.815` was labelled CORPUS in a routing brief and is measured three times to 0.21%.
368. **Search the codebase for a working instance before recording that none exists** (fact 771). Question 170 asked for a correct citation form that was already committed in four places.
369. **When a source corroborates the very thing it refutes, fold both halves.** M55 refuted `sigpow`'s separation numbers and, in the same section, measured the canonical form ABOVE the old one at matched repetitions. Only the refutation was folded. **The omission that runs in your own argument's favour is the one to go looking for.** (M58 omission 1, fact 640)
370. **A deletion audit is not finished until it is reconciled against what you claimed.** `d7eedfa` counted two and deleted three, and the missed one was a blank line -- invisible to the filter, invisible in the render, and load-bearing for item anchoring. **Count from the diff, not from memory, and count blank lines.** (M58 L10, fact 780)
371. **Search the corpus for the question before commissioning the milestone, and name what you found in the brief.** Two briefs were written onto answered questions while their reports sat in the index. **The corrective is not a check, it is a sentence in the brief**: state the prior report, and state that "this is already settled" is a successful outcome -- otherwise the agent's incentive is to produce a finding. (Fact 782, rule 40)
372. **When a count changes with a threshold, check whether the THRESHOLD moved.** Two experiments here gave opposite ISO trends -- counts up 20x, counts down 350x -- purely because both thresholds were ISO-dependent. **The fix is not a better threshold but no threshold: measure a fixed population.** (M48c, fact 789)
373. **A signal with a known INVARIANCE is worth more than a signal with a large amplitude.** Dark current's value here is not that it is big; it is that it **cannot** depend on the ISO dial. That one invariance breaks the gain/read-noise degeneracy that dark `sigma_DN` alone can never break. **Look for the quantity whose value you know a priori, not the one with the best signal-to-noise.** (M48c, facts 790, 793)
374. **A selective estimator lifts every high-contrast pixel, so any "the estimator concentrates X" claim needs a contrast-matched control.** Without one this milestone would have reported that the merge concentrates defects by 23-44%; with one the defect-specific component is zero within 8%. (M48c, facts 798, 799)
375. **Estimate reproducibility by RE-DRAWING, not by propagating.** Two draws of a matched control differed by 8% -- larger than any error bar computable analytically, and free. Compare fact 665, where a precision estimated by subdividing one measurement was wrong by two orders of magnitude. (M48c, fact 800)
376. **A bitmask is not a boolean, and numpy will not tell you.** `uint16_bitmask & bool_array` silently extracts bit 0 and raises nothing; the counts stay plausible. **Any array whose semantics are "bit k means condition k" must be loaded through a named accessor, never indexed directly.** (M48c, fact 805)
377. **Exclude the mundane explanation from metadata before claiming the interesting one.** Two EXIF reads -- integration time and capture timestamp -- eliminated the two cheapest alternatives to a headline result, and the interleaved capture order was the stronger exclusion of the two. (M48c, fact 792)
382. **Rule 39 binds PER CELL, not per claim.** An error bar borrowed from a neighbouring sweep configuration is not an error bar. M57 read a jackknife `se` off the gate-0.00 row (0.259 px) when its contrast used gate-0.99 (0.069 px), and on that basis called a real result unbelievable. **The error was conservative and it was still an error.** (M57, fact 815)
383. **An instrument built on the same key as the instrument it replaces inherits its blind spot.** M49 audited citations by number and missed content; M56 was hired to fix that, **built an index keyed on the fact number**, and produced two bad counts about what citations *say*. If the new instrument must see something the old one could not, **the key has to change, not just the question**. (M56, fact 828)
384. **Mark unrecoverable findings unrecoverable; never reconstruct them.** A reconstructed finding presented as a measured one is worse than an admitted gap, because the reason it matters is that someone is relying on evidence they cannot check. Facts 714, 718 and 720 remain unverified and say so. (M56, fact 829)
385. **A stale constant confined to a subset of rows has a fingerprint, and the fingerprint is a reusable triage rule.** `LADDERS` is wrong on exactly the ISO-50 rungs because of `max(iso, 100)`. **Once the fingerprint is named, the blast radius can be enumerated instead of re-measured.** Look for the predicate that selects the wrong rows before auditing them one at a time. (M56, fact 824)
386. **When a metric hunt fails, the product claim becomes two-dimensional -- and that is an outcome, not a defeat.** Four milestones went looking for one number that would say "sharper and quieter". The measured answer is "quieter, and here is the cost in sharpness". **A contested single number is worth less than an honest pair.** (M57, facts 813, 814)
387. **Ask for the whole optical path by name, not for "the gear".** A circular polariser was in front of most of the corpus for the entire project (fact 845 -- **not all of it, which was my own unchecked generalisation**) and surfaced only in passing, three weeks in -- after a teleconverter had already surfaced the same way. **Filters, teleconverters, extension tubes and diffusers all change the measurement and none of them appear in the EXIF fields anyone checks.** Enumerate the path element by element. (fact 832)
388. **A renamed input is a silent failure, not a loud one.** A glob whose directory disappeared returns zero files and raises nothing, so a pipeline keeps running and measures nothing. **Any script reading an external corpus should assert a non-zero file count before it does arithmetic** -- one line, and it converts a silent wrong answer into an error. (fact 831)
389. **Recording a defect is not repairing it.** I folded a new fact naming fact 627's wrong scoping clause and left the clause exactly where it was, so the decision record simultaneously asserted the error and documented it. **A row that describes another row's error, without touching that row, leaves the error in the place people actually read.** If you find a defect while folding, repair the source row in the same commit. (fact 837)
390. **Check emphasis balance per ITEM, with code spans stripped -- never per line.** Numbered items wrap across continuation lines, so a per-line `**` count produces about eighty false positives here and hides the four real ones. Group each item with its continuations, strip `` ` ``-delimited spans, then count. **Nothing had ever run this and four disciplines had been mis-rendering.** (fact 844)
391. **Provenance the owner cannot recall is not recovered by asking harder -- date-order the corpus and look for a rule.** Asked which stacks carried the polariser, the owner could name some and not others. The EXIF capture dates resolved it into a single clean boundary (25 May) that covers every stack including the ones he could not recall, and turned an open-ended contamination into one falsifiable claim. **Reach for the metadata the camera wrote before the memory of the person who was there.** (facts 845, 846)
392. **An inference you hand a subagent as a premise must be labelled as an inference.** I told M61 the corpus contained three ISO 100/400 matched pairs. I had inferred this from EXIF and filename similarity and had not verified it; two of the three were different angles and depths. Stated as fact, it would have produced a confounded gain-boundary result that looked clean. **Rule 12's MEASURED/DERIVED/ARGUED labels apply to briefs, not only to reports** -- and I violated this again in the same message (fact 846). (fact 847)
393. **Never invent a citation namespace at fold time.** I relabelled M53's per-turn findings as a flat `F1`-`F10` while folding, and twenty-five rows then cited labels that appear in no artifact. **A citation the source never used is worse than a vague one, because it manufactures false precision** -- it reads as a pointer into a document and resolves to nothing. If a brief tells an agent to number locally, the fold must carry the local numbering **and the turn that scopes it**, or record a hash instead. (facts 850, 851)
394. **An audit's findings carry a timestamp; re-check every "X does not exist" claim against HEAD before folding it.** Twice now I have folded a report-is-missing finding that had already been repaired -- fact 765 (26 minutes stale) and fact 843 (8 minutes stale, folded 2 minutes after it went stale). **Absence claims decay faster than any other kind, because live agents are actively producing the thing whose absence is being asserted.** The substance survived both times by luck. Re-run the existence check yourself; it costs one command. (fact 853)
395. **A check can be correct in its logic, fire reliably, produce a plausible-looking list, and still be measuring the wrong object.** M59's line-ending check named 13 files and every one was an artifact of the author's `core.autocrlf` setting. **Nothing in a red exit code distinguishes that from a real finding.** Discipline 351 one level up: it is not enough to confirm that the failure is your own check firing -- confirm the check is looking at the thing you meant. Judge the committed blob, not the working copy; and **a check that guesses is worse than a check that abstains.** (fact 859)
396. **Count rows by what the renderer will do, not by what a regex matches.** A blank line inside a markdown table terminates it, so 458 of 639 fact rows were rendering as paragraph text while a check that regex-matched `^\| N \|` reported all of them present. **The check measured the text; the reader sees the render.** Any structural check on a markup document must model the markup. (fact 857)
397. **Build the null by permuting the data, not by resampling the statistic's internals.** A roll, a rotation or a subject swap answers "what would this read on data that cannot contain the effect?"; no internal resampling can. **Quote every real-data reading with its null z. A reading a null reproduces is not a reading, whatever its standard error says.** This dissolved a whole class of prior readings at 48 FFT pairs per cell. (facts 861, 862)
398. **Fix a signal step in the physical quantity, never in the operator's units.** "0.05 px of blur" sounds small and is -- 0.376% of MTF. "A 10% MTF loss" is checkable against a lens. Every separation number in two published facts was conditioned on a step three tenths of one percent in the quantity being measured, and nobody noticed because the units hid it. (fact 864)
399. **A threshold without a specificity measurement is a wish.** Before publishing a decision threshold, feed it pairs that differ **only in noise** and count how often it fires. A +-0.003 threshold measured 75% false alarms at realistic noise while its sensitivity was a perfect 1.00. **Sensitivity is the easy half and it is the half everyone reports.** (fact 866)
400. **Monotonicity and homogeneity gates cannot reject a metric that measures nothing** -- a constant passes both. Only a two-sided power test, with a specificity arm, can. Any battery whose gates are all one-sided is measuring conformity, not capability. (fact 867)
401. **Pin a nuisance in the spec AND measure its leverage anyway.** Pinning stops it being *chosen* wrong; it does not stop it being *implemented* wrong. (M55b section 1.1)
402. **State the threat model a monotonicity claim is made under.** An adversary requiring an amplitude 145x-602x anything the physical system can produce characterises a *class* of statistics; it does not disqualify one member of it. Without the bound, a refutation and a curiosity look identical. (fact 865)
403. **A pre-registered spec may be amended only if the amendment can be shown not to have been tuned.** Three conditions, all checkable by a third party: **no candidate yet exists**, the trigger is **external** to the candidate set, and the amendment can only **tighten**. An amendment that could loosen a threshold is indistinguishable from tuning, whatever its motive -- and the evidence is a full re-run showing not one number moved. (fact 873)
404. **A kill condition that no code reads is prose.** Every threshold in a spec's constant table must be traceable to a line that enforces it, **and the enforcement must be shown rejecting a planted violation.** Two of this spec's own thresholds sat unenforced until a directory rename forced the function open. (fact 871)
405. **Calibrate an acceptance battery against a known-bad reference AND a passability probe before publishing it, and commit the intermediate logs.** A gauntlet nothing can pass is not a gauntlet; a gauntlet everything passes has no power. **Both directions must be measured, and the revision history is part of the evidence.** (M55b section 6)
406. **Golden vectors pin values; they do not pin properties.** A frozen spec must freeze monotonicity, homogeneity, swap invariance and the negative branch as **executable assertions**, or a rewrite that preserves every stored number can still destroy every property they were chosen to demonstrate. (M55b section 9)
407. **An executable spec must be bit-reproducible by a third party, so never serialise a set.** A `set` literal's iteration order follows `PYTHONHASHSEED`; three output lines reordered across runs with every value identical. **A spec whose artefacts are compared by hash would have reported a false regression.** Compare parsed JSON, not bytes. (fact 875)
408. **Treat an uncommitted experiment file as already lost.** `open(p, "w")` **truncates before it validates its own arguments**, so a script that fails on its first line can still destroy its input. Commit before patching, or patch via a temp file and `os.replace`. Recovery from `.pyc` is possible and was done here, but comments do not survive it. (fact 874)
409. **A one-sided hedge applied to the wrong population is not conservative -- it is wrong.** "These are lower bounds because the polariser suppresses speculars" is sound reasoning and was applied to three stacks that had no polariser. **The direction argument being a theorem does not protect you if the premise is false for the case at hand**; it makes the error invisible, because the hedge still reads as caution. Check the population before trusting a hedge's direction. (fact 877)
410. **When a claim you broadcast turns out false, correcting your own copy is not the fix -- enumerate the recipients.** I told five agents the polariser was in the path for every corpus frame before checking. **Three of the corpus's twelve stacks are on the other side of that boundary**, so any hedge an agent applied on my word to `112MSDCF`, `113MSDCF`, `119MSDCF` or `109MSDCF` is not conservative, it is simply wrong. A broadcast claim needs a broadcast retraction, and the recipient list is knowable. (facts 845, 877)
411. **To decide whether a constant inherits a confound from the data that established it, read its DECLARATION, not its provenance.** `CONTAINER_MAX_DN` was established partly on a stack of unknown optical provenance and is immune, because it is 2^14-1. **The same question -- "is this constant contaminated?" -- has an algebraic answer for some constants and an empirical one for others, and the declaration is what tells you which.** (fact 879)
412. **When a premise is retracted, grep the corpus for its dependants the same hour -- and record the ones that SURVIVE, not just the ones that fall.** Fact 861 retracted the contiguous split; one grep found nine mentions, three live dependants and one survivor. **Recording fact 706 as "checked and unaffected" is the load-bearing half**: without it a later reader cannot distinguish a fact that was examined and held from one nobody looked at, and will either re-do the audit or distrust the whole family. (fact 881)
413. **Immunity to a retracted premise is READ, not re-measured -- from the declaration for a constant, from the construction for a statistic.** `CONTAINER_MAX_DN` is immune because it is 2^14-1; M53's flat-ROI statistic is immune because its denominator is a median over every frame. **Neither answer required opening a single frame**, and both were available the same hour the premise fell. Reach for the definition before scheduling a measurement. (facts 879, 883, discipline 411)
414. **An exposure audit belongs in the committed report, not only in the reply that requested it.** M53's own words: a milestone whose twenty-five fact rows spent a day citing an artifact that did not exist should not answer "what else is exposed?" in chat, because **that is the same failure with a shorter fuse.** The list will be cited when the finding propagates; a citation into a conversation is not a citation. (M53 section 10)
415. **Flag an uncertain item as uncertain instead of guessing, even when the guess would be right.** M53 flagged two recollections it had not reconstructed; one (M2's placebo A) was correct and closed with a single grep. **The flag is what bought the check, not the doubt** -- a confident guess in the right direction is never re-examined, so its correctness is luck that looks like knowledge. (fact 884)
416. **A direction argument that is valid in form makes its premise feel checked.** M54's own words, and the mechanism behind discipline 409: "suppressing speculars can only lower the clipped population" is a theorem, and the confidence it earns transfers illegitimately to the *premise* that a polariser was fitted. **The soundness of the inference is precisely what stops anyone auditing its input.** Both M54 and I proposed such a hedge within an hour; neither of us checked the premise. (facts 877, 885)
417. **A negative control is only as strong as the ABSENCE of the instrument, not the zero in the count.** Four stacks with zero clipping are a powerful control if the lens was bare and a worthless one if a filter was suppressing speculars, **and the count is identical either way.** Before quoting a zero as evidence, state what else could have produced it and rule that out by provenance rather than by magnitude. (fact 885)
418. **Never allocate a milestone number while another agent is still producing reports under it.** I dispatched a second `M60` while M54 was authoring `M60` and `M60c`, making every `M60` citation ambiguous -- including folded ones. **The linter cannot catch this: it checks structure inside files and has no notion of milestone identity.** Allocate from the report index, not from memory of the highest number dispatched. (fact 888)
419. **An acceptance test is not the arm that passes -- it is the arms that fail.** M62 ran six selector configurations against the sqrt(N) invariant and all six failed, including the shipped binary at 0.7690x, **and two placebos landed on 1.0000 to four digits.** Without the failing arms, a merge scoring 5.4778x is a number; with them it is a measurement. **Report the separation, never the score alone.** (facts 889, 890, 892)
420. **Derive the harness's own expected value analytically BEFORE running it, and check the derivation against the instrument's printed output.** M62's choice of reference decides whether the ceiling is unbounded or 1.3912 -- **and a harness capped at 1.3912 would have reported a correct merge as failing, indistinguishably from a real failure.** The derivation matched the CLI's own output to 0.03%, which is what makes the headline falsifiable rather than merely impressive. (fact 893)
421. **Transmit a fact to an agent in its corrected form and the correction never has to be sent.** Four agents got my universal polariser claim and needed retracting; the one whose brief carried the date rule needed nothing, and grepped clean. **The difference in cost was entirely in how the brief was written.** When a fact is known to be contested or recently repaired, put the repaired form in the brief rather than the convenient summary of it. (fact 897)
422. **Write a verdict to BOTH namespaces: the fact that establishes it and the question it settles.** M59's A4 check found **4 of 125 questions** carrying a verdict asserted only in section 4. **The fold naturally writes where the evidence is, not where a reader looks**, so a question list decays into overstating how much is unknown -- and one of the four had retired a systematic the corpus was applying everywhere. (fact 898)
423. **Measuring a rate is not reading the instances.** M59 argued a check down to advisory from a 32% residual without reading the six cases; four were real defects and the two false positives were grammatical, fixable by rule. **A summary statistic is precisely the thing a check exists to replace, so deciding a check's fate by one is circular.** Read every instance before demoting a check, or before shipping it. (fact 899)
424. **If a check strips markup before counting, assert the stripper's own residue.** A silent stripper failure is unfalsifiable from the output: every dependent check goes quietly green instead of loudly red, **converting absence of evidence into evidence of absence across the entire instrument.** This is the one check worth keeping if all others must go. (fact 902)
425. **A fixture that asserts nothing happened must prove it could have.** Pair every silent fixture with an exclusion control -- the same input with only the trigger removed -- or a fixture that is silent because nothing matched will pass as a fixture that is silent because the exclusion worked. **Discipline 250's dead check, one level up, inside the test suite.** (fact 903)
426. **When a check is calibrated in-sample, write its DEMOTION condition into the code.** M59's A4 exclusions were derived from the only two false positives available, so its 0% false-positive rate is in-sample and cannot be otherwise. **The failure mode of such a check is not that it breaks -- it is that the exclusions get widened until the number goes away.** Name that failure in the docstring, where the person about to commit it is standing. (fact 904)
427. **A recovery is complete when the last dangling pointer reaches the map, not when the map is written.** I folded M53's namespace recovery, recorded the rule-31 gap as CLOSED, and left 21 fact rows citing labels that resolve to nothing without a document the rows do not name. **The satisfying artifact -- the reconstruction -- is not the deliverable; the repaired references are.** After any recovery, count the citations that still point at the broken form. (fact 905)
428. **When a check cannot be built, name what the missing information IS and propose the convention that supplies it.** M59 refused a milestone-identity check after measuring all three candidate signals -- 80% false positives on filename, 292-of-293 single authorship, and unrelated slugs on the legitimately multi-part milestones. **The reason generalises: the distinction is not a property of the filesystem, it is who was dispatched and what they were asked, and nobody wrote that down.** A reasoned refusal plus a convention beats a check that infers intent from spelling. (facts 906, 907)
429. **A fix that makes a check MORE FORGIVING must be regression-tested against the commit where its true positives were known.** Every loosening arrives looking like a bug fix and each is individually defensible -- **which is exactly how a calibrated check dies quietly.** M59 removed 9 false positives and proved all 4 true positives survived, at a named sha. Without that pin, "I improved the check" is an assertion. (fact 910, discipline 426)
430. **A probe must IMPORT the shipped matcher, never reimplement it.** M59's first held-out probe reimplemented A4 and reported 9 residual defects against a linter that no longer produced any. **The failure direction is the expensive one: it reports a defect that does not exist, inviting a fix to code that is already correct.** (fact 912)
431. **"Not measured" and "not measurable" are different claims -- never let one stand in for the other.** A4's false-negative rate requires an enumeration of every real inconsistency in the corpus, which is the thing the check exists to produce, so it is unobtainable rather than merely unobtained. **Say which, because a reader can act on the first and can only accept the second.** (fact 913)
432. **Before an instrument judges a change, ask what passes it while being wrong.** M62's square-root-N battery scores a merge that has **stopped discriminating focus entirely** exactly the same as a correct estimator, because a static burst is degenerate for focus. **The headline number was not wrong; its authority over the next change was an unexamined assumption.** Every acceptance test should be interrogated for the degenerate pass before it is trusted, and the guard added must have measured power (fact 917). (facts 916, 917)
433. **Check every required criterion for the direction it FORECLOSES.** M62's first pre-registration would have auto-rejected the intended outcome of the change it existed to certify. **The failure mode is not bias toward a result -- it is a criterion that makes the outcome under test impossible to pass.** Separate control arms from decision arms by role: a control scoring unexpectedly high is a **loss of control**, not a failure, and at least one control must retain power or the verdict is "cannot certify". (fact 918)
434. **An acceptance harness whose verdict depends on its author is not an instrument.** Take the binary from an environment variable, keep every arm -- subcommand, flags, tolerance -- in a data file, and report an unsupported invocation as `UNSUPPORTED` rather than crashing. **Then prove reproduction digit-for-digit across multiple HEADs**, because a single clean run cannot distinguish a stable instrument from a lucky one. (fact 919)
435. **A quantity DERIVED through a chain of constants must not be used to change any constant in that chain until it is measured directly.** M48c derived a 2.174x gain discrepancy from hot-pixel dark current read *through* the shipped gain relation, excluded the obvious causes, and still refused to touch a constant. **M61's direct photon-transfer measurement then refuted it outright.** Acting on the strongest derived result available would have broken a correct constant -- **the derivation was not weak evidence, it was evidence about a different thing.** (facts 920, 921; discipline 326)
436. **In a shared working tree, commit with `git commit -- <paths>`. Never `git add <paths>` followed by a bare `git commit`.** The first scopes the commit; the second scopes only the staging and then writes the entire shared index, sweeping in whatever a concurrent agent staged in between. **A `git diff --cached` audit does not protect you -- it is a separate command and nothing holds the index still.** "Never `git add -A`" is necessary and not sufficient. (facts 930, 931)
437. **Pre-register where a test HAS POWER, not merely which direction it should point.** An ordering test between two readings that are both inside the null is a coin flip, and reporting it as a failure is as wrong as relaxing it. **State the precondition under which the observable is meaningful, and report cells outside that precondition as "no power" rather than as pass or fail.** (fact 929, discipline 433)
438. **A rule validated on one ROI class has not been validated.** Nullity in the split-half test partitions cleanly on ROI content -- flat ROIs inside the null, detail ROIs outside -- so no splitting rule can be certified globally from a single class. **Stratify every acceptance cell by ROI content and report the strata separately**, because a mixed pass rate averages two different answers into one meaningless number. (fact 926)
439. **If two gates in a spec can both apply to one cell, the spec must say which wins.** B6 and B9 give opposite verdicts on flat-ROI parity cells that section 4 explicitly expects to occur. **A spec capable of two verdicts on one input is unfinished, and the gap surfaces only when a cell lands in the overlap -- so enumerate the overlaps deliberately rather than waiting.** (fact 928)
440. **Check what a delta is a delta OF, not just whether its endpoints look right.** Fact 23's regularisation effect and fact 71's operator effect both run ~34.4% to ~1% on the same ROI, agreeing to within 16% **by coincidence** -- and that near-agreement is precisely why a ring-operator number propagated to four sites as if it were Tenengrad's. **Near-agreement between two measurements of different things is a propagation hazard, not a reassurance.** (facts 932, 933)
441. **Do not run the measurement that decides a question in the same milestone that framed it.** Framing and answering in one pass conceals whether the framing was chosen to fit the answer. **Name the missing measurement, state the current claim as ARGUED, and leave your own report incomplete** -- M60c did this unprompted over a measurement costing one boolean. (fact 935, discipline 419)
442. **`cargo doc --no-deps` is a real check and nothing else in the workspace runs it.** It found three unresolved intra-doc links that `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and 220 passing tests all pass over -- and for a documentation-only change it is **the only command that exercises the edit at all.** (fact 936)
443. **A plant that an older clause already catches proves nothing about the new one.** M55's first plants failed because a pre-existing per-subject clause fired before the amendment was reached -- the plant passed for a reason unrelated to the thing under test. **Place plants where the PRE-amendment code demonstrably passes, and show that it does.** This is a control lacking power, arriving from the opposite side. (fact 941)
444. **Prove a tightening against the REAL pre-amendment code, extracted from history.** M55 loaded `b6_rollup` via `git show 54a8305` and ran 64 exhaustive configurations: 0 newly accepted. **A paraphrase of the old behaviour tests the author's memory of it, not the behaviour.** Pair with byte-identity checks on the functions that must not have moved. (fact 940, discipline 429)
445. **When two checks appear to conflict, ask whether one tests the INPUT and the other tests the CANDIDATE.** B9 asks "can anything be measured in this cell?"; B6 asks "given a readable cell, is the answer right?". They are **sequential, not competing**, and the apparent contradiction was a vocabulary error. **Never resolve such a conflict by exempting the hard cells -- an exemption is a silent drop. Name the cell `NO-POWER` and keep it in the battery.** (facts 937, 938)
446. **A threshold that cannot fire is dead code, and the fix is to annotate it, not re-cut it.** B6's advertised 90% bar is unreachable at real subject sizes -- 0 of 2324 failure placements trip it first. **Retuning a number after seeing which cells fail is exactly the tuning a pre-registered spec exists to prevent**, so the honest repair is to record that the clause cannot fire and leave it. (fact 942)
447. **If rule 40 made you read the other instrument first, say so -- convergence is not corroboration when one party read the other.** **[UNTESTED -- see fact 946. Every observance so far has been free, because the convergence was genuine anyway. The real test is a case where the reading order makes the agreement worthless.]** State the reading order, name what genuinely predates the other work, and distinguish a shared taxonomy from an independently derived mechanism. (fact 944)
448. **Do not narrow a true general result with a conditional -- a hedge that implies an escape hatch which does not exist is a false suggestion of scope, not caution.** M55's redundancy proof holds for every subject composition; recording it "at the real subject sizes" would have invited a reader to think a different held-out set could revive a dead clause. **Where an enumeration covers the boundary and algebra covers the rest, label them separately: MEASURED for the enumeration, DERIVED for the universal form.** (facts 942, 945)
449. **An audit that is a SEPARATE COMMAND from the operation it guards cannot constrain that operation in a shared tree.** Prefer an intrinsically scoped operation over an unscoped one preceded by a check. `git diff --cached` before `git commit` is the canonical failure: it was *true when it ran* in both recorded sweeps. **This is the same "necessary but not sufficient" shape as every commit-hygiene rule this project wrote before rule 42** -- the check describes a state, the operation acts on a later one. (facts 930, 952; M64's D3)
450. **Where a default ships a CONSTANT, guard the spread across every available subject -- not one.** M64 widened the degeneracy guard from the one stack it was given to all seven and found that the nominated baseline was **not** the worst case; `coffee-bean` beat `109MSDCF` by 1.33x. **A constant is a claim about the whole population, so a single-subject guard is a category error, however careful the subject choice was.** (facts 948, 917)
451. **Do not move a pre-registered default after seeing that another value scores better on your own instrument.** Gate 8 beat M64's pre-registered 4.0 on the acceptance battery and it shipped 4.0 anyway, routing the question to the instrument's owner. **A pre-registration abandoned the moment it costs something was never a pre-registration** -- and the temptation is strongest when the better number came from your own pre-check, where no one would have seen the change. (fact 950)
452. **Do not pose a mechanism question as a binary unless you have enumerated the space.** My brief asked "sensor or decode" for the B-plane deficit; the answer -- an in-camera digital scale before quantisation -- is **neither**, and a less careful agent would have picked the nearer of two wrong options. **A forced-choice question makes an agent's report look decisive and its content wrong.** Ask what the mechanism is and what observable separates the candidates. (fact 955)
453. **Name the instrument's blind spot in the same breath as its result.** A PTC ratio found the B-plane deficit and **algebraically cannot identify it** -- `var/mean -> s*g` is the same under a digital scale and a gain change. **A measurement that establishes an effect is not thereby evidence about its cause**, and the gap is invisible unless the estimator is written down. (fact 956)
454. **A confound you find after the fact is worth less than one you named before, and the re-test passing does not change that.** M61 omitted highlight linkage from its pre-registration, went back and attacked its own ceiling test with it, and **reported the omission as an error rather than the recovery as diligence.** The distinction matters because the failure mode of a missed confound is a result that **looks clean while being void**. (fact 957)
455. **When a rule is broken repeatedly by the very edits that discuss it, replace the rule with a tool.** Rule 29's header deletion has recurred five times and **every recurrence was inside an edit about the previous one** -- so awareness is not the missing ingredient. Same shape as discipline 449: a rule describes a hazard, it does not enforce anything. (fact 960)
456. **Honour the consequence your pre-registration attached to an unmet criterion, even when you can argue the criterion was wrong.** M65's K5 failed on every stack; section 4.3 said that voids D1; **M65 voided D1** -- while supplying, and declining to lean on, a sound argument that the criterion's floor was unreachable. **Reporting NOT MET and then proceeding as though it were met is the same act as rewording it.** (fact 965)
457. **A downstream smoother cannot beat the window of the operator feeding it.** A 17x17 regulariser over a 27x27 operator removes 19% of response noise, not the ~82% independent samples would give, because the samples are already averaged. **Size a regulariser against the operator's correlation length, not against its own footprint.** (fact 964)
458. **Two quantities that both respond to the same knob are not thereby the same quantity.** 56.70% of pixels change winner while the acceptance set moves 0.44% -- a 129-fold separation between the index map and the admitted set. **Co-movement under an intervention is the reason conflations survive review**, not a defence against them; separate them by the intervention that moves one and not the other. (facts 963, 934)
459. **A signal that separates cleanly is not thereby the signal you named it after.** Bimodality at occluding edges fires at **78.3%** with **AUC 1.000** and is a **single-depth defocus side-lobe**. **AUC measures separation from the control you chose, not correspondence to the mechanism you believe in** -- so the control that matters is the one where your mechanism is *absent but the surface phenomenon is present*. A silhouette on blank card cost almost nothing and killed the interpretation outright. (facts 967, 968)
460. **Test reproducibility across two captures of the same scene before interpreting a per-pixel detection.** M63's bimodality flags did not agree between two 299-frame captures of one scene (kappa ~ +0.11). **A detection that does not survive re-shooting the same subject cannot support a reconstruction regardless of what it means**, and this test is cheaper than any mechanism study. The corpus has same-scene repeats (`bee-1`/`-2`/`-3`) and they should be used this way routinely. (fact 968c)
461. **When a proposal argues several capabilities fall out of one object "for free," price them separately -- they can fail independently.** The unified posterior was argued to yield merge weights, confidence, occlusion detection and a no-frame-in-focus flag from one structure. Measured: occlusion is a side-lobe, entropy adds ~0.01 AUC over peak height, and boundary mass has **no population**. **The elegance of a single object is an argument for implementing it once, never evidence that each thing it is claimed to do is real.** (fact 969)
462. **An acceptance instrument whose objective saturates cannot also choose the parameter it scores.** M62's battery is maximised on the half-line [8, infinity) -- every point of which admits every frame -- so tuning the gate to its argmax builds the degeneracy the battery exists to detect. **Where a score is monotone up to saturation, its argmax is a statement about the instrument, not the system.** Check for an interior optimum before treating a maximum as a recommendation. (fact 973)
463. **Never measure from a build artefact you did not observe being built.** `Finished in 0.10s` with no `Compiling` lines proves freshness, **not authorship** -- and in a shared tree freshness with respect to *someone's* change is not the same as freshness with respect to yours. M62 rebuilt rather than trust `target/`. Same shape as discipline 449. (fact 976)
464. **State a limitation without a conditional unless you have checked that the conditional's escape hatch exists.** "My fixture cannot arbitrate this" implies a better fixture could; M62 checked, found its own fixture fails identically, and restated it as **no fixture of this class can**. **A hedged limitation directs future effort down a road you have not verified is open.** (fact 975; extends discipline 448)
465. **Try the algebra before the apparatus.** M66 settled the project's most expensive open question -- is a fixed gate an N-dependent statement -- with a **pointwise strict inequality**, and used measurement only to size the effect. **The measure-first discipline is right when the mechanism is unknown and wasteful when it is derivable**; ask which case you are in before building a harness. (fact 979)
466. **A criterion you are confident will pass earns its keep by failing.** M66's K1 was a formality -- gate 0 must admit everything -- and it failed at 1.0000058, exposing `<=` admitting **exact f32 ties**. K2 failed by having a **false premise**, not an unmet threshold. **Do not drop 'obvious' criteria from a pre-registration to save effort; they are the only ones positioned to catch what you are not looking for.** (fact 983)
467. **When a milestone finds something bigger than its charter, it must flag and NOT chase it.** M66 found `FOCUS_NOISE_SD` running 19-21% low on real texture -- larger than the N-dependence it was sent to measure -- and left it post hoc and unruled. **Chasing it would have meant deciding a question in the milestone that discovered it**, the exact failure M60c refused (discipline 441) and the reason M65 exists. (fact 984)
468. **Apply a result about the subject to the instrument that measured it.** M66 proved `Gate::tolerance()` states a fixed threshold against a null that drifts with N; M62 checked its own guard G and found **the identical defect -- a fixed 0.95 line, no N in its statement.** **An instrument built to detect a class of error is not thereby immune to it**, and the check costs one reading. **Every bare-constant threshold in this corpus should now be checked for an unstated N.** (fact 987)
469. **Retire your own cautions when the evidence removes them.** M62's warning that the guard omits the five largest stacks was **inverted** by M66's finding -- larger N carries *more* margin. **A scoping caution costs nothing to leave in place and misdirects effort indefinitely**, so it must be revisited by whoever wrote it whenever new evidence touches its premise. (fact 988)
470. **Read the source report, never the orchestrator's summary of it, when ruling.** M62 caught a conflation of two configurations in my fold -- an N=19 *prefix* figure presented as an at-own-N result -- by going to M66's tables. **A second-hand number is a different claim from the number**, because the configuration travels separately from the value and is the first thing lost. (fact 981; compare fact 925)
471. **A rounded display is not a measurement.** M62 reported an arm's `n_eff` as "exactly 1" from a 3-decimal display; it is 1.0000058, and the same criterion exposed `<=` admitting exact f32 ties. **Where a value is asserted as an identity, check it at full precision or state it as a tolerance.** (fact 991a, fact 983)
472. **A conservative error and an optimistic error of equal magnitude are different objects -- but the claim that you have one must state the REGIME it was measured in.** **CORRECTED: this discipline originally read "a partial correction can be worse than no correction" on M68's authority, and M68 withdrew that.** The partial B-plane fix is *smaller* in magnitude than no fix at almost every read-noise share; it is worse only in the pure-dark limit. **What survives is the sign flip -- conservative to over-confident -- concentrated exactly where a sigma-denominated gate adjudicates.** **Couple the constants; do not prohibit the partial fix.** (facts 994, 997)
473. **Locate a mechanism by where the NOISE is generated, not by where the SIGNAL is scaled.** M61 derived its separating observable from the signal path and got the sign inverted -- source-follower noise arises *downstream* of `q/C`, so a conversion-gain difference leaves dark sigma flat at 1.00, not at 0.84. **A separating observable derived from the wrong stage of the chain will confirm whichever hypothesis you started with.** (fact 993)
474. **Commit your disagreement with the record BEFORE you measure.** M68 put its refutation of M61's physics into committed code ahead of the run, so the disagreement could not be back-fitted to the result. **A pre-committed objection is evidence; the same objection raised afterwards is interpretation.** (fact 993)
475. **A failed gate is not licence to guess why it failed.** M68's D1 uniformity gate failed; it withdrew the dependent estimate, then ran E1 and **refuted its own explanation of the failure** -- the gradient was common to R and B, not a blue property. **The obvious reading of a gate failure is a hypothesis and needs its own test.** (fact 995)
476. **Ask whether the REGIME is robust, not only whether the number is.** I put two questions to M68 -- is the sign robust, does it hold across the range -- and the sign held while the range did not, which retracted the headline. **A confirmation request that only re-checks the value cannot catch a scope error**, and scope errors are what survive peer review. (fact 997)
477. **Scope a withdrawal as carefully as a claim.** M68's failed uniformity gate withdrew `f`, a position estimate; it did not touch the ratio underneath, which survived on two independent arms. **Discounting everything downstream of a failed gate destroys sound results** -- name the quantity the gate actually bore on. (fact 999)
478. **Say which of your numbers are not yours.** M68 volunteered, unasked, that the gain factor in its own recommendation was M61's and had never been re-measured. **A recommendation assembled from constants of mixed provenance must label them**, or the weakest link inherits the credibility of the strongest. (fact 998)
479. **Register the DIRECTION of your instrument's bias before you run it.** M67 stated in advance that its PSF is symmetric and monotone by construction and its validation suite blind to the PSF, so **every accuracy number is an upper bound and every failure number a lower bound.** **A simulator cannot falsify the assumption built into it**; naming which way it lies is the only honest use of it. (fact 1003)
480. **Distinguish NOT MEASURED from NOT MEASURABLE.** The first routes to a milestone, the second routes to the owner as a capture request. M67 ruled per-pixel focus correctness not measurable on the corpus and amended `captures-needed.md` with the exact capture that would change it. **Conflating the two either wastes a milestone or silently drops a requirement.** (fact 1005)
481. **When a pre-registered criterion fails on a subset, check whether an independent guard already predicts that subset.** M67's C1 failed on 3 of 10 cells; they are exactly the cells M62's guard G fails, and that guard was built for an unrelated purpose. **Two instruments drawing the same boundary is evidence the boundary is real** rather than an artefact of one arbitrary threshold. (fact 1002)
482. **An agent may refute a test the orchestrator specified, and should.** My brief asked M67 for a frame-subsetting test; it is **bit-exact vacuous** against a hard gate, which M67 established by reading `merge.rs` rather than by running it. **A method proposed in a brief carries no authority over the code.** (fact 1005)
483. **A resolving citation is not a verified claim.** M67's asymmetry assertion cited a real fact in a real report; the evidence underneath it was **a fit that saturated its grid, inside the one gate that milestone FAILED.** `corpus_lint` C1 proves a citation *resolves* -- it cannot prove the cited thing was *measured*. **Trace to the measurement, not to the citation.** (fact 1006)
484. **Prefer an invariant to a fitted ground truth.** M67's cylinder test uses `k*(x,y)` being independent of `y` for any surface of revolution -- true whatever the radius, so **nothing on that axis can be tuned into agreement.** A fitted geometry can absorb the error it is meant to expose. (fact 1008)
485. **State the class of failure your test cannot detect, in its pre-registration.** M67 specified in advance that its proposed axial arm is blind to a bias constant in `y` -- **a failure mode it had already measured** (`devmax` 8.25-8.34 frames at `H` ~ 1: large but smooth). **A blind spot disclosed afterwards reads as an excuse; disclosed in advance it is a scope.** (fact 1009)
486. **A possessive on the apparatus is not a claim of authorship.** *"Measured on my own plant"* describes the PLANT. M62 named M66 as the finder in the same sentence, and said *"I implemented nothing"* four lines later. **I read the possessive and stopped reading.** When a report credits a number, the reading that matters is who ran it, and that is a different word in the sentence than the one that catches the eye.
487. **Both of my errors this cycle were against reports that stated the opposite IN PLAIN WORDS.** M62 wrote *"No re-run... I implemented nothing"*; I recorded a replication. M62 wrote *"the real branch is not run because no real burst exists"*; I told M69 the burst was delivered. **The failure mode is not misreading. It is not reading** -- substituting a summary, including my own, for the source. The fix is mechanical: **before a claim about another milestone enters a brief or the record, open that milestone's report at the line.**
488. **Name synthetic plants and real captures apart, in the record, at every mention.** Fact 889's *"30-frame static burst"* is SYNTHETIC, and the phrasing is what seeded my error: it reads as a capture. **Any fact whose plant is synthetic must say so in the fact, not in the milestone report it cites** -- because the fact is what gets read.
489. **When you tell an agent that data exists, cite the enumeration, not your memory of it.** M69 checked `captures-needed.md` §12 and enumerated two roots before designing, found the burst absent, and had to redesign around a control it had been promised. **A false premise about the data is the most expensive error an orchestrator can put in a brief**, because it is discovered only after the design that depends on it has been built.
490. **A constant calibrated on a plant where the quantity cannot vary has no measured form, only a measured value.** `FOCUS_NOISE_SD` was fitted on pure noise with zero signal, so its texture dependence was not overlooked -- it was **unobservable by construction**. **Ask of every calibration: what could this fixture have shown me that it did not?** If the answer is nothing, the number is a value without a domain.
491. **Price an error bar in BOTH directions whenever the objective saturates.** M69's recalibration costs +0.37% one way and -3.63% the other, on the same magnitude of error, because M62's objective saturates above gate 4. **A single-number blast radius would have reported the safe end and been right by luck.**
492. **Reproducing a number digit-for-digit tests the code; only a second plant tests the claim.** M69 matched M66 at delta = 0.0000 and then refuted it on three further latents where the sign was not even consistent. **Exact agreement is the weakest evidence of generality the corpus can produce, and it is the most persuasive-looking.**
493. **A negative claim is the one kind of assertion the linter cannot check, so it needs the most manual care.** C1 verifies that citations resolve. **A statement that something is undiscussed cites nothing, so it passes every automated check the project owns while being the easiest kind of claim to get wrong** -- it requires proving absence over a corpus of 92 files. **Before recording that the corpus does not contain something, grep the corpus for it and paste the result.** Fact 1021 asserted absence for a constant with six facts about it.
494. **Never delete a hedge when folding. If a milestone wrote *"in the corpus I searched"*, the fold says *"in the corpus M69 searched"* or it does not make the claim at all.** I turned a scoped negative into an absolute one and put it in capitals. **The qualifier is the part that is doing the work, which is exactly why it looks like padding at fold time.**
495. **Writing a discipline is not the same as having it, and the gap can be minutes wide.** Disciplines 486-492 were committed, and the next fact I folded broke 486 in the same way. **Treat a newly written rule as unimplemented until a mechanical step enforces it** -- the rule bought nothing at the moment it was most available.
496. **A control that returns the answer you wanted is the one you will never scrutinise.** M72's `C2` compared the greens against the R-B pair, found them 8.6x more correlated, and returned GREEN-SPECIFIC -- the expected result, from a pre-registered control, and it was **the wrong comparison**. Only `F4`, written expressly to break M72's own headline, found that within-green neighbours correlate just as much. **Pre-registration protects against a test that could fail. It does not protect against a test that succeeds for the wrong reason.** Pair every confirming control with one adversarial control chosen by someone trying to kill the result.
497. **Plant a simulation specifically against the biases that FLATTER your hypothesis.** M72 found quantisation diluting its statistic by an ISO-dependent 8% **in the direction that mimicked the answer it was looking for**. A bias that opposes the hypothesis announces itself by making the result harder to get; one that flatters it is invisible. **Enumerate which way each known bias pushes, and plant against the ones pushing your way.**
498. **When a defect turns out to be general, fix the assertion rather than the arithmetic.** M72 declined to patch `green_luma_sigma` -- which would have been correct in exactly one call site -- and pointed at the doc comment asserting green independence as physics, because the pipeline pools neighbouring pixels in many other places that a green-specific constant would silently miss. **A local patch to a general defect converts a visible error into an invisible one.**
499. **A tolerance band is written for a specific estimator; correcting the estimator invalidates the band.** All three of M72's pre-registration failures had this one cause, which it named itself: *"I wrote bands for idealised estimators and ran corrected ones."* **State the estimator in the pre-registration next to the band**, or the corrected run is silently testing something else.
500. **Widening the comparison finds misattributed numbers that re-measuring never will.** Twice in two days a milestone has found the corpus holding a real measurement attached to the wrong object -- M68's `alpha_B` ratio, and now `rho(G1,G2)` as a green-pair property when it is one entry in a sensor-wide neighbour field. **Neither was found by doubting the number. Both were found by measuring the thing next to it.**
501. **A null control is null only with respect to a NAMED statistic.** The G1/G2 pair is a guaranteed null for gain and is **not** a null for independence -- they correlate at +0.09133 like any other neighbour pair. I recorded it as *"a free, physically-guaranteed null on any per-plane statistic"*, which is false for every statistic that pools the two planes. **Write the statistic into the control's description, or the control will be reused where its guarantee does not hold.**
502. **Pre-registration binds you to RUN a test, not to honour one that is provably incapable of passing.** M73's registered `H_ax` clause compared an integer interval against a continuous fit, which a width-1 set satisfies only on a measure-zero set. It pointed at a FAILURE and M73 disqualified it anyway. **The disqualifying proof must be constructed independently of which answer the rule was giving** -- that is what separates a repair from motivated reasoning, and it is why the direction that costs you a headline is the safe one to find first.
503. **A geometric invariant must name its exact class, because the weaker class is what will get written down.** The cylinder invariant requires **constant radius**; 'surface of revolution' is a different and false claim, and it propagated from M67's report into the ledger and into my report to the owner. **The more general-sounding premise is the one to distrust.**
504. **A simulated plant can reproduce in ORDERING and fail in DECOMPOSITION.** M67's 12% ratio transferred exactly; its causal framing -- correctness lives in the gate, not the election -- shrank threefold, because **the plant's election was half as accurate as a real subject's and the gate's lift was measured against it.** **When a plant reports how much of an effect a component contributes, check the plant's baseline against reality before quoting the share.**
505. **The estimator chosen at pre-registration time can decide the outcome before any data is touched.** M73 registered a per-column **line** fit; the cylinder's axis turned out well out of plane, and the obvious alternative -- a constant -- would have understated the transferred effect fivefold and made a surviving prediction look refuted. **Register the estimator that survives the idealisation being wrong, not the one the idealisation implies.**
506. **The question is not whether a constant is bare, it is where the constant is COMPARED.** M74's counter-example settles it: `FINE_FOCUS_NOISE_SD` sits in a **denominator** whose threshold is calibrated per stack against a permutation placebo, and is **safe**; `FOCUS_NOISE_SD` sits in a **directly-compared tolerance**, and was not. **Same shape, opposite verdicts.** Auditing constants by their declaration site finds the wrong half of them; audit the comparison.
507. **A homogeneous plant cannot express spatial dispersion, so a dispersion measured on one is a LOWER BOUND and never the number that matters.** M74 measured 1.371x on its plant and **1.70x-3.99x within a single real stack** -- and put the second number in its own headline section. **Every form check run on a uniform plant inherits this limb; state it there rather than in an appendix.**
508. **A repository path can encode a false citation, and no citation check can see it.** `experiments/M60-bimodality/` names the wrong milestone for `M63-bimodality.md`, and I relayed the directory's number as the report's. C1 validates numbers against the record; it has never validated a directory name against the report it claims to belong to. **Rule 40 caught this only because naming prior reports in a brief forces someone to open them.**
509. **An ordering that is not monotone in the obvious parameter falsifies the obvious mechanism, and it is usually free.** A 29x29 bare field beating a 23x23 regularised one rules out support width without a single extra run, because the arms were already there. **Before designing an experiment for a mechanism, check whether the existing arms already order in a way it forbids.**
