510. **A check written after the defect escaped is worth less than the rule that caught the defect, and both are worth keeping.** `C3` exists because rule 40 -- name prior reports in every brief -- forced an agent to open a file I had cited from memory. **The human-facing rule caught it; the machine check only stops the next one.** Do not let adding the check retire the rule that made the catch.
511. **Grandfather a defect with its reason IN THE CHECK, rather than fixing it, when the fix would falsify a record.** `experiments/M60-bimodality/` stays misnamed because seven committed reports record that path as the path they ran under. **A record is not a bug to be tidied; the collision is made visible instead, and only new instances fail.**
512. **Quotation marks in this corpus are a verification claim, not a prose device.** If the words are not in the source, do not use quotation marks -- write the paraphrase unquoted. Facts 775, 856 and 887 each put the orchestrator's own summary inside quotes and attributed it to a milestone; all three were de-quoted at source. A reader cannot tell a summary from evidence once it is inside quotes, and in this corpus quotation is how a claim gets checked. Found by advisory `Q1`.
513. **When a check flags a row, read the SOURCE, not the row.** `Q1` reported only that fact 856's quote was absent from M53. Opening `M54-clip-mask-measured.md:589` found the real finding: the phrase was the orchestrator's own, and M54 had already named it *"that universal quantifier"*. **The check found a misquote; the source found the author.** Had the row been edited until the check went quiet, fact 1053 would not exist -- and this discipline was itself violated in the very commit that introduced it (see 517).
514. **A ratio trend is not a property of its numerator.** Before attributing a moving ratio to one plane, either fit the absolute observable or enumerate every mechanism the ratio admits and show which are excluded. M68 published a chroma-plane drift that M75 showed was a *green*-plane drift, using M68's own data and reproducing M68's own numbers exactly. A ratio measures the difference of slopes and nothing more; M68's admitted four mechanisms, two of them opposite in sign. Facts 1054, 995.
515. **When a result depends on which of two estimators you pre-registered, measure the floor of the one you did not pick -- and if you cannot tell which to trust, delete the fit rather than pick.** M75's pre-registration was honoured in full and still under-scoped its headline: the claim held for `alpha_high` and failed for `alpha_low`. **Pre-registration bounds honesty about failure, not about scope.** Deleting the fit then produced a discovery the fit was hiding -- two gradients with different relationships to the dual-gain switch. Facts 1057, 1058.
516. **A failed gate whose explanation you correctly refused to guess at can still have a measurable answer, and it is usually reached by changing the OBSERVABLE rather than the hypothesis.** M68 refused to guess why gate D1 failed, and its one attempt refuted itself. The answer -- per-plane analog scales that vary across the array -- came from fitting alpha absolutely instead of in ratio. Same data, same frames, same agent lineage. Facts 1056, 995.
517. **Silencing a check is not fixing what it reported.** Disciplines 512-516 were written as four-column table rows and inserted into section 4, because the fold anchored on `| 513 |` and matched the *fact* numbered 513. `S1` fired correctly on the column mismatch; the orchestrator gave the rows four columns, which satisfied `S1` and left them in the wrong section entirely, in a format section 5 does not use -- **section 5 is a numbered list, not a table.** `C1` caught it two commits later only because these disciplines happened to be cited by number. **A check reports a symptom at a location; the defect is not necessarily there.** This is the fourth instance of the orchestrator's substitute-the-summary-for-the-source failure (facts 1040, 1053, 1061).
518. **A plant must measure what it planted.** M71's correlated-noise plant ran at twice the requested correlation because of a dropped factor of 2 in the kernel solve, and both arms passed anyway -- so the milestone would have described a test it did not run, with the right conclusion for the wrong reason. Assert the realised amplitude of every planted quantity inside the plant, not in the brief that requested it. Fact 1073.
519. **Verify a noise model ACROSS its signal range, never at a point -- because when two errors cancel, the model looks calibrated exactly once.** M71 found the shipped model over-confident above S = 504 DN, reaching -12.8% at S = 8000, with the 2.16%-high profile gain and the absent PRNU term cancelling precisely at the crossover. A single-point check placed anywhere near 504 DN would have certified it. Fact 1064.
520. **A placebo that comes out larger than the effect withdraws the effect.** M71 measured CPL spatial non-uniformity at 0.373% against a time-matched placebo of 0.526% and withdrew the result rather than report the smaller number. Fact 1066.
521. **A wrong reading that yields a PLAUSIBLE number is camouflage.** M70 misread fact 471 as a near/far half-width ratio when it is a measured-versus-modelled FWHM check, and the wrong conversion produced 0.053 beside its own measured 0.0404 -- close enough that nothing looked amiss. Implausible errors announce themselves; plausible ones must be caught by opening the source. It took the number from SYNTHESIS's compressed rendering rather than from `M67:520`. Fact 1080.
522. **Pre-registration bounds the analyst; only a null run bounds the instrument.** M70's criterion H was honestly registered and honestly executed and was still unreadable on 7 of 12 stacks, because the structureless floor climbs toward the Gaussian value with frame count and passes inside the bar at K=299. Register a null run alongside every criterion, so an unreadable instrument is distinguishable from an absent effect. Fact 1084.
523. **Never half-wave-rectify per-frame values before summing them across frames.** A statistic that clips band signal at zero before summing rectifies noise into apparent signal, inflating as 0.4K/sqrt(2 ln K) -- 42.07 at K=299 where truth is 0. This made one of M70's own pre-registered criteria unsatisfiable by construction and is a live hazard for any Wiener or matched-filter merge. Fact 1079.
524. **`S1` cannot see a row that is malformed AND coincidentally matches its header's width; audit with an absolute pipe-count check, not a relative one.** M70 found this by auditing all 36 of its tables after its own P5 row silently discarded two cells for four commits. Fold the stricter check into `corpus_lint`. Fact 1085.
525. **A spec validated on metadata is not validated.** M55's substrate check read EXIF and frame counts and still shipped an ROI outside the image on all six held-out stacks (fact 1087). **Bounds-check every registered pixel coordinate against the real geometry at registration time**, and prefer a fixture that fails loudly at registration over one that fails at first decode.
526. **Before shipping an acceptance clause, exhibit an input that fails it.** B6's pooled-90% clause is unfailable across all `2^24` placements and provably so (fact 1092). A clause with no witness of failure is decoration, and reads as a safety net while being none.
527. **A fixture that holds a quantity constant cannot test a rule about that quantity's variation** (fact 1091). The plant must be able to express the failure (fact 24); so must the **fixture**, and the fixture is the part nobody re-reads.
528. **Never name a throwaway script after a standard-library module, and write temp scripts to a dedicated subdirectory.** `python $env:TEMP\x.py` puts `TEMP` on `sys.path[0]`, and every agent on this machine shares one `TEMP` (fact 1093). Use `$env:TEMP\strehl-verify\`.
529. **Declining to promote your own strong result is the discipline, not a failure of it** (fact 1089). M76 held `rho = -0.8596, p = 0.0024` at INCONCLUSIVE because its registration demanded 20 cells and it had 18. Re-earn such a result on a repaired fixture; never launder it through a relaxed rule written afterwards.
530. **Never write backticks, or any PowerShell metacharacter, inside a double-quoted PowerShell string.** The backtick is PowerShell's escape character and is consumed silently (fact 1096). Build file content in Python (`io.open(...).write(...)`) or use a single-quoted here-string; `chr(96)` is the reliable way to emit a backtick from a generated script.
531. **A control is worthless until it has been shown to go red.** Run every new check against a planted defect and confirm the exact violation ids and a non-zero exit, then confirm green after removal (facts 1094, 1096). A green control that was never made to fail is indistinguishable from a control that cannot fail.
532. **Any tool that selects a subset of work must refuse an unrecognised selector, not silently select nothing** (fact 1094). Empty-selection-reports-success is the same silent-green class as a crashing renderer that never prints its violations.
533. **An internal consistency identity is a diagnostic, never an acceptance gate** (fact 1098). Arm A satisfied the conservation identity to within 7.4% of truth while worsening held-out error. **Score on held-out prediction.** A treatment that improves an identity and worsens prediction has found the identity's blind spot, not the effect.
534. **Any filter added inside a measurement probe is an instrument effect until shown otherwise** (fact 1099). Resampling, blurring and shifting all suppress the statistic you are measuring. Always run the zero-effect self-pair: it must return the identity, and M23 measured a bilinear one returning 0.3719 where truth is 1.000.
535. **When a milestone measures an instrument artefact, route it into the brief of every later milestone that adds a filter.** M78 pre-empted the resampler trap because its dispatch named it; the fact table alone would not have been read in time (fact 1099).
536. **Establish that a control is *sensitive* to the parameter it certifies before treating its agreement as evidence** (fact 1101). M5's placebo reads 0.2154 at both tile sizes, so its agreement carried no information about tile size -- and an inference was drawn from it anyway. An invariant control is a placebo for the wrong thing.
537. **Fold the full invocation with any number: every non-default flag, not just the driver name** (fact 1100). `--tile 128` versus the committed default of 256 moved `f_sig` from 0.2762 to 0.2375 and cost two milestones a reconciliation. A number without its invocation is not reproducible.
538. **Settle a units question from the code, never from the prose** (fact 1102). Whether `e_flat` was a variance or a standard deviation changed the comparison exponent by a factor of two, and M70's report did not say.
539. **Reproduce a multi-value fingerprint, not a single number, when adjudicating a reproduction dispute** (fact 1100). M76b matched six quantities on each side of the tile-size split, which identified the configuration rather than merely detecting disagreement.
540. **Prove a constant *can* be global before shipping one as a global** (fact 1103). Two sibling stacks 2.4% apart in information content needed gates 3.31x apart. Calibrate the threshold against the stack in hand, as `through_focus.rs:718-730` already mandates for its own order statistic.
541. **An acceptance bar is part of a configuration, not a portable number** (fact 1106). Fact 890's `[0.90, 1.10]` came from a 30-frame burst and could not be met at N = 22-299. Re-derive every bar in the configuration where it will be applied, and record `N`, subject and invocation beside it.
542. **Any statistic built on a per-pixel argmax inherits max-over-N inflation, and subtracting the noise model does not remove it** (fact 1105). `sqrt(raw^2 - model^2)` removes the model's variance, not the selection bias, so the statistic can report 10x detail retention on pure noise. Rule 4 applies to acceptance instruments, not only to the merge.
543. **Quote no `n_eff` without its stack** (fact 1104). The corpus spans 31.7x, and the thesis-critical question was first answered on the two most extreme members of it.
544. **In a shared working tree, `cargo clean -p` plus a rebuild is not proof of authorship** -- another agent may rebuild in between. Use a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when a build artefact is evidence.
545. **One loud fixture failure means audit every cell of the fixture** (fact 1109). Three of M55's four ROIs were silently valid under a transposed reading and measured the wrong sensor region without error; only the fourth crashed. Loud failures are the sample, not the population.
546. **Validate the constants a rule derives from, not only the coordinates it emits** (fact 1108). `QUAD_W`/`QUAD_H` were transposed at fixture generation and every derived coordinate inherited it, while the fractional rule itself was correct throughout.
547. **A substrate validator must check the units the fixture is written in** (fact 1110). M55 validated EXIF and frame counts and printed pixel coordinates it had no means to check. Bounds-check registered coordinates against real image geometry at registration time.
548. **An external reviewer's claim about what the corpus lacks is a hypothesis about our filesystem, and must be checked against it before commissioning work** (fact 1111). The reviewer cannot read our tree. Grep `docs/research/` and the ledger for the topic before dispatching; the cost of checking is one command.
549. **When a milestone's conclusion closes a workstream, that conclusion must itself be independently verified** (fact 1112). G-edof killed deconvolution on novelty grounds and was never checked, because the corpus's verification effort follows *builds* rather than *literature verdicts*. A wrongly-closed workstream leaves no failing test to reveal it.
550. **Before reporting anything as unallocated, unbuilt or open, grep the ledger and `docs/research/` for it** (fact 1114). Three claims of absence failed this check in one session -- one from a reviewer, one from me acting on the reviewer, one from my own tracking state. The corpus is 95 reports; recall is not inventory.
551. **When one milestone's quantity becomes another's optimisation target, ask its author whether that use was intended** (fact 1118). M70's `n_eff` is a count, not a prescription, and the identification silently embedded in `T*` was never measured. The check costs one message and caught a load-bearing assumption mid-build.
552. **A dispersion measured in derived units may live in the unit rather than the phenomenon** (fact 1116). Before concluding a constant is unfixable, express the measurement in units that touch none of the suspect constants -- M70's frame-domain ladder agreed to 4.7% where the threshold-domain reading dispersed 3.31x.
553. **An estimator's null must be characterised on the region class where it will be read** (fact 1117). The spectral count spans -2.5 to +3.0 on untextured tiles at every window size, so a flat-region reading carried no information. Flat tiles have no measurable target, not a target of zero.
554. **A negative literature verdict must state whether the source's conclusion is general or configuration-specific, and name which of its assumptions our regime violates** (fact 1120). Levin's result is a fixed-total-exposure comparison; read as general it closed a workstream it does not reach.
555. **When several routes agree, audit for shared assumptions before treating the agreement as independent corroboration** (fact 1121). Three mechanisms differed but all three assumed no opaque visibility change and an adequate known response, so the agreement licenses only the narrowed claim.
556. **Never chain the corpus gate and a commit in one shell call** (fact 1123). Run `corpus_lint.py`, read the exit code, then commit as a separate call. A gate whose result nothing reads is not a gate, and `N1` caught this defect correctly while the chaining discarded the answer.
557. **Derive acceptance thresholds from the calibrated noise model and expose only the risk budget as policy** (fact 1126). M80's `2.32635` is the alpha = 0.01 normal quantile, not a tuned DN value, so the bar adapts per ROI and per stack while the human choice stays visible. This is the standing repair for the bare-constant defect class.
558. **Report the residual of any bias correction, not just the corrected value** (fact 1124). Subtracting the analytic order-statistic term over-corrected by -433% and drove a variance negative; the correction was refuted by its own arithmetic, and only computing the residual revealed it.
559. **An instrument must be able to answer "not measurable"** (fact 1125). A statistic that always returns a number certifies regions it cannot read, which is how fact 1105 reported ten on nothing. Pair the refusal with a positive control showing where it stops answering, or it will refuse everywhere.
560. **A milestone's citation of a third milestone is a compressed rendering, and inherits every risk of one.** Fact 1130: M70 cited M69's 4.06x, I lifted it into a committed fact and a dispatch, and it was a category error. **Read the third source before the number becomes load-bearing anywhere.** Rule 40 said "read the source"; it now means the *cited* source, not the citing one.
561. **Before dispatching a repair hypothesis, check whether it is arithmetically capable of closing the gap.** Fact 1128: the corrections span 1.38x against a 49.75x gate spread. That comparison needs no experiment and would have downgraded the arm from *primary* to *cheap control* before an agent spent a night on it. **State the lever's measured range next to the gap's measured size in the dispatch itself.**
562. **A coarse ladder's invariant rung is not an invariant threshold.** Fact 1131: three crossings spanning 1.306x all land on 8 DN because the ladder doubles. **When reporting a transition, report the derived crossing and its span, not the rung** -- and when reading someone else's, look for the continuous value in the same paragraph.
563. **An abstention budget is not an admission rule.** Fact 1132: alpha prices answering when you should not; it does not price admitting a bad frame when you must decide everywhere. **Before transferring a threshold template between instruments, name the error it budgets and check that both instruments face that same error.**
564. **An audit's unit of analysis decides what its number means, and the unit must be named in the headline.** Fact 1134: M83 measured three deliberately-chosen load-bearing claims per report, so its 72.2% is an *architectural-exposure* rate and it said so rather than letting the figure be read as a base rate over prose. **Report the population, the sampling rule and what the number is NOT** -- an audit that inflates its own scope is the defect it is auditing.
565. **A survey's strongest sentence is usually its weakest evidence.** Fact 1135: every overstatement M83 found ran the same way -- a bounded experiment, an incomparable measurement, a conditional theorem, a two-product sample or an API capability, promoted to a universal or a magnitude. **When a survey states a number or the word "no", go to the primary source; that is where this corpus breaks.**
566. **When the survey that certified a novelty claim is audited, the novelty claim must be re-derived, not merely narrowed.** Fact 1136: two audits have now each caught a survey missing its own nearest prior art (Pertuz 2013; Schechner 1998). **A "verified-absent" claim inherits the search quality of the report that made it**, and neither report's search was adequate.
567. **A licence conclusion must be a release checklist, not an adjective.** Fact 1138: "LGPL is satisfied because we publish our source" is not what LGPL-2.1 §6 says. **Write the obligations as steps someone performs at release** -- notices, library source, modification rights, relink mechanism -- or the conclusion cannot be checked.
568. **A global scalar summary of a spatially varying decision does not locate the pixels that matter.** Fact 1141: `coffee-bean` reached whole-image mean `n_eff` 18.424 while **97.41% of its detail ROI remained a pure selector**. Before reporting any whole-image mean as evidence that a behaviour changed, **report the same statistic inside the ROI whose quality is being claimed.** A mean over mostly-flat background is a measurement of the background.
569. **An instrument that abstains on every row has measured its own power, not the hypothesis.** Fact 1140: 18 of 18 rows unreadable, the largest central estimate reaching **51.1% of the pre-frozen null bound**. The correct report is NOT ESTABLISHED with the bound printed beside the observation -- never a span assembled from values the rule just declared unreadable, and never a refutation manufactured from their signs. **Encode the abstention in the data structure**, as M82 did by emitting `span: null`, so no downstream reader can quietly promote it.
570. **When one constant has defeated three separate calibration attempts, the next move is a better instrument, not a fourth scheme.** M77 found the gate non-portable, M81 refuted the unit hypothesis and made it worse, M82 normalised the request successfully and then could not read the price. **The failures have changed character** -- from wrong, to worse, to unresolvable -- and that progression is evidence about the *measurement*, not about the constant. Fund resolution next.
571. **An orchestrator's own observations enter the corpus at the same evidentiary bar as a milestone's, or lower.** Facts 1143-1145 are mine, made in one sitting, on one subject, with no repetition and no independent check -- and fact 1144 is code reading, not measurement. They are labelled accordingly and each names the milestone chartered to verify it. **The author never verifies their own work applies to the author of the corpus too**, and sixteen recorded errors say it applies there most.
572. **A visual impression is a hypothesis with a milestone attached, never a finding.** Fact 1145 could have been written as *the gate does not cause the halo* and shipped as architecture. What it actually licenses is a charter to build the metric that could say so. **Do not let something seen at 100% zoom become a number.**
573. **Issuing an instruction to an agent is not observing its effect, and the ledger must record only the second.** Fact 1146: a queued stop message sat undelivered behind an unfinished turn while `AGENTS.md` already described the agent as retired. **Read the agent's status back before recording a state change**, and when relaunching work someone else may still hold, **assume the incumbent is live until its own output says otherwise.** The subordinate agent applied this correctly and I did not.
574. **When two agents collide on one brief, prefer independence over cancellation if the measurement is high-consequence.** M84 and M84b were an accident; keeping both converts my error into the strongest check the project can buy on its first physical ground truth. **The conditions are strict**: separate stems, a standing bar on reading each other's method or numbers, mandatory disclosure of any contamination, and an explicit instruction not to tune toward agreement. **Disagreement is then a finding.** Absent those conditions it is duplicated work, not verification.
575. **The diffraction cutoff is ground truth you did not have to capture, and it falsifies for free.** Any change claiming more resolution can be checked against it: **energy above `f_c` is not recovered detail, because the optics cannot have put it there.** Adopt it as an acceptance test wherever resolution is claimed. It catches precisely the failure that visual inspection *praises* -- a demosaicer or sharpener that manufactures super-cutoff energy and looks better for it -- and it costs one FFT.
576. **Audit the attribution, not only the arithmetic.** Fact 1147: a VERIFIED 2.8x ceiling rested on a teleconverter the owner does not own. **The number survived; the provenance did not.** A right answer reached through a wrong source is a latent error that detonates the moment someone follows the citation to look up a *second* quantity -- here the pupil magnification the advisor already names as its dominant uncertainty. Checking that a figure is correct is not checking that its source is.
577. **An orchestrator's brief is a fact claim and inherits every rule that governs one.** Fact 1148: *"so m <= 2"* carried no citation, contradicted a VERIFIED line, and propagated into subordinate reasoning **as a falsifier**, where being too conservative refutes true hypotheses. Briefs are not commentary. **Cite them, or mark them ARGUED where the subordinate can see the label and overrule it** -- as M84b did, correctly, by ignoring mine.
578. **Before assuming a parameter, search the corpus for a measurement of it -- and treat a labelled assumption as an unpaid debt, not a discharged one.** Fact 1157: I set `p = 1`, wrote *"assumed, +/-38%"* beside it, and felt covered. M5's measured `B` gave `N_eff` directly with no `p` needed. **The label made the assumption look diligent while it did the damage of a silent one**, and it inverted a headline and shipped a bad falsifier to a live implementer. **Ask what measured quantity makes the assumption unnecessary**, not merely how uncertain the assumption is.
579. **Bars measure precision; only independent re-implementation measures correctness.** Fact 1158: a 0.27 px rms projective residual, and every pre-registered bar passing, in a coordinate frame that was wrong by 3.12 degrees. **A threshold constrains you to the number you predicted in the frame you predicted it in, and is silent when the frame is wrong.** Pre-registration is necessary and is not sufficient. Where a result is high-consequence, fund a second implementation of the estimator, not a tighter bar on the first.
580. **When two independent claimants disagree, the disagreement is the finding -- publish it, adjudicate it on stated causes, and do not collapse it.** Fact 1156: M84 and M84b returned opposite verdicts on the same frames, and M84b listed the specific limits under which a negative would be honest. **A single claimant would have shipped either verdict unopposed.** The arrangement is only worth its cost if the orchestrator then **resists the urge to declare a winner**: record both, name the capture that settles it, and leave it open.
581. **Before telling an agent that something has not been measured, search the corpus for it -- and cite the search in the brief.** Three times in one night I asserted an absence that was false: `p = 1` where M5 had measured the bellows factor (fact 1157), *"nobody has measured"* the bee through-focus responses where M70 had measured all three, and a *"new"* ISO-matched pair that M61 had already owner-verified (fact 1165). The failure is not carelessness about facts -- it is a **category error about what a brief is**. A brief that asserts absence is making a MEASURED claim about the corpus and must be evidenced like one. **The linguistic tell is exact and greppable: "nobody has", "unvalidated", "not established", "no such" appearing without a citation.** The cost is uniquely high because the victim is a whole agent-night. Now rule 43.

582. **A knob's scale and a knob's price are two claims, and repairing the first is not evidence about the second.** M82 collapsed a 22.176x raw-gate spread into a 0.4% achieved-gain spread and still returned NO SHIP, because portability of the *outcome* says nothing about portability of what the outcome *costs*. Report capability results and product results in separate verdict blocks, and never let a strong capability number carry a product decision it did not earn.

583. **Never characterise a spatially free quantity by its whole-image mean; report it inside registered ROIs.** `coffee-bean` has whole-image mean `n_eff` 18.424 and a detail cell that is 97.41% bare selector (fact 1160). The mean was not wrong; it was answering a question nobody asked. Any statistic whose spatial distribution is the actual subject of interest must be reported locally, in ROIs registered before measurement, or it will conceal exactly the failure it was computed to detect.

584. **Before designing a control around a parameter, check that the parameter survives the algebra of the statistic.** M82's coordinate reduces to `mean(1 / sqrt(n_eff))`, in which sensor sigma cancels identically -- so the ISO-matched arm I designed to isolate a noise-model defect was void by construction (fact 1164). No execution care could have rescued it. **Derive the statistic symbolically and confirm the variable of interest is still in it** before spending an agent on the measurement.

585. **A milestone that reports over several turns restates its earlier findings in its final report -- fold the delta, not the document.** I folded M82's detail-ROI admission result as fact 1141 when it first reported, then folded the identical measurement again as fact 1160 from its final report, having written a commit message calling it *"the night's most consequential measurement"* both times. **Two numbers for one measurement is worse than none: a later reader, and a later agent, will count them as independent corroboration of each other.** The cause is structural rather than careless -- a final report is *supposed* to be self-contained, so its restatement of earlier work is correct behaviour by the agent and a trap for the folder. Before folding a report from an agent that has reported before, **diff its candidate facts against what its own prior turns already contributed**, and grep SYNTHESIS for the distinctive numerals in each candidate. Now mechanically enforced as `corpus_lint` check `D1`.
586. **When a milestone cannot produce its deliverable, emit an explicit machine-readable refusal, never a degraded artefact.** M84 shipped `depth_map.emitted = false, valid_pixels = 0` and no file, on the reasoning that an assumption-scaled plane or an all-false mask is *easier to misuse than an explicit refusal* (fact 1174). A consumer can branch on absence; it cannot detect that a well-formed array encodes an unidentified scale. **State the refusal in the same schema the success would have used**, so that reading the result is how the caller learns, rather than noticing a missing path.
587. **A BUILD MILESTONE'S ACCEPTANCE MUST NAME ITS CONSUMER, NOT ONLY ITS TESTS.** M86 delivered a 107 KB alignment module with 23 passing tests, a seven-subcommand harness and a report -- and **nothing in the shipped pipeline called any of it**, so the owner's output was byte-identical before and after. Every gate the milestone set for itself was green and the user-visible effect was zero. **When dispatching work whose value is user-visible, register the consumer as an acceptance condition** -- name the call site that must exist, or state explicitly that this milestone is a library and a later one will wire it. The failure is silent precisely because a library with no callers still compiles, still passes, and still looks finished. (SYNTHESIS facts 1178, 1180.)
588. **TWO AGENTS ADDING A ONE-LINE MODULE DECLARATION TO THE SAME FILE IS A REAL CLOBBER RISK, AND IT WAS SURVIVED BY LUCK RATHER THAN DESIGN.** M85 committed M86's `pub mod align;` line in `e59f1b0`; had the two landed in the other order, one would have silently overwritten the other. M86 reported this against its own interest. **Shared registration points -- `lib.rs` module lists, CLI subcommand tables, plugin registries -- are the highest-collision, lowest-content lines in the tree.** The orchestrator owns them: subordinates building a new module must deliver the registration line **as a verbatim patch in their report** and never apply it themselves. (SYNTHESIS fact 1178.)
589. **DISTINGUISH AN IDENTIFIABILITY FAILURE FROM A PRECISION FAILURE BEFORE SPENDING ANYTHING ON PRECISION.** M88 could not separate 87 from 106-135 cy/mm not because its instrument was imprecise -- it was validated to **+1.19% +/- 1.50%** and reaches **114.6 cy/mm** from a 48.83 cy/mm lattice -- but because `rise^2 = d^2 + c^2` has two unknowns and one measurement, with the nuisance term 3x the signal. **More frames, better fitting and longer runs cannot repair an under-determined system; only a different capture can.** The diagnostic is cheap and should precede any measurement campaign: **write down the model, count the unknowns against the independent measurements, and check that the quantity of interest is separable from its nuisance terms at the available scatter.** (SYNTHESIS facts 1182, 1183.)
590. **PREFER AN INSTRUMENT WHOSE NULL IS A THEOREM TO ONE WHOSE NULL IS A CALIBRATION.** M89's fourth-difference kernel annihilates any cubic exactly, so `E[z^2] = 1` follows from the algebra and the measured null landed at **0.9897 with nothing tuned**. Contrast the constants that have cost this project the most: `FOCUS_NOISE_SD`, the still-uncalibrated gate, M12's shrinkage scalar, and `dsig` -- whose null had to be measured and then **failed at 0.343 px**, abstaining 18 of 18 rows (**and the measured null was itself wrong by 1.7587x, fact 1242 -- which strengthens this discipline rather than weakening it: a fitted null can be wrong in a way a theorem cannot**). **A fitted null must be re-established on every new scene, and the corpus has repeatedly discovered that it does not transfer; a derived null has nothing to transfer.** When choosing between two candidate statistics, **weight the existence of a closed-form null above sensitivity** -- and a derived null additionally confers immunity to any model error living in the annihilated subspace, which is how M89 survived M90 (fact 1190). (SYNTHESIS facts 1186, 1190.)
591. **WHEN A DELIVERABLE FAILS ITS BARS, ASK WHICH *STAGE* THE DEFECT LIVES IN BEFORE RE-SPECIFYING THE DELIVERABLE.** M89 was asked for a Wronski-shaped robustness weight on the merge average. It failed (**-5.21%** against **+10%** required, p999 **38% worse**) -- and the reason was not that the weight was badly shaped but that **the damage happens one stage earlier**: 4.78% of output pixels are elected from a frame more than 8 sigma discrepant, because a moving frame is often the *sharpest* one and this pipeline selects before it combines. **Down-weighting a frame in the average cannot help when it has already won the election.** The generalisable move is the diagnostic M89 ran rather than the fix: it measured **what fraction of the benefit was even reachable** from the specified stage -- **6.0%** -- which converts "my deliverable failed" into "the specification targeted the wrong stage, and here is the number proving it". (SYNTHESIS fact 1189.)
592. **A PLANTED DEFECT THAT ONLY AN EXTERNAL CHECK CATCHES MEANS THE IN-CRATE TEST IS THE WRONG SHAPE.** M90 planted a defect; it was caught by an external hash comparison and **not** by M90's own in-crate test. The lesson is not "add another test" -- it is that **a test written by the same reasoning that wrote the code inherits that reasoning's blind spot**, which is why this project separates author from verifier. **When a planted defect is caught only from outside, treat the in-crate test as failed even though it is green**, and say what shape of assertion would have caught it. M89 hit the mirror image of this on the same night: its instrument survived a model error precisely because the error lived in a subspace its kernel annihilates (fact 1190) -- **know which errors your test is structurally blind to, and state them.**
593. **AGENTS SHARE ONE WORKING TREE, SO ONE AGENT'S UNCOMMITTED DELETION IS EVERY AGENT'S RED GATE.** M90's report was deleted from the working tree and, because `corpus_lint` check `C2` verifies that every cited document exists, **the gate went red for four sibling milestones that had done nothing wrong** -- and stayed red until M90 recovered the file. The deletion never reached a commit, so `git log` on the path shows nothing: `--diff-filter=D` returns empty. **A shared advisory gate couples every agent to every other agent's working tree**, and a red gate that is not yours is therefore not evidence that you did anything. **Diagnose a sudden gate failure by asking what changed on disk, not what changed in your own diff**, and never delete or move a file you did not create -- including to "clean up".
594. **PROVE A METRIC IS LIVE BEFORE YOU REPORT A NULL WITH IT.** M85's gate ladder reports "no change" (0.985x-0.997x) on facets. A dead metric reports exactly the same thing. It was made admissible by a **plant**: the same estimator, same five files, reads **0.151x on defocused background** and drops to **0.063x** under a planted sigma=1.0 px blur. M85 also hashed all five renders first, since an inert `--gate` flag would have voided the whole run. **A null is a claim about the world only if the instrument could have said otherwise, and you must show the instrument saying otherwise.**

595. **A POWER CONTROL IS MANDATORY FOR ANY INSTRUMENT WHOSE HEADLINE IS AN ABSENCE.** M91 retired *two* of its own instruments this way: handed a disturbance that was uniform by construction, they failed to detect it on 6 of 6 stacks. Without that control both would have reported "drift is spatially uniform" -- a confident, wrong, publishable-looking answer. Discipline 594 is the same medicine for a *positive* instrument reporting a null; this is the case where the instrument itself must be thrown away. **Two milestones reached this independently on the same night.**

596. **A PLACEBO THAT READS A RECOGNISABLE NUMBER FROM ELSEWHERE IN THE RUN LOCALISES THE BUG.** M91's `gamma = 1` placebo did not merely fail: it returned **26.58985 DN, exactly the independently computed corrected-vs-uncorrected RMS from a different arm**, which named the comparison-target defect in its own design. **A placebo's value is not only that it reads zero.** Prefer placebo outputs on the same scale as the real arms, so a wrong wiring produces a *recognisable* number rather than a merely wrong one.

597. **A SURROGATE VERIFIED BIT-IDENTICAL IS A LEGITIMATE WAY AROUND FILE CONTENTION, AND THE ONLY ONE.** Fact 1205 reimplemented the averaging stage from the public API and matched `green_mean` bit-for-bit at 8.2M pixels on six stacks. Where that bar is met, dispatch experiments against the surrogate instead of serialising agents onto the contended file. Where it is **not** met, the surrogate is a different program and its results are about itself. **"Close enough" is not a bit, and the bar is the bit.**
598. **A CONTROL THAT READS EXACTLY ZERO IS THE MOST DANGEROUS RESULT IN AN INSTRUMENT, NOT THE MOST REASSURING.** M88b reports that **three of the five defects it found in its own design were controls reading exactly `0.000` that looked like passes.** Exact zero is what a correct null looks like *and* what a disconnected probe, an unreached branch and a self-cancelling comparison look like. **Pair every zero-reading null with a positive control on the same wiring**: M88b cut its treatment set from 5 ROIs to 3 after finding **two that passed the null and were blind to a planted effect**. A null shows the instrument is quiet; only a plant shows it can speak.

599. **REGISTER THE COMPARISON, THEN COMPARE -- FIXED WINDOW COORDINATES ARE NOT A FIXED SUBJECT.** M88b's first paired design compared ROIs at fixed pixel coordinates and produced a **spurious 5.7 um** difference from nothing but the subject having moved within the window. It was removed by integer registration before measurement. This is M88's own Bar 3 failure recurring in a new form, **inside the milestone that had already learned it**, which is the argument for encoding such lessons as controls rather than as intentions.
600. **A BYTE-IDENTICAL RESTORE IS NOT A RESTORED CONTROL, BECAUSE THE BUILD SYSTEM NEVER SAW IT CHANGE.** M90 planted a defect, restored the source with `shutil.copy2`, confirmed the file was **byte-identical to HEAD** -- and its bars stayed red. `copy2` preserves mtime **by design**, so `cargo` concluded nothing had changed, skipped the rebuild, and **left the planted binary live underneath clean source**. Every source-level check passed while the artefact under test was still the mutated one. It was caught only by re-running the control externally. This is discipline 592 in a new costume -- the verification inheriting the blind spot of the thing it verifies -- and it generalises past `cargo` to every cached build system. **Restore must invalidate the cache, not merely restore the bytes** (touch the file, or force the rebuild), **and the restoration must be proven by re-running the control, never by comparing source.** (SYNTHESIS fact 1210; M90 round 2 N4.)
601. **MEASURE THE STATISTIC THE CONSUMER ACTUALLY SEES, NOT THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO AVERAGE.** `rho_warp` averaged over all frame pairs is **3.4x** too optimistic, because `Estimator::fold` admits an **interval around the winner** and therefore only ever sees the near-pair end of `rho(d)`, where correlation is at its highest. The all-pairs mean is not a conservative simplification of that -- it is a different population, and it is biased in the direction that matters. Before averaging over a population, **state which members the consumer is exposed to and average over those.** (SYNTHESIS fact 1211.)
602. **A SEARCH THAT RETURNS ITS OWN BOUND IS NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THE TELL IS REPEATED IDENTICAL VALUES ACROSS DIFFERENT INPUTS.** The orchestrator's first breathing-drift run reported **exactly 0.936700** for seven different frames, because an iterative bracket refinement had walked to the edge of its initial range and had no way to express "the optimum is outside where I looked". Every individual number looked plausible; only the **repetition** revealed it, and a table of per-frame results is what made the repetition visible -- a single summary statistic would have hidden it completely. Two requirements follow. **Any bounded search must report whether its optimum sits on a boundary**, and a boundary hit must be surfaced as a distinct outcome rather than returned as a value. **And identical outputs from non-identical inputs must be investigated, never averaged**, because that pattern is also what a disconnected probe, a cached result and a saturated estimator all look like. Related to discipline 598, which is the same failure wearing the value 0.000 instead of a bound. (SYNTHESIS facts 1217, 1218.)

603. **STRATIFY A GUARD BAR BY THE COVARIATE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE GUARDED FAILURE MATTERS, BEFORE ACCEPTING ITS GLOBAL RATE.** M93's gate removed the correct sharp frame at 0.0194% of pixels, comfortably inside its 5% bar. That global number was not trustworthy until it was split by detail-SNR, where it read 0.0000% in the top bin against 0.0142% overall -- the hazard was concentrated exactly where the product does not care and absent exactly where it does, which inverts the direction the milestone had assumed. A global rate averages the cases that matter against the cases that do not, so a bar can pass for the wrong reason and a bar can fail for the wrong reason. State the covariate at pre-registration time, not after the number lands.

604. **A SPATIAL-COHERENCE BAR MUST DISTINGUISH A CORRECT SUBSTITUTION FROM AN INCORRECT ONE, OR IT WILL FAIL IN THE WRONG DIRECTION AND MEAN NOTHING.** M93's election-speckle bar counted elected indices differing from their neighbourhood median, and the gate made it 201-429% worse on contaminated stacks -- not because the gate was wrong but because every substitution the gate correctly made scored as incoherence. A metric that measures *change* cannot grade a stage whose entire job is to change things. Sibling of discipline 591: both are specifications that targeted the wrong quantity, and in both cases the milestone learned more from diagnosing the bar than it would have from passing it.

605. ~~**A GLOBAL SHARPNESS METRIC CAN BE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH IMAGE QUALITY, BECAUSE MISREGISTRATION MANUFACTURES GRADIENT ENERGY.**~~ **RETRACTED, fact 1250.** The premise was the orchestrator's visual claim that the registered render is sharper; that claim was a 1.25% magnification artefact and has been withdrawn. With it withdrawn the metric and the eye agree, and there is no measured instance of anti-correlation. The *mechanism* remains plausible -- a doubled edge does carry two gradients -- but it is now ARGUED with no supporting observation, and no milestone may build on it. (facts 1235, 1237, 1250)

606. **BEFORE COMPARING TWO RENDERS BY EYE, CHECK THAT THEY HAVE THE SAME FIELD OF VIEW, BECAUSE MAGNIFICATION READS AS SHARPNESS.** The orchestrator judged `bee-3`'s aligned render 'dramatically better' than the unaligned one at thumbnail scale and was wrong to: `fit_to_cover` gives the aligned render a ~7% smaller field of view, so at matched output size it renders larger, which reads as sharper for reasons unrelated to registration. The correct comparison is against a field-of-view- and resampler-matched null with only the effect under test removed. This is the visual form of the ordinary confound, and it fooled the person who wrote the rule about it.

607. **A BOUND CARRIED AS A CONSTANT MUST BE CHECKED BACK TO WHETHER IT WAS EVER A VARIANCE.** M57's 0.34310 px null travelled through two milestones as a hard bound on what this project could measure. It is a **single draw** -- element 1 of a three-element array -- and the 128-draw standard deviation at the identical cell is 0.29457. It was also measured with 1.7587x too much injected noise, because three scripts set `ISO = 500` as a module constant and applied it to an ISO-160 stack. The corrected single-ROI null is 0.089-0.094 px, so the effect the project believed it could not resolve was resolvable at **N = 1** all along. Fact 127's rule about constants applies with double force to numbers that *bound* what you attempt, because they do not merely mislead a calculation, they cancel work.

608. **A CONTROL THAT INJECTS A COMMON MODE MUST HAVE ITS MAGNITUDE CALIBRATED AGAINST THE VARIANCE OF THE STATISTIC IT IS TESTING, OR IT IS VALID FOR ONE ESTIMATOR AND INVALID FOR ANOTHER.** M92's NC1 reused one noise realisation verbatim at every ROI. As a control on a *correlation* estimator it worked, moving `rbar` up to +0.36. As a control on an *averaging exponent* it failed on all three stacks, missing its registered `alpha < 0.15` expectation, and that clause had been made milestone-voiding. Report the failure rather than satisfying the clause quietly, and pre-register estimator-specific controls per estimator.

609. **PRE-REGISTERED AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO ESTIMATORS MUST BE STATED IN A SHARED COORDINATE.** M92 made a literal disagreement between its pixel-domain and slope-domain exponents fatal, then found the slope-domain clause compares a quantity to itself under a nonlinear map; converted to a shared coordinate the two agree to a median of 0.0078. A clean result would have been voided by an arithmetic artefact of the registration itself. Registering a bar does not make it correct, and a bar that can fail for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis is a defect in the registration.

610. **A CAVEAT DOES NOT STOP A WRONG NUMBER FROM BEING USED, SO PREFER NOT TO SHIP IT.** The orchestrator folded `leg-spines 1.1288` explicitly flagged unverified and handed it to M97 with the caveat attached; it was the headline evidence that the sharpness metric reverses by region, and it was an artefact of a 1.25% magnification difference. An unverified number that supports the author's thesis will be read as support and the flag will be read as modesty. Either verify it before folding or state the mechanism that would make it wrong, so the reader can check it instead of discounting it. (facts 1237, 1250)

611. **BEFORE ACCEPTING A NULL RESULT, ASK WHETHER THE INSTRUMENT CAN EXPRESS THE DEFECT -- SENSITIVITY TO A PLANT IS NOT ENOUGH.** M97's straightness metric detected +4.252 px of planted misregistration and +0.038 px from alignment, and the natural reading is that alignment does nothing. But the plant and the defect are different transforms: straightness responds to translation and is analytically blind to the scale change breathing actually causes. **A plant validates a metric only if the plant has the same form as the defect.** This is discipline 24's 'plants must be able to express the failure' turned on the metric rather than the data. (facts 1251, 1252)

612. **WHEN THE ORCHESTRATOR AND A SUBORDINATE DISAGREE, THE ORCHESTRATOR TESTS ITSELF FIRST.** M97 reported a measurement contradicting a fact the orchestrator had folded from its own eyes. The orchestrator wrote a probe designed to kill its own claim, and the claim died. Rank is not evidence, and an orchestrator that defends its folded facts against subordinate measurement corrupts the corpus at the one point where nothing downstream can catch it -- every other fact in this table has been through an adversarial reader, and the orchestrator's have not. (facts 1235, 1250)

613. **AFTER BUILDING A MASK, ASSERT THAT IT CONTAINS THE THING YOU ARE LOOKING FOR, BEFORE COMPUTING ANYTHING THROUGH IT.** Three masks in one session excluded the artifact they were built to find, and each would have returned a confident wrong answer. Selection criteria correlate with the target more often than is comfortable -- a smoothness criterion excludes steps, a darkness criterion excludes bright defects, a background criterion excludes anything on the subject. Pick a probe region you already believe contains the target, assert coverage, and let it abort. Three lines. (fact 1256)

614. **A SMOOTH RAMP WITH A KINK LOOKS LIKE AN EDGE, SO SEEING A HARD BOUNDARY IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A DISCONTINUITY.** The orchestrator saw hard-edged plateaus in the render four times and measured a ramp every time -- ~26 px transitions with per-pixel changes under 1.1x. The visual system enhances gradient discontinuities into apparent steps, which is exactly the wrong bias for an imaging project whose artifacts are measured in DN. In this corpus a visual observation is a **hypothesis with a location attached**, never a measurement, and it must name the instrument that would confirm it. (facts 1250, 1255)

615. **A PLANT MUST NOT PERTURB THE MECHANISM IT IS MEASURING THROUGH.** A 40% brightness ramp planted to amplify a brightness artifact instead captured the election -- the brightest frames won everywhere, the elected field went constant, and the artifact vanished. The plant was applied upstream of a decision, so it changed the decision rather than the decision's consequence. Before planting, ask what the estimator does *differently* in the presence of the plant; if the answer is 'it chooses differently', freeze the choice first and plant downstream of it. (fact 1260)

616. **MEASURE NOISE ON A LOCAL RESIDUAL, NEVER BY POOLING MASKED PIXELS ACROSS A FRAME.** `mottle.py` pooled `img[flat]` over a 7032x4688 frame and reported a per-channel SD that was dominated by the background's frame-wide brightness gradient, not by noise. The tell was arithmetic rather than visual: a 17x17 box blur left the SD unchanged, so the reported 'mottle' came out at exactly the box size, 17.02x, identically in all three channels. Subtract a local mean first and every statistic is about the band you intended. A number that equals a parameter of your own code is a bug report. (fact 1258)
617. **An audit of a defect class must classify its hits by *role*, not count them.** M92b found 31 sensor constants disagreeing with their stack's EXIF, of which **exactly 3** were defects: 20 fed the deliberately frozen detail operator, where disagreement with EXIF is rule 15 working as designed, and 4 defined synthetic plants, where there is no truth to disagree with. The unclassified headline -- "31 defects" -- would have invited someone to correct 20 frozen constants and silently break every cross-milestone comparison in the corpus. **The classification is the audit; the count is not.**
618. **Control a guard against planted *non*-defects as well as planted defects, because a guard that over-fires gets disabled.** M92b's `check_tree()` scored 10 of 10 only because two of those cases were correct constants it was required to **ignore** -- one right-by-EXIF, one operator-only. A guard proven solely against true positives has an unmeasured false-positive rate, and the first time it blocks legitimate work someone turns it off, which costs more than never having written it.
619. **A bare stack name is not an identifier.** `119MSDCF` exists under two different roots at **ISO 50 and ISO 400** -- a 4x gain difference -- so resolving a stack by directory name alone silently selects the wrong sensor constants. This defeated M92b's own ground-truth table on its first run. Key a stack by root **and** name, and read the constant from EXIF rather than from a lookup keyed on the name.
620. **Point a new scanner at the defect you already know about before you trust what it says about the ones you do not.** M92b's first revision reported **0 instances tree-wide** (wrong root) and its second missed **tuple unpacking** -- which is precisely how `s7_bias_or_variance.py:44` concealed its `ISO = 500`. Fixing that one blind spot moved the count from **121 to 254**. A scanner that cannot find the known instance is reporting its own coverage, not the tree's contents.
621. **A held-out or relative error score cannot detect a global shrinkage, so the acceptance bar for an *estimator* must be absolute and end-to-end.** M86's alignment solve passes its held-out reprojection check while applying only **50.2%** of the drift that is physically there, because shrinking every frame's warp by a common factor leaves the frames' agreement *with each other* almost untouched -- it is the agreement with the **scene** that collapses. M97's words: *"any future acceptance bar for the solve needs an absolute, end-to-end check."* Whenever a fitted quantity is scored only against other fitted quantities, ask what multiplying the truth by a constant would do to the score; if the answer is "nothing", the score cannot validate the fit.
622. **Resolve a disputed measurement by *gathering* rather than by reading, and write the extractor yourself.** Facing a contradiction between M86's prose and its own sidecar, M97 wrote an independent sub-lattice extractor, gather and NCC scale ladder *in the milestone* rather than importing the pipeline's -- explicitly *"so that a shared bug cannot make two measurements agree with each other and with nothing else."* Its figure of **0.85714** reproduced the orchestrator's independently measured **0.85715** to five decimals, which is the strongest cross-check the corpus holds on any geometric quantity. Two implementations sharing a helper are one implementation.
623. **Any cache or sidecar a concurrent process can read must be written through a temp file and renamed.** M97 measured -- by accident, while debugging something else -- a **torn read** of `bee-3-cpl/warpmap.txt`: a sibling milestone was rewriting it in place and the reader got a half-written file that parsed and merely lacked a key. With many agents live in one working tree this is not a theoretical race. Write-then-rename makes a reader see either the old file or the new one and never a partial one.
624. **PowerShell's `[int]` rounds half to even, so `[int](3/2)` is `2`.** `$v[[int]($v.Count/2)]` on a sorted 3-element array returns the **max** and calls it the median; M97's timing harness reported **29.51 s** for a set whose median is **21.67 s**. Use `[math]::Floor` for an index. The general form: a language's default rounding mode is a silent participant in every index and every bin edge you compute.
625. **Accept a remedy on ground truth, never on the metric that named the defect.** M87's halo correction improves its own halo metric by **72.9%** on the owner's bee while **erasing the abdomen hairs and replacing them with a milky scalloped blob more objectionable than the halo it removed**. Against a synthetic scene with known truth the same correction cuts the halo metric **79.8%** and raises RMSE against truth by **254.6%**. In the author's words: *"the metric and the eye disagree, and the eye is right."* An artifact metric measures the presence of the artifact, which is not the same quantity as the correctness of the picture, and optimising the first will happily destroy the second.
626. **A remedy that also fires on a control containing no defect is keying on the wrong feature, however good its headline looks.** M87's mode partition cut the halo metric **63.9%** on a region built to contain no occlusion at all -- raising RMSE **558.4%** -- and on real data it moved **85.4%** of pixels at a *planted non-occluding disc* against **82.1%** at the bee's genuine occluding edge, i.e. slightly **more** where there was nothing to fix. The detector keys on silhouettes, not occlusions. Run the no-defect control before believing the defect one.
627. **A model-fit statistic is not a correctness statistic; do not gate admission on R-squared.** M87's synthetic plant, where the unmixing genuinely works and band RMSE is **1.71%**, has a median band R-squared of **0.058** -- *lower* than `bee-3-cpl`'s **0.131**, where the same arm fails. A model can fit a wrong thing tightly and a right thing loosely. The quantity that matters here is the intercept, and on real data nothing currently checks it.
628. **An instrument needs specificity as well as sensitivity, and the specificity control is the one that changes the design.** A plant proves the instrument can respond; it does not prove the instrument responds to the right thing. Pair every sensitivity plant with a plant of a DIFFERENT defect that the metric claims to be blind to, and require it to read null. The anisotropy metric passed its sensitivity plant while a direction-blind Gaussian moved it 44% (0.5268 -> 0.3069) -- it was a softness detector, not an orientation detector, and only the specificity arm could tell. Fact 1281.
629. **Choose a plant's sub-step count from its magnitude, or the plant models something other than what it names.** A radial smear integrated over a fixed 7 sub-steps is not a smear at 150 px, it is seven copies 25 px apart, and a comb's transfer function has passbands rather than a monotone roll-off. That plant left the outer annuli untouched (0.6337 -> 0.6304) while firing at the CENTRE, where its spacing happened to land its first zero inside the measurement band -- the exact inverse of the geometry it was supposed to model, which would have been read as the instrument failing. Require the largest step to be at most half a pixel, and interpolate: a nearest-neighbour plant at 1 px rounds to a no-op and silently reports mean |delta| of 0.00 DN.
630. **Select the measurement population on the UNTREATED data and reuse that exact set in every arm.** A treatment that destroys signal will otherwise select its own survivors. A per-arm texture-quantile filter dropped precisely the outer tiles a planted radial smear had hit hardest, leaving a population enriched for tiles the plant had failed to affect, and a 150 px plant consequently read as a 0.0026 change. This is the same failure mode as fitting a threshold on the test set, and it is invisible unless the arms are paired by construction.
631. **A degraded anchor must be built the way the pipeline would emit it, not the way the degradation is defined.** Binning is defined as a block mean, and the obvious anchor replicates that mean across its block -- but a real binned pipeline scales back up smoothly and emits no blocks. The replicated anchor's block edges put 9x more power at 0.445 cyc/px than the full-resolution source, inverting the two anchors and sending the test toward the wrong verdict; switching the same anchor to a smooth rescale separated them by 2.6563 dex and reversed the answer. Facts 1284, 1285. The general form: when an anchor is a synthetic degradation, ask what artefacts the synthesis introduces that the real process does not, and gate the test on the anchors actually bracketing the measurement before reading any verdict from it.
632. **Two independent routes to the same mechanism is worth more than either measurement's error bar, and it is what licenses acting instead of measuring again.** The coverage rescale was found twice in one night by authors who had not seen each other's work: M98 optically, recovering k = 0.9315 from a photograph of a ruler at 0.68σ, and the orchestrator spectrally, pricing that same operation at 64.2% of a deficit measured against an independently decoded RAW. Neither alone would have justified changing the output path -- the orchestrator had already been wrong twice the same night, on the half-drift (fact 1280) and on binning (fact 1284), each time with a plausible single line of evidence. The rule: **when a mechanism is expensive to act on, require a second route to it that shares no instrument, no author, and no assumption with the first**; and when you get one, stop measuring and build. Facts 1287, 1289.
633. **Verify a subagent's claim that something is ABSENT with the same rigour as a claim that something is present -- and treat 'retracted' and 'absent' as opposite findings.** M98 reported "discipline 605 does not exist in SYNTHESIS"; it exists at line 3066, struck through and retracted via fact 1250, and is cited as live corpus in fact 1273. A strikethrough or a stale copy most likely defeated the search. The distinction is not bookkeeping: an **absent** discipline invites the next milestone to re-derive the claim from scratch, whereas a **retracted** one forecloses it *and records why*, which is the more valuable artefact. One grep settled it before the error could propagate into a report. Companion to the standing rule about confirming a claimed fabrication is actually in the target document.
634. **Read the invocation that produced the file before drawing any conclusion from it -- the default path is almost never the path your artefacts took.** The orchestrator spent three messages and two reversals on whether the output was binned, arguing from `main.rs`'s documented default, while both of its own render scripts had been passing `--demosaic` all along. One grep of `gallery.py` settled what an hour of spectral measurement had left contested, and it should have come first. This is the same failure as mistaking a module filename for a command name, one level up: **a documented default is a claim about the program, not about your data.** Fact 1291.
635. **When a bound is offered as an explanation, state in the fact whether it identifies or merely permits.** The demosaic spread of 0.3518 dex makes a 0.1301 dex residual unsurprising, which is genuinely useful -- it means no new mechanism need be invented. It is **not** evidence that the residual *is* demosaic, and a fact that blurs the two would let a later milestone close an open question it never actually answered. Write the distinction into the fact itself rather than only into the script's docstring, because the fact is what gets read. Fact 1292.
636. **Never cache derived data in the directory you read the inputs from, and treat a read-only corpus as an invariant the code enforces rather than one the operator remembers.** Every agent tonight was told `D:\personal\macro` is read-only; eleven cache files landed there anyway, because the *program* wrote them and no one had told the program. The failure is structural, not one of discipline: an instruction given to agents cannot bind a binary they invoke. Two consequences worth carrying: derived state belongs in a location derived from the *output* path, never the input path; and any file multiple processes may write must be temp-plus-renamed, because with enough concurrency a torn read is not a race you might lose but the steady state. Fact 1296.
637. **Before attributing a complaint, establish which artefact the complainant actually looked at.** Hours went into deciding whether the owner judged the dark render or the exposed one, and the answer was sitting in one line of the script that built the thing he was shown. Two consequences: the fix you are most excited about is not automatically the fix for the complaint you received, and a defect being real is independent of it being *the* defect -- exposure was genuinely broken and genuinely not the answer. When elimination is the method, name what was eliminated and how, because an argument from elimination is only as strong as the completeness of the list. Facts 1293, 1297.
638. **An artifact-suppression metric is satisfied by destruction as readily as by reconstruction, so it can never certify a fix on its own.** M87 registered bar X4 to catch exactly this and **X4 FAILED**: three of four *deliberately broken* unmixings still improved the halo metric by **77-85%**, one of them wrong by six orders of magnitude. Flattening a near-edge profile satisfies the metric whether the veil was removed or the neighbourhood was obliterated. **Any suppression metric needs a paired fidelity term measured against truth** -- on the plant, the working reconstruction moved band RMSE 3.46% -> 1.82% while the cosmetic partition moved it **+254.6%**, and only the fidelity term could tell them apart. This generalises far past halos: it applies to every denoiser, deblurrer, and artifact remover this project will ever gate. Facts 1298, 1300.
639. **Sweep a correction's strength; never evaluate it at a single setting.** M87 tested photometric normalisation against the halo at five strengths and found the response **monotone increasing** -- the best correction is none. Evaluated only at full strength it reads **−8.4%**, which is a plausible-looking win pointing the wrong way. A one-point test cannot distinguish "this helps" from "this hurts and the endpoint happens to sit low", and the cost of the ladder was four extra runs. Fact 1301.
640. **Attribute from a current read, not merely from the right file.** The orchestrator attributed three lint violations to M87 by file -- the correct method, discipline 593 -- and was still wrong, because the read was stale: the violation had been fixed two commits earlier and the reported line number was 41 lines off. M87 disproved it with two independent instruments and told the orchestrator not to fold the thanks. **Re-run the check immediately before attributing it to someone**, and treat a line number that does not match as evidence the read is old rather than as a rounding error. Related: the orchestrator also briefed M87 with a falsifier whose test population did not exist -- three boundaries claimed to have reversed contrast polarity were reflectance edges at a single depth.
641. **Write the candidate list down before eliminating anything, because the causes you never considered are invisible to an argument from elimination.** Fact 1297 eliminated exposure and concluded "therefore sharpness", in the same commit as discipline 637, which warns that elimination is only as strong as the list's completeness. The omitted cause -- the occlusion halo -- had already been *seen by the same author* in their own review artefact. An enumerated list turns an omission into a visible blank; an unenumerated one turns it into a confident conclusion. Facts 1297, 1304.
642. **Measure a degradation's cost on the image it will actually be applied to, not on a sharper proxy.** The orchestrator priced the coverage rescale by gathering on a single rawpy-decoded frame and read **+0.2392 dex**; M104 planted the same factor on the **render** and read **+0.1789**. A resample costs more on sharper input, so the proxy inflated the answer by 34% and, through it, a bar registered with two agents. The general form: a degradation's cost is a property of the *pair* (operation, input spectrum), never of the operation alone. Fact 1309.
643. **State every sharpness bar in a named frequency band, and never accept 'no measurable difference' from a band-averaged metric.** M104 measured the rescale's cost as a **null at the comb and +0.1623 dex near Nyquist** -- a defect living entirely in the top octave, invisible to any metric that integrates across the band. That is how a +7.35% interpolated enlargement of every pixel survived in the shipped pipeline. Corroborated from the other side by M87, where a gather destroying ~49% of gradient energy moved the halo metric by +0.6%. Fact 1307.
644. **A stem check is not a lock: it answers whether a number has been taken, not whether it is about to be.** M104 checked four registers, found `M101` free, and committed first -- and another agent claimed `M101` within the hour. It renumbered itself rather than standing on precedence, on the grounds that six renames beat a permanently ambiguous citation stem. With many concurrent agents, treat identifier allocation as racy by default and prefer yielding to arguing. M104's P10.
645. **Before declaring two measurements in conflict, express them in the same convention.** The orchestrator halted a milestone over M87's −3.18% against M99's +5.31%, which were **brightness** and **correction gain** -- reciprocals. In one convention they were +3.23% and +5.31%: the same sign, agreeing, differing only by region. A reciprocal convention flips a sign and is indistinguishable from a defect at a glance, and the cost of the check is reading one line of the source that computes it. **Escalate after the conversion, never before.** Fact 1311.
646. **A probe region should be chosen for compactness, not merely for avoiding the subject.** M87 registered an area control on its `distance_transform_edt(~mask) > 60` far-background region and **the control failed**: a contiguous block of the same area drifts 0.041% where the distance mask drifts 0.206%, five times worse, because a mask that hugs the subject has a long perimeter and leaks flux across all of it. Subject-avoidance is necessary and not sufficient; perimeter is the term that was missing. Fact 1312.
647. **A split-half is not a placebo, and neither is sufficient alone.** M101's placebo (B2) passed at 0.000 on the same plane where the split-half (B1) failed at 0.077. They answer different questions: the placebo proves the instrument is not hallucinating agreement between unrelated coordinate sets; only the split-half proves the map is a map. **Two published censuses of this sensor ran neither.** Any claim that a detected population is real needs both. Facts 1316, 1317.
648. **Cross-census agreement is not reproducibility when both censuses read the same frames.** M101's map replicates M48c's independent census to **+7.0%** at site-by-site Jaccard **0.90**, and simultaneously fails its own split-half at **0.077-0.401**. There is no contradiction: two criteria applied to one noise realisation will agree with each other while each is individually unreliable. **Agreement between analyses is evidence about the analyses; only resampling the data is evidence about the data.** Fact 1316.
649. **When a registered bar fails, first ask whether your own instrument caused it.** M101's split-half halved the frame count, which raised the DN cut, which made the two halves maps of *different sensitivity*. It re-ran with the cut held fixed in DN at the full map's value: G2 moved 0.352 to 0.401 and the failure survived. **Do that before either moving the bar or believing the result** -- the bar must not move, and a self-inflicted failure is not a finding. Fact 1316.
650. **Give a null an amplitude ladder, not just a control.** "No enrichment" is a weak claim that any insensitive instrument can produce. "No enrichment below 100 DN, 1.20x at 250, 1.43x at 500, and the real defect is 1.5 DN" is a **bound**, and it converts a null into a measured margin of 67x. Every null this project ships should carry the dose at which the effect would have been visible. Fact 1315.
651. **Predict where a positive control will turn on before you plant it.** M101 derived `dFocus = 0.002905*A/sigma_L` from the shipped arithmetic and predicted the election would begin preferring a planted spike between 100 and 250 DN; it did. A control that confirms only *that* an instrument responds is far weaker than one that confirms *where* -- the latter tests the model of the mechanism, not merely the wiring, and it is what licenses extrapolating the null down to the real amplitude. Fact 1315.
652. **Never put a numeric constant in a dispatch that you have not read from the shipped source in the same session.** The M101 brief asserted "RN ~3 e-" as this sensor's read noise. `profile.rs` ships 4.20 e- below ISO 400 and 1.2392 above it; ~3 appears nowhere except as fact 795's re-labelling of 1.2392 into electrons, which is explicitly not what the model evaluates. **A fabricated constant in a brief carries the orchestrator's authority** and will be used unless the agent independently re-derives it. Fact 1322.
653. **Rules 40 and 43 exist because the orchestrator is the one most likely to break them.** The M101 brief presented as open a question that four committed reports had already worked, and the agent -- not the orchestrator -- caught it by searching `docs/research/` before measuring. **A subordinate's literature search is the last line of defence, not the first.** Brief every milestone from a search run in the same session, and put the search in the dispatch, not the conclusion drawn from it. Fact 1322.
654. **Look for an accidental lever in data already held before commissioning a capture.** Every one of the 242 delivered darks is 1/100 s, so the calibration set alone could not separate a fixed per-site offset from dark current, and two published reports quoted the mixture without noticing. The owner's ordinary photographs run at 20x the exposure at the same gain, and that single uncontrolled difference settled the fork for free. **A dataset that varies is worth more than one that is internally consistent.** Fact 1318.
655. **Verify that a fix reaches the artefact the complaint was about, not merely the defect it names.** M95 measured a real, large, shipped defect -- the viewing render binned 32.97 MP to 8.24 MP -- and the orchestrator was one sentence from reporting it to the owner as the answer to his verdict on the gallery. **`gallery.py` already passed `--demosaic`; every render he judged was 32.97 MP.** A general mechanism and the particular image in the owner's hands are different claims and need separate evidence. Third instance of this class after facts 1297 and 1304. Fact 1324.
656. **A bar must not equal the plant it is meant to detect.** M102's D1 planted a one-frame index shift against a bar of `|median signed| <= 1.0`; the estimator recovered **-1.0000 exactly** and the plant passed on the threshold. A plant sitting on its own bar cannot fail, so the arm proves nothing while reading green. Separate the plant from the bar by a stated margin before running. Fact 1329.
657. **Size a geometric plant against the scene, not against the sensor.** M102's D2 expressed an unmodelled warp as a fraction of the sensor half-diagonal and it did nothing. Swept, it reddens only at **2.91 depth-slab widths**: an index map is blind to geometric error below the scene's depth autocorrelation length, because shifting a pixel to a neighbour of the same depth changes no index. **The scale that matters is the one the statistic can resolve**, and it is a property of the content, not the detector. Fact 1329.
658. **A synthetic agreement figure is worthless wherever the synthesis assumed the thing being checked.** M102 flagged this correctly against itself -- its photometric drift reproduces fact 1254's *predicted* 1.1132 rather than the measured 1.1091, and it warned M99 not to read that as validation. **The same objection applies to its 96.96% aligner recovery**, which was measured against a breathing track M102 planted as linear because the corpus does not record the track's curvature. Before quoting a simulator agreement, name what the generator assumed, and check the list against what the number is being used to prove. Fact 1331.
659. **A bar that binds only where the previous attempt succeeded cannot catch the next failure.** The orchestrator required the halo fix to be scored against **truth**; M87 refused, because truth exists only on synthetic data and the previous attempt **already passed there** (3.46% -> 1.82%) while failing on the real bee where no truth exists. Before registering a bar, run it mentally against the *last* failure: if it would have scored that failure green, it is the wrong bar. Fact 1333.
660. **Report which direction a confound runs, not merely that it exists.** M97b's gradient-energy metric is genuinely fooled by misregistration seams -- a deliberately jittered render measures **sharper** (0.674 / 0.665 / 0.851). That does not weaken its result, it **bounds it from below**, because the best-registered arm still measured the most energy. A confound running against the claim is evidence for it; a confound reported without its direction is an unpriced caveat that invites dismissal. Fact 1326.
661. **An exact zero from a sensitivity check is a suspect, not a pass.** M95's geometry sweep monkeypatched a module-level constant that `s6_signal.py` binds as a **default argument**, evaluated once at definition time, so the patch changed nothing and the run printed a change of **exactly 0.00 percentage points** -- a number that reads as a clean pass and is in fact the instrument reporting it was never perturbed. The same run also hard-coded the constant a second time in a loss weight. **The exact zero is what gave it away**; treat any control that returns a perfectly round null as unverified until the perturbation is confirmed to have landed. Compare discipline 648. Fact 1337.
662. **Do not offer a spread across adaptive algorithms as a menu of available wins.** The orchestrator twice described a 0.3518 dex band-power spread across rawpy's demosaic algorithms as a free win. Six of the candidates are content-adaptive, so the ranking rewards **hallucination as resolution** -- the spread bounds what could be won and what could be faked equally, and band power cannot separate them. The reasoning was already written in `demosaic.rs:19-51`, in the file documenting why MHC was chosen. Fact 1336.
663. **Re-read the shipped source before dispatching from your own plan, not merely before writing a brief from memory.** The orchestrator's carry-forward next-steps list named a milestone to dispatch on the 484 flat fields and prescribed moving PRNU into `PlaneNoise::variance`. The data had been consumed by M71 and the prescription refuted by M90, whose reasoning is written in the module header of the exact file the change would have touched. **A plan written at time T is a claim about the repository at time T, and it expires.** Rules 40 and 43 bind the brief; this binds the plan that produces briefs. Fact 1338.
664. **"Measured and implemented" is not "shipped" -- check which binary path the owner actually invokes.** The exposure correction was recorded in fact 1293 as *already implemented and tested when found*, and it was: in `gallery.py`, in numpy, outside the binary. The corpus carried it as solved for long enough that two subsequent milestones chased sharpness instead. **Before ranking a defect as addressed, name the executable and the flag the owner runs and confirm the fix is on that path.** This is the same class as fact 1324, where a real fix was confirmed in general and never checked against the artefact in hand. Fact 1339.
