665. **Open the render before you describe it to the owner.** The orchestrator opened M97b's side-by-side rather than relaying its prose, and the bright low-texture regions of the gain-corrected arm show smooth waxy blobs with hard boundaries occupying a large fraction of one panel -- an artefact M97b reported honestly but which reads in text as a caveat and on screen as disqualifying. The owner photographs insects and flowers, which are bright and smooth exactly where this fails. **A sharpness win that melts highlights is a net loss, and only the image says so.** Routed to M103 as a gate on shipping, with three candidate mechanisms to separate.
666. **A crop selector that maximises a sharpness statistic is a biased instrument for judging how a subject rendered.** `gallery.py`'s `detail_peak` chooses the highest-gradient-energy box, so on `flowers-cpl` it returned sharp background fabric beside mushy petals and presented it as the stack's 100% crop. The selector will preferentially display the backdrop precisely when the subject is failing, which is the one case the crop exists to reveal. **Site detail crops by subject or at random, and never let the quantity being judged also choose where it is judged.** Fact 1343.
667. **Before reasoning about what the owner saw, establish which file he was shown.** The orchestrator twice folded a conclusion about the owner's verdict from the gallery renders, reaching opposite answers, when the images he had actually been given were a different set written hours earlier -- binned to 8.24 MP, uncoloured, unaligned, and haloed. **The transcript names the path and the file carries its own timestamp and dimensions; both are cheap and both are authoritative.** Owner feedback is evidence about a specific artefact, and it is worthless as evidence about any other. Facts 1344, 1345.
668. **State the scope of any search that produces a negative claim, in the same sentence as the claim.** The orchestrator briefed a milestone on *there is no exposure logic in the CLI at all*, from a grep of one crate, when the logic sat fully implemented and tested in the other -- and instructed the agent to rebuild it. *"A grep of `crates/strehl-cli/src` finds none"* would have carried its own limitation and invited the check; *"there is none"* did not. **Absence of evidence is a fact about the search, and a brief that omits where you looked converts it into a fact about the repository.** Facts 1346, 1347.
669. **When a recorded absolute hash fails, restore the pre-change source, touch it, rebuild, and measure whether your own change is the cause -- before accepting any explanation, however plausible.** Four recorded hashes failed at once and a good story was available immediately: M95, M97, M86c and M87 had all landed since, and one of them wires alignment into the very path in question. The story was correct, and believing it would still have been wrong, because **the byte-freeze is the bar that exists precisely to not be argued away.** The control cost two 30-second rebuilds and converted *probably not me* into `CF266004...94B868 == CF266004...94B868`. Note the trap it had to route around: `Copy-Item` preserves the source mtime, so an untouched restore leaves cargo serving the binary you were trying to replace. Facts 1348, 1349.
670. **A gallery must render what the tool emits. If a script post-processes the output before the owner sees it, the owner is judging a program that does not exist.** `gallery.py` applied its own 0.92 gain on top of an un-exposed render for the whole period in which the owner said *those stacks don't look too good yet* -- so the verdict, the fix and the measurement were each about a slightly different image. **Any deviation between what is rendered and what is shown must be either eliminated or printed next to the picture.** Fact 1350.
671. **A cosmetic correction must be judged on a picture, and the crop must be chosen on the difference so that neither render selects the view.** M87's table said `-79.8 %` halo metric and `+254.6 %` RMSE, which is enough to decide *fidelity* and not enough to decide *whether the owner will prefer it* -- those are different claims and only the first had been measured. Looking settled it in one image: the correction trades a smooth artifact for a hard one. **Choosing the crop on the difference is the part that makes it evidence** rather than illustration; picking it on either render is discipline 666's biased selector wearing a new hat. Fact 1352.
672. **Parse machine output from its structured table, never by regex over its prose.** This corpus writes reports that cite fact numbers inline, so a pattern anchored on a label will sooner or later match a citation rather than a value -- `n_eff[^0-9]*([0-9.]+)` returned **212**, the fact number in the sentence following the label. **If a value must be scraped, anchor on the column structure and assert the result is in a possible range**: 212 effective frames from a 182-frame stack is impossible on its face and one bound would have caught it. Fact 1356.
673. **Design comparisons so the arms must disagree, because agreement where disagreement is compulsory is the cheapest instrument check there is.** The bogus `n_eff` was caught by nothing more than a pure selector and a 15-frame average reporting the same number. **A single-arm run would have folded it as a fact.** This generalises past parsing: whenever an arm's expected behaviour is qualitatively different, print the quantity for every arm and look at them together before interpreting any one of them. Fact 1356.
674. **Never score sharpness with an unreferenced high-frequency metric, because artifacts are high-frequency and the metric cannot tell them from detail.** Laplacian energy on a `flowers-cpl` crop rated pure selection **2.73x sharper** than the estimation merge; the picture shows the excess is polygonal winner-field patchwork with hard tile edges. **A sharpness proxy is only meaningful against a reference or a perceptual model** -- and when neither exists, the fallback is not a different proxy, it is looking at the image. Fact 1359.
675. **Before blaming the merge for a soft render, render `--gate 0` and look: pure selection is the upper bound on what selection can show.** If gate 0 is also soft, no single frame held the detail and the fault is upstream in the capture, which is a shooting instruction rather than a code change. Pin the exposure to a literal for both arms first, or the render becomes the variable instead of the merge. On `flowers-cpl` this took one script and moved the diagnosis from *the merge over-averages* to *the bracket did not span the subject*, corroborated independently by a 33.74 % boundary rate. Facts 1357, 1358.
676. **Pre-register bars two-sided, and state in advance what a result on the *other* side of 1.0 would mean.** A ratio bar of the form *"above 3x means A, below 1.5x means B"* silently assumes the effect cannot invert, so a strong inverted effect is scored as the null: 0.13x -- a 7.8x concentration the other way -- was reported as *"independent of contrast"*. **If a statistic can in principle run either way, every bar must have three branches, not two.** Fact 1362.
677. **Render a spatial statistic as a map before interpreting any scalar summary of it.** A boundary rate, a confidence rate and a re-election rate are all fields, and their *shape* carries the mechanism while their mean carries almost none of it. Region summaries said centre 30.79 % against periphery 27.53 % -- near-identical, and read as *"concentrated nowhere"* -- while the map showed the population is thin contours tracing occlusion edges, which no region-average could have expressed because contours run through every region equally. **The scalar was not merely weak here, it was actively misleading in two independent ways at once.** Facts 1360, 1362.
678. **Audit the control's render path with the same suspicion as the treatment's.** When two code paths exist in order to be compared against each other, any asymmetry between them is a thumb on the scale, and the *control* is the side nobody revisits -- it was written once, it is "the naive thing", and it attracts no further attention. `argmax-baseline --srgb` stayed at half resolution for nine milestones after `stack --srgb` was migrated, biasing every side-by-side toward the estimator. **Where two subcommands must agree on a rendering decision, express the decision once and make it impossible to change one without the other**; the fix duplicates the literal rule `demosaic || (srgb && !binned)` in both arms so that a future divergence requires editing both. Facts 1363, 1364.
679. **A passing check on the property you changed says nothing about the properties you did not think about.** The commit's headline check was resolution parity, and the branch it added could have transposed the CFA interleave while satisfying that check perfectly -- right size, wrong colours. Before claiming a branch correct, ask what a *different* defect in the same branch would look like to the check you just ran, and add the check that would see it. **Then state what your new check still cannot see** -- here, a bug shared by both compared paths. Fact 1366.
680. **Never read a pass/fail gate through a truncating pipeline.** `$LASTEXITCODE` reads **0** after a command that exited **1** whenever `Select-Object -First N` short-circuits the stream, and that is the standard idiom in this project for keeping tool output small. It fails in the dangerous direction: failures become successes, and red controls become green. **Capture the output and the code in two statements, then filter the captured variable** -- `$out = & $exe ... 2>&1; $code = $LASTEXITCODE` -- and never let a display convenience sit between a process and the status you are about to trust. Truncation also swallows error detail, so the same mistake hides the diagnosis it just mis-scored. Facts 1368, 1369.
681. **Before prescribing a fix, verify that the CONSUMING command can accept it.** ORCH instructed 7 live agents to isolate themselves with `strehl align --out <scratch>`; the instruction was inert, because `strehl stack` has no sidecar argument and always reads `<stackdir>/warpmap.txt`. The producing side took the flag, the consuming side ignored it, and every affected agent would have believed itself isolated while sharing the same file. **A workaround is not verified until it has been traced through the reader as well as the writer** -- and here the correct mechanism (`STREHL_WARPMAP`) already existed, better designed than the one being invented, and was found only by reading the consumer. Fact 1367.
682. **When one operation has both a manual and an automatic entry point, check that their defaults agree -- and treat any divergence as a defect in the manual one.** The automatic path is exercised on every run and its default is therefore continuously tested; the manual path's default is chosen once, by whoever wrote the flag, and is often the naive value (`0`, `1`, the first element) rather than the considered one. `strehl align --reference` defaults to frame 0 where the merge uses the middle frame, so invoking the tool by hand degrades the registration relative to not invoking it at all. **A new operating rule that tells people to use the manual path inherits every divergence the manual path has** -- rule 45 did exactly that -- so audit the defaults at the moment you promote a manual invocation, not afterwards. Fact 1370.
683. **Do not name a mechanism from a small crop. Enlarge until the artifact's boundary is fully inside the frame, then name it.** A 520 px view of a silhouette veil read as hard-edged polygonal tiling; the same region at 1100x900 showed smooth organic contours and no straight edge anywhere. Small crops truncate curvature into apparent straight lines and truncate gradients into apparent flat regions, so they systematically bias a diagnosis **toward** the geometric, tiled, algorithmic-looking explanation -- which is the explanation an engineer is already primed to accept. The cost is not a wasted look but a misrouted milestone: the two readings have different owners, different files and different fixes. Facts 1371, 1372.
684. **Before building a switch, grep the consumer for the value.** Twice in one session a milestone was commissioned to make something selectable that was already selectable end to end -- here the gather kernel, already serialised by `warpmap.rs:597`, parsed at `:806` and honoured at `merge_cmd.rs:923`. The check costs one grep of the *consumer* -- not the producer, which is where the earlier `align --out` mistake came from. Facts 1373, and `19c0a61`.
685. **When ablating, prefer varying a serialised field over changing code.** Rewriting one line of a sidecar holds every other solved quantity byte-identical and supplies a free validity control: the unmodified arm must reproduce a prior render exactly. A code-level ablation holds nothing fixed by construction, requires a rebuild, and offers no way to detect that something else moved underneath it. Fact 1376.
686. **A dimension in a sidecar or log describes the stage that wrote it, not the pipeline's output.** `plane 3516x2344` beside a `7032x4688` render reads as a 2x upscale and is not one -- a four-plane CFA is half-size on each axis by construction. Resolve any such apparent discrepancy against the **writer's own log line**, which states the emitted geometry directly, before inferring a resampling step that would invalidate every measurement taken downstream of it. Fact 1377.
687. **Record the entire invocation beside every frozen hash -- directory, limit, and every flag INCLUDING the ones left at their default.** "We used the default" is not a record, because defaults move and because the next reader cannot tell a default from an omission. One absent `--gate` on a `DEFAULT_GATE = 4.0` pipeline manufactured a hash mismatch that was internally consistent in every other respect and cost a 1.9-hour investigation. Facts 1379, 1382.
688. **An untested freeze is an unverified freeze.** Every byte-freeze in this project was enforced by prose in a report; one of them went stale for weeks while being cited *in the source code* as live proof. A citation to an artifact is a dependency and nothing in the build knows about it. The test must make intended change **visible and deliberate**, not prevented -- most moves here are improvements, and a golden test that only says "assertion failed" gets silenced by the third person who hits it. Facts 1381, 1382.
689. **When a freeze breaks, verify the command before investigating the code.** Re-render the baseline with its own recorded invocation first; only then diff commits. The corpus's one instance ran the search in the opposite order and spent 1.9 h bisecting eight commits, three of which were ancestors of the baseline and two of which touched no `crates/` file. Fact 1379.
690. **A convention announced is not a convention enforced; if it matters, make the wrong thing impossible rather than forbidden.** Two independent instances in one session: a frozen hash held only in prose went stale for weeks while being cited in source, and a rule broadcast to seven agents was violated within minutes. Before relying on a written rule, ask what mechanism would make its violation fail loudly -- a test, a validation, a permission -- and cost that mechanism out. Where enforcement is genuinely blocked (file contention, an owner's workflow), **record the blocker explicitly** so the deferral is a decision rather than an omission. Facts 1381, 1385, 1386.
691. **A residue of n = 3 supports no statistics of its own; test its mechanism against the population it came from.** Three unmoved pixels invited a geometric story (edge, corner, column) and every such story was refuted -- but the refutation came from n = 29 572 samples, not from the three. Where a handful of outliers is all the evidence there is, find the larger population they are instances of and characterise **that**; the outliers can then only be reported as consistent with it, which is the honest strength of the claim. Facts 1387, 1388.
692. **A freeze record must bind the environment, not only the command line.** Environment variables that alter the pipeline -- `STREHL_ALIGN`, `STREHL_WARPMAP`, `STREHL_FIX_HALO` -- are as much part of a frozen hash's provenance as any flag, and are **more** dangerous because nothing in the shell history records them. A freeze that reproduces only under an unrecorded variable looks identical to a stale freeze from the outside. Fact 1389; rule 47 as amended.
693. **One fixture cannot cover both an isolated path and an integrated one; pin both and state the trade.** An isolated fixture (dependencies disabled) is reproducible and blind; an integrated one covers the real pipeline and inherits its fragility. Choosing only the integrated one buys coverage at the price of the exact instability the freeze exists to detect; choosing only the isolated one is safe and tests nothing that matters. Facts 1389, 1392.
694. **Establish where a knob has leverage before attributing an artifact to it, and choose ROIs across the leverage axis rather than at one extreme.** The first sharpness crop was taken on the most-detailed tile in the image -- which is precisely the region where the gate provably does nothing (n_eff = 1 at every gate), so the comparison was inconclusive **by construction** and would have read as 'no effect' whether or not one existed. Sampling flattest / median / most-detailed turned the same four renders into a decisive result. Fact 1393.
695. **A profile referenced to a baseline that itself moves between arms measures the baseline, not the feature.** When every ring of a radial profile -- including the far ring intended as background -- shifts monotonically in the same direction across arms, the reference is moving and no localised claim can be extracted. Either pin the reference to one arm, or measure a quantity invariant to the shift. Facts 1398, 1399.
696. **A bar that fails cheaply is worth more than a bar that passes.** Bar G0 (auto-exposure must not differ between arms) failed at 0.05 stops and forced four re-renders costing ~3.6 minutes -- and the failed arms then supplied an independent corroboration of the main result through a different mechanism (fact 1397). Registering a confound check before the run converts a discovered confound from a retraction into a measurement. Fact 1397.
697. **A predicted structural signature is only a falsifiable test if the band it lives in is signal-dominated; check that first, with a control that can show the band is full of something else.** Predicting a resampling cutoff at a named frequency is exactly the right shape of test -- it can only pass at one place -- but it has no power where noise already fills the band. The control that revealed this was free: an arm known to change noise but not detail showed 3-4x the power at the same frequencies, and the apparent 'cutoff' moved with it. Fact 1401.
698. **Report every placement number with the gauge it was measured in, because the gauge changes it by 2.6x.** The same track reads **98.2 px** referenced to frame 0 and **37.5 px** referenced to rung 144. A bare 'error in px' for an alignment solve is not a number, and two such numbers from different milestones are not comparable. Facts 1407, 1408.
699. **Score the bar on what the system actually consumes, not on the most convenient summary of it.** Four separate acceptance bars, across four milestones, all scored the composition end-to-end because it is one easy pair -- while the merge gathers all 299 frames independently. The error survived that long because nobody asked what the *consumer* reads. **Before accepting any bar, name the consumer and check the bar measures its input.** Fact 1407.
700. **When a mechanism turns out to have the opposite sign to the one you assumed, re-read your failed instruments before rebuilding them.** I declared my veil profile a failure because it found darkness where I predicted brightness, and reached for contamination to explain it away. The darkness was the signal (facts 1403, 1405). **A measurement that disagrees in *sign* is the single most likely place a wrong model is hiding** -- an instrument that finds a large, structured, repeatable effect you did not predict has probably not failed.
701. **A rule derived from a summary statistic must be re-scored when the gauge changes; it does not inherit its authority.** Rule 6's discard instruction was correct on every end-to-end measurement ever run against it and is harmful by 628.1 px per frame. **Standing rules in this corpus are measurements with a shelf life, not axioms** -- when a new gauge appears, the rules written in the old one are the first things to re-run. Fact 1408.
702. **A checker that cannot print its findings is not a checker, and a shared exit code hides which of the two failed.** `corpus_lint.py` found seven violations and reported zero of them because its reporter could not encode the text it was quoting, then exited 1 -- the same code it uses for 'violations found'. **Every gate in this project must be tested in the mode its callers actually use** (here: stdout piped, not a console), and **must distinguish tool failure from subject failure in its exit code or its output**, or a green run and a broken run are the same observation. The A/B that establishes this needs the pre-fix arm to go *red* first; a passing post-fix arm alone proves nothing about the fix. Fact 1412.
703. **A defect the pipeline BAKES IN outranks a defect the pipeline merely fails to remove, because only one of them is still fixable downstream.** Axial CA is optical and universal; what makes fact 1413 serious is that the merge elects on green and then gathers red and blue at green's frame, so the sharp red is in a frame the renderer chose not to read and no later stage can recover it. **When triaging quality defects, sort by whether the information still exists in the output**, not by effect size.
704. **Rank a fix by parameters-per-pixel-of-gain, not by how fundamental it sounds.** M107 measured two chroma mechanisms in one milestone: one needs a merge-architecture change, a per-channel noise model and 4-4.5x wall clock; the other is **one scalar** worth **~3 output px at the corner** with no extra pass. The second is the one to ship, and the discovery order was the reverse of the shipping order. Facts 1414, 1417.
705. **When an ablation reads 'threshold, not dose', stop looking for a proportional term -- the mechanism is a gate.** Coverage-alone and warp-alone each cost nearly as much as both together, because the cost is triggered by the sampling phase being non-integral *at all*, not by how far from integral it is. **I predicted 64.2% from the size of the geometric change and measured 7.8%**, because I reasoned about magnitude where the mechanism was binary. Before pricing a fix from the size of the thing it removes, check whether the response is graded. Fact 1419.
706. **A normaliser that fits a free parameter is blind to any defect that looks like that parameter.** `decompose`'s per-bin alpha absorbs a linear gain by construction, so every control built on it was structurally incapable of seeing a change that acted as a gain -- and would have returned green forever. **The only way to find this class of blindness is to plant the exact defect the control claims to catch and confirm it goes red.** A control that has never been shown to fail is not a control. Fact 1423.
707. **Periodically re-render the pinned baseline and check whether the product actually moved, because a night of commits is not a night of progress.** 14 commits and 3 changes to `crates/` produced a byte-identical image. That is simultaneously a clean freeze result and an uncomfortable one, and only the re-render distinguishes 'correctly inert' from 'busy'. **The cheapest honest status report is the hash of the output**, not a count of commits or facts. Fact 1424.
708. **A before/after montage is an argument, so build the control that removes its cheapest explanation.** Most of the visible difference between the judged render and HEAD is brightness, and brightness is free -- a third panel applying the new exposure to the old pixels costs nothing and converts the montage from a flattering comparison into a measurement. Likewise: upscale the *older, worse* image with NEAREST rather than a smooth kernel, and register with **integer** offsets only, or the presentation itself blurs the quantity being compared. Facts 1425, 1426.
709. **Pre-clear `$LASTEXITCODE` before every arm of an exit-code experiment, and verify the pre-clear took.** It is ambient state that survives across commands, so an arm that fails to set it silently inherits its neighbour's verdict. This is discipline 706 in a new costume: without the pre-clear, the control could not have gone red, and it did not. Fact 1429.
710. **When a bar goes red on an unexpected VALUE rather than an unexpected direction, interrogate the value before touching the bar.** `exit_code_trap.ps1`'s E2 was written as `Code -eq 0` because that is what the defect had been reported to look like, and it failed against `-1`. The reflex is to read the bar as too strict and relax it; the correct reading was that the corruption is host-dependent (fact 1428), which is a finding the loosened bar would have erased. **A bar that fails for a reason you did not anticipate has just done its job.** Facts 1427, 1428.
711. **Never hand down a bare workaround: name the defect it compensates for, or you have immunised the recipient against detecting it.** `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in a brief looks like a courtesy and functions as a blindfold -- it suppressed a live defect in the corpus's own gate for every agent who complied, which is every agent. Write workarounds as **"do X because Y is broken; if Y ever works, tell me"**, never as a bare instruction. Fact 1430.
712. **Give a harness three exit codes -- pass, subject failed, tool failed -- because two collapses the distinction that matters.** The default path in both PowerShell and Python leads to one failure code for both, so this must be done deliberately. Without it, a broken instrument is indistinguishable from a genuine red, and this corpus's recurring failure mode is precisely mistaking the instrument for the subject (facts 1412, 1428, 1429). Fact 1431.
713. **Look at the whole image before trusting a number computed on part of it.** A hand-placed ROI inherits every error in its placement, and averaging is the most efficient way to dilute a localised defect to nothing -- my ROI cleared a 2.002% magenta blob to a 0.2% agreement with LibRaw. **Let the predicate find the region**: threshold, then report the bounding box, centroid and extent from the data. It cannot be mis-aimed and it gives the extent for free. Facts 1432, 1434.
714. **Before publishing a before/after comparison, make it prove the two sides show the same thing.** Register a correlation floor and let it abort the montage. `then_vs_now_all.py`'s R1 caught that the judged and current `marker` renders cannot be rigidly registered at all, because alignment's FOV crop makes the difference a scale change rather than a translation. Without the bar the montage would have rendered anyway, silently comparing two different parts of the subject. Fact 1433.
715. **When two agents produce two different mechanisms for one defect, suspect the shared harness before either theory.** ORCH said count, M104c said race, and both were reasoning from arms that inherited a stale `$LASTEXITCODE`. The pre-clear settled it in one run, 5/5 in each direction, and the answer was the *original* claim. **A disagreement about mechanism is evidence about the instrument**, and re-measuring with the confound removed is cheaper than arguing. Facts 1427, 1429.
716. **Before building a control, grep for one -- this codebase documents controls that milestones then rebuild.** M104c was assigned an identity-warp null; the null it actually needed already existed as `STREHL_ALIGN=zoom`, with a comment stating its purpose verbatim, and the assigned design provably could not have worked because `cover_or_explain` overrides placements downstream. **The orchestrator specified a mechanism it had not read the code for.** Specify the *property* the control must have and let the implementer find or build it. Fact 1436.
717. **Put the pre-registered prediction in the harness's own data structure, and let a mismatch fail the run.** `exit_code_trap2.ps1` carries a `Pred` column written before execution and bar E4 scores every arm against it. That is what caught the cold-start anomaly: a harness that merely *printed* codes would have shown `1,-1,-1,-1,-1` and been read past as noise. **A prediction stored beside the measurement cannot be quietly revised after seeing it** -- and when E4 went red the correct response was 320 more reps, not an edited prediction. Pair it with a determinism bar (E5): unanimity across reps is what distinguishes a mechanism from a tendency. Fact 1437.
718. **An output-artefact audit needs an unstacked single frame of the SAME scene as its control, and the control must be run before any finding is dispatched.** Without it there is no way to separate "strehl produced this" from "this is what the subject looks like", and the separation is not guessable: one check had the control scoring *worse* than the product. Develop the middle frame through LibRaw with camera WB and no auto-bright, run the identical battery, and report every number as a ratio to its control. Fact 1438.
719. **A metric that can exceed its own logical range is not a weak metric, it is a broken one -- stop and find the defect rather than ranking with it.** The overshoot check returned 147%, and a fraction cannot exceed 100%: numerator and denominator had different supports. Had it returned a plausible 14.7% the same bug would have been invisible and the number would have been folded. **Range-check every ratio metric against its definition before reading it**, and treat an out-of-range value as information about the instrument, never as a large effect. Fact 1438.
720. **A placebo that is pre-registered but not yet run does not protect anything -- run it BEFORE the headline, not after.** M104c had the flat-ROI placebo registered in their design table when they published -33.0% with a caveat. Running it cost **one command**, inverted the conclusion, and moved the number by ~8x. The caveat was not a footnote, it was the finding. **If a control is cheap enough to be worth registering, it is cheap enough to run before you report the thing it controls for.** Facts 1436, 1439.
721. **Before trusting any energy-in-a-band metric, measure the band on a region with NO signal in it.** The decisive datum was that the flat tile scored **1.69x higher** than the detail tile -- once seen, the metric's meaning is obvious and no further argument is needed. This generalises past sharpness: for any ratio metric, evaluate it where the numerator's subject is known absent and check that it reads small. If it does not, the metric is measuring something else. Fact 1439.
722. **To tell a broken instrument from an unusable subject, inject a synthetic signal at the real data's scale through the identical code path.** M104c's fitter accepted 0 of 103 real ROIs; the question "is my fitter broken?" was then settled in one command by pushing a synthetic sigma=1.2 edge, **at the real DN range**, through the same function -- it returned -0.4% against analytic. Without that probe the honest report is "no result"; with it the report is "the photograph cannot answer this", which is actionable and became a capture request. **A zero-accept rate is never self-explaining.** Fact 1440.
723. **"Machine built, no fuel" is a legitimate and reportable milestone outcome -- do not force a number out of a subject that cannot supply one.** Two independent milestones have now built validated slanted-edge instruments that no capture in the corpus can exercise. The wrong response is to quote the near-0 deg readings; they are aliasing artefacts 5-20x below optical possibility and would have entered the corpus as sharpness. The right response is what both did: state the instrument passes, state the subject fails, and name the capture that unblocks it. Facts 1440, 1442.
724. **Never gate on "nonzero" -- assert the exact expected exit code.** A red control that accepts any nonzero code accepts the corruption artifact itself on Windows PowerShell 5.1, where truncation yields `-1` (fact 1443). The habit that survives is `if ($code -ne 101) { throw "expected 101, got $code" }`. M108's freeze harness was saved by exactly this habit -- it records literal values (`EXIT=101`, `EXIT=0`) rather than a predicate -- **not by being immune**.
725. **When a subordinate corrects a rule you wrote, reproduce its measurement before adopting its replacement text -- and then check the replacement against the tree, because your own contrition can be wrong too.** I confirmed M108's four-host table independently and it held cell-for-cell. But my first draft of the correction wrote that rule 47 "used to send you to" PS 5.1; grepping AGENTS.md returned **0** occurrences of `powershell -File` or `-Command` as a recommendation. The old bullet merely *named* the edition while mislabelling the reading safe. **An overstated mea culpa is still a false statement in the corpus**, and it would have sent the next reader hunting a recommendation that was never there.
726. **When comparing two arms as images, a single shared stretch can render one arm unreadable -- stretch per arm and report the brightness difference as a NUMBER.** My first contact sheet used one shared percentile stretch for both arms, reasoning that a per-arm stretch would let a brightness difference masquerade as a structural one. On `lavendar` that choice rendered the control arm **pure black**, and the comparison it existed to make was impossible. The fix keeps the original concern satisfied without the blindness: stretch each arm to its own percentiles so both are legible, and print the luma-mean ratio (0.978 on `marker`) so the brightness question is answered explicitly instead of implicitly. Fact 1444.
727. **Look at the output before commissioning another metric for it.** This defect had been described by the owner in plain words, had survived one failed scoring attempt, and had no owner -- and it took one contact sheet and one 60-line probe to find, measure and localise, after many hours of metrology on quantities that change no pixel tonight. The corpus's measure-before-build discipline is right, but it does not license measuring things nobody is looking at while the visible defect goes uninstrumented. Fact 1444.
728. **A cache key must cover every input that can change the output bytes, or it silently invalidates every A/B running against it.** Fact 1446: an unrelated prior command changed a stack's output hash because `StackIdentity` omitted `reference` and `resampler`. The failure is invisible at the call site -- the command line is identical -- so no agent can detect it from its own transcript. **Treat an unkeyed input as a fleet-wide measurement defect, not a local bug**, and prioritise it above pixel work, because it taxes the credibility of every number produced while it stands.
729. **An agent blocked on a permission I control is idle capacity, and seven unanswered requests is my failure, not a queue.** M97 asked for the `merge.rs` lane **seven times** across a ten-hour run while the file sat uncontended, and filled the gap with metrology I had dispatched -- work it itself summarised as *"none of them will change a pixel tonight."* The lesson is not "grant everything": it is that **a request to enter a file is a scheduling decision only the orchestrator can make, so leaving it unanswered converts a working agent into a waiting one.** Ask every long-running agent what it is blocked on; M97's answer named a defect (fact 1446) that outranked everything else in flight.
730. **When a validator quotes its input, parse its output into records, not lines -- a wrapped quote puts a newline inside the message.** My control for the C1 fix (fact 1448) split the linter's output on `\n` and tested `"99998" in line`; the violation was present but its number sat on the record's second line, so the bar reported **FAIL on a fix that was correct**. That is a **false RED**, and its consequence class is worse than a false green in one specific way: **it argues for discarding a good change.** I nearly reverted the fix. Delimit records by the `path:line: [CODE]` prefix and join continuations. This is the same mechanism as the wrapped-prose search rule, relocated from source text to tool output, which is why the earlier rule did not protect me: I had filed it under "reading Markdown", and the instance arrived while reading stdout.
731. **Prefer a measured narrowing to a guessed one: survey the population a pattern matches before you tighten it.** The C1 fix had two plausible forms -- forbid blank lines, or require the citation to be on one line. The second is simpler and stricter and would have **destroyed 172 real citations**, all of them invisible in the green run because narrowing a check removes violations rather than adding them. The 10-minute survey (`c1_gap_survey.py`: 12 832 / 172 / 20) chose between them on evidence and simultaneously proved the false-positive class was 100% pure. **A tightening cannot be validated by the gate going green, because going green is what a too-tight gate does.**
732. **A feature is not shipped when it is measured and tested; it is shipped when the default render path calls it. Verify the call, do not assume it.** Facts 1449-1450: ~2 500 lines across three subsystems -- including the owner's own optical profile -- compiled clean, passed unit tests, and were folded as measured results while **no code in `stack` or `merge` referenced them**. `pub` suppresses `dead_code` in a lib crate, so the compiler cannot tell you. **Run `experiments/ORCH-drift-check/unwired.py` before claiming any capability exists**, and when accepting a milestone that adds one, require the report to name the call site in the default path or to state explicitly that it is deliberately opt-in and why.
733. **An inventory instrument needs a positive control as much as a measurement does -- otherwise "nothing is wired" and "my grep is broken" are the same output.** `unwired.py` was believable only because `flat_ratio` and `clip` came back **wired**, with real `use strehl_core::...` imports and live call sites, in the same run that reported `optics`, `photometric` and `robust` as orphans. **A tool that reports a problem everywhere is reporting itself.** The cheapest form of this control is to include, in the same run and by the same code path, an item you already know the answer for.
734. **When a verified patch's stated blocker is "file ownership", that is a scheduling failure by the orchestrator, and it must be escalated as one rather than re-measured.** Fact 1420 said it in as many words -- *"the largest single measured quality gain available to the shipping binary... already written and controlled... **the blocker is file ownership, not evidence** -- `align.rs` has been written by M86, M97 and M103 in the last twelve hours. **Sequencing it, rather than measuring it further, is the remaining work**"* -- and it still sat unlanded, because the one actor who can resolve a lane conflict is the one who assigns lanes. **A subordinate cannot unblock this by working harder; it can only keep measuring, which is what happened.** Treat the phrase "blocked on ownership" in any report as an interrupt addressed to the orchestrator personally, and answer it in that turn. Compare discipline 729: **seven unanswered requests for a `merge.rs` lane produced the same waste by the same mechanism, and I did not recognise the second instance from the first.** **CORRECTED by fact 1453: the second instance never happened.** M95 had already landed the variant in `843f6e1`; fact 1420 was stale and I did not check it. The general rule stands on discipline 729's instance, which is real and measured, but **the failure I actually committed here was not slow sequencing — it was acting on a perishable fact without re-verifying it (discipline 736), and then dispatching an agent to do work that was already in `HEAD`.** Left in place rather than deleted, because a discipline derived from an instance that did not occur is exactly the kind of error this corpus exists to make visible.
735. **Ask each long-running agent what it is blocked on, and read the answers against each other -- the composition is often invisible from every individual seat.** Fact 1452 exists only because three findings from three agents were held side by side: a kernel result that could not ship because of fringing, a chroma measurement showing the fringing was optical rather than kernel-made, and an inventory showing the optical correction was built and connected to nothing. **Each agent had one third and no way to see the other two.** The orchestrator's distinctive product is not more measurement; it is the join, and the join only happens if the parts are asked for and actually read.
736. **Before acting on a corpus fact that names a blocker, re-verify the blocker still exists.** Fact 1420's *"the blocker is file ownership"* was true when written and false when I acted on it (fact 1453): the author had cleared it in `843f6e1` and the corpus had not caught up. **This corpus is written concurrently by a dozen agents, so its claims about the state of the tree have a shelf life measured in hours, while its claims about optics and noise do not.** The check that would have caught it cost one command. **Facts decay at different rates by kind: a measured MTF is durable, a statement that a file is unwired or a patch unlanded is perishable** — and the perishable ones are exactly the ones that trigger dispatch decisions. Compare fact 1449's unwired-code inventory, which is the same perishable kind and should be re-run rather than cited once it is more than a few hours old.
737. **Never broadcast a diagnosis you have not run yourself.** I relayed a clippy attribution from a transient working tree and it told two agents that failures in their own files were someone else's (fact 1454). **A false all-clear is far more dangerous than a false alarm: the alarm gets investigated and dies, the all-clear is believed and compounds.** The orchestrator's word carries further than any subordinate's precisely because recipients cannot see the evidence, which raises rather than lowers the standard of proof required before speaking. When relaying is genuinely necessary, **attribute it explicitly as unverified relay** so the recipient knows what standard it was held to. Ask the fleet to contradict you; being contradicted is cheaper than being believed while wrong.
738. **A control that cannot go red is worse than no control, and controls can poison themselves.** M109's cache-visibility control forced a solve in one arm — **and that arm wrote its warpmap into the redirect directory**, so on re-run the supposedly cache-blind arm read back its own output, both arms took the sidecar path, and `A == B` became **vacuous while still printing green**. It was caught only because the harness carried an explicit **inertness guard** that printed `CONTROL INERT` and hard-failed. The general shape: **any control with a side effect on the state it controls for will converge to passing**, and passing is indistinguishable from working. Every control needs (a) a state reset per arm and (b) an assertion that the perturbation actually perturbed — M109 evidenced its perturbation from `strehl`'s own stderr, `align=solved` **111 s** against `align=sidecar` **63 s**. Compare disciplines 730 and 731: the same failure mode, reached by a different route, for the third time tonight.
739. **When your test set cannot falsify the more aggressive option, ship the conservative one and register the capture that would decide it.** M109's stricter trigger cleared far more magenta (**0.0944 % to 0.0260 %**) but touched **6.56 %** of the frame; it changed **0** strongly-coloured pixels on `marker` and **zero** pixels on `lavendar-cpl`, because *the corpus contains almost no saturated clipped colour*. **A test set that cannot express a risk will always report that risk as absent**, and the better-looking number is exactly when that bias is most tempting. The correct move is neither to ship on unfalsifiable evidence nor to abandon the variant, but to **name the missing capture and defer the decision to it** — recorded in `docs/captures-needed.md`. **Distinguish 'measured safe' from 'unmeasurable here' in the report itself**, or a later reader will read the absence of counter-evidence as evidence.
740. **A harness built to measure a patch must refuse to run when the patch is absent.** M109's `measure_stack.ps1` exits **2** with *"`merge_cmd.rs` does not contain the section 6 patch yet"* rather than measuring and reporting. Without that guard the harness runs happily against the **unpatched** path and reports the resulting null as a finding -- *"the fix made no difference"* -- which is indistinguishable from a real negative result and far more damaging, because it is the kind of negative that gets believed and closes a line of work. **The guard belongs in the harness, not in the operator's memory**, because the operator running it is often not the one who wrote it and is frequently running it hours later. Same family as discipline 738: an instrument that cannot detect its own inapplicability will report confidently on nothing.
741. **In a tree that other agents are editing, build both A/B arms from one tree at one moment, toggling only a file you own.** The intuitive "before" -- a binary built earlier and kept -- is **confounded**, because a rebuild for the "after" also picks up every other agent's edits in the interval. M109 measured the exact exposure: at its moment of measurement `optics.rs` was **+73** lines and `robust.rs` **+12** from other agents, so a stored-binary comparison would have attributed their work to its own patch. Its solution is the right general one: **one tree, one moment, one toggle, in a file you own** -- here flipping `color.rs`'s ceiling to `+inf`, which is the negative-control mechanism reused as an A/B arm. **This is the general form of M110's P10 finding that an archived render has a shelf life of minutes in a shared tree**; the shelf life applies to binaries and to every artefact derived from them, and concurrency is what creates it. Restore via `$env:TEMP` and never `git checkout -- <path>`.
742. **Parameterise an existing measurement script for a second arm; never copy it.** A duplicated script is **a second opportunity to choose a flattering ROI, threshold or crop**, and the divergence is invisible in the report because both arms cite "the same" method. M109 parameterised `montage.py` and then **proved the refactor byte-neutral** -- defaults reproduce `575045B5...` and `C38167BD...` exactly -- which is what makes the claim of sameness checkable rather than asserted. **A refactor of an instrument is itself a change requiring a null**, and PNG output through `cv2.imwrite` is run-to-run reproducible, so that null costs nothing to run.
743. **Before asking whether an effect is present, ask whether the population samples the covariate at all -- and report that support check first.** M109 registered this as a precondition and it converted two unanswerable questions into *stated* ones instead of two spurious numbers. **The distinction that matters is between "measured and absent" and "not measured", because they produce identical-looking output** and only the first is a result. Concretely: **a trend statistic needs a minimum populated-bin count as a hard precondition, not a nicety** -- a denominator filter can silently reduce it to the degenerate case where the correlation is ±1 by construction (fact 1457) -- and **the denominator profile must be printed before the gate**, so an UNDECIDABLE verdict ships with its evidence rather than as an assertion.
744. **When a bar disqualifies itself, leave the instrument untouched and register the next question separately.** M109's B10 failed its own controls; it left `radial.py` exactly as written, did not quote its readings (per the bar's own registered consequence), and opened B11 and B12 as new pre-registered bars rather than adjusting B10 until it passed. **Editing a failed instrument converts a reported failure into a silent repair**, and the repaired version carries the authority of the original registration without having earned it. The failed instrument is also evidence in its own right -- fact 1457 exists only because `radial.py` still demonstrates the degeneracy on demand.
745. **A null must be checked for being maximally DIFFERENT from the arm, not only for being nominally equal to it.** I prescribed a null in which an identity sidecar was resampled at `k = 1.0` against the arm's `k = 0.9974`. **On an identity sidecar `k = 1.0` is an exact no-op while `k = 0.9974` is a full non-integer resample**, so the two are as far apart as the experiment can make them: it fires at **+0.1851 dex** and would have voided a correct measurement as contaminated. M112 identified this **in advance**, registered the substitution, and used a null whose true value is **zero by construction**. The general trap: **a null designed by varying a parameter can accidentally straddle a discontinuity in what that parameter means** -- here, integer versus non-integer sampling -- so the parameter looks like a small change while the operation is a total one. **Prefer nulls whose expected value is zero by construction over nulls that are merely expected to be small.** Note the direction of the damage: this null fails *loudly*, condemning good work, where discipline 738's failed *silently*, blessing bad.
746. **Revising a pre-registered bar before data is legitimate; after data it is not -- and the difference is visible in git history.** I sent M112 a recalibration inviting it to re-register a more defensible bar. It arrived **after** Phase 0 had resolved, and M112 **refused**: it left `PRE-REGISTRATION.md` byte-unchanged at its original commit and answered on the merits instead, pointing out that the measured recovery was **negative** and that **no bar admits a wrong sign** -- not even the one my own decomposition implied. **An orchestrator offering to relax a bar is a pressure on the result whether or not it is intended as one**, and the correct response to it is the one M112 gave. Pre-registration only means anything if the file's history is the record and the author defends it against the person who commissioned the work.
747. **Assert physical bounds on a derived quantity; do not rely on the verdict computed from it.** A normalised field height above 1.0 passed under `SUPPORT ADEQUATE` (fact 1463), because a verdict is a function of its input and cannot detect that the input is impossible. **Every derived quantity with a known range -- a normalised radius in [0, 1], a correlation in [−1, 1], a fraction in [0, 1], an MTF in [0, 1] -- should be asserted against that range at the point of computation**, which costs one line and catches unit errors, resolution mismatches and axis confusions that no threshold can. Corollary, and it is the more valuable half: **when an unrelated control fails, re-read the output you already accepted.** That is the only routine event that makes an author revisit a result they have stopped questioning, and in this project it has now paid out repeatedly.
748. **For every control, name the concrete change that would make it fail. If you cannot name one, it has no power and must not be counted in a score.** Two of four controls in fact 1468 asserted properties the code guarantees three and six lines above the assertion; both passed, both were counted, and "4 of 4 passing" was doing real persuasive work. The rule is mechanical and costs one sentence per control. **Its sharper form: a control whose statistic is monotone in the artefact it guards against is worse than absent**, because it will actively rank the worst candidate first -- C4 preferred a 137 %-overshoot kernel. Check the *direction* of a discriminating statistic against the failure mode, not merely its ability to separate.
749. **A synthetic number and an end-to-end number are different quantities; never fold one and cite it as the other.** Fact 1466's +0.1343 dex was pure NumPy over one image and never invoked the binary; end-to-end through the shipped merge the same comparison is +0.083 to +0.099. Both are correct measurements of different things. **A folded result must carry the boundary it was measured inside** -- synthetic / in-crate / end-to-end -- exactly as fact 1460 requires a frame count and a `stack-digest`. The failure mode is identical in both cases and it is not arithmetic: a quantity is quoted in a decision whose scope is wider than the measurement's.
750. **When a hazard has a symmetric form and a one-sided form, the one-sided form is the dangerous one, because it has no tell.** I reasoned about cache contamination as two A/B arms colliding (fact 1446) and missed that a *single* measurement can silently inherit a setting from an unrelated earlier command (fact 1469). A collision between two arms at least produces two numbers that disagree; a lone contaminated measurement produces one confident number and nothing to compare it to. **Ask of any contamination hazard: what would it look like if it happened to exactly one measurement?** If the answer is "like a clean result", isolation is mandatory rather than prudent.
751. **A control must disable the proposed mechanism and leave everything else standing; if the statistic survives that, it is measuring a confounder.** M111's boundary-coincidence statistic read 1.686 with the election fully disabled, where it could not possibly have had a cause (fact 1472). **Coincidence is not attribution**, and the failure is invisible from the number alone -- 1.686 looks like a result. The constructive form is to build the comparison so causality is structural: difference two renders that differ *only* in the mechanism under test, as `D = luma(gate 4) - luma(gate 1e5)` does, and the confounder cancels by construction rather than by argument.
752. **Never derive a mask, ROI, threshold or denominator from the arm under test.** The blob statistic used the merged image's own p75 as its mask and read 1384; the same quantity under an independent third arm's mask read 115 (fact 1473). The region moved with the effect. This is one family with fact 1468's powerless C2 (the normaliser removed the defect the control existed to detect) and with scoring one demosaic against another's output: **whenever the instrument is built out of the thing being measured, the answer is partly guaranteed.** Masks must come from a third arm, a fixed geometry, or the raw input.
753. **Test the premise before the mechanism.** Premises are usually one query; mechanisms are usually a sweep. Hypothesis H1 in fact 1471 required regions below the noise ceiling for the regulariser to act on, and **0.00 %** of either ROI qualified -- a single median would have killed the hypothesis before any parameter was swept. The related orchestration error is worth naming separately: **I reached for the most recently interesting constant rather than the one with the right spatial scale.** Fact 84's regulariser was salient because it was priced at -35 %; the artefact's 54 px plateaus pointed at a 27x27 window in a file I had not opened. **Match the candidate to the scale of the symptom, not to its prominence in the record.**
754. **Verify a subordinate's claims about the tree against the tree at the moment you fold them, not at the moment they were reported.** Discipline 736 tells me to re-verify a named blocker before *acting*; this is the stricter obligation, because **folding launders a perishable measurement into a durable claim that everyone downstream will read as current**. Fact 1469 was measured honestly at `e924229` and was false at `HEAD` before I ever wrote it down. The check is cheap and mechanical: **any claim of the form "the code does X" gets one grep at fold time**, and any claim carrying a commit hash gets `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. This is now the third stale-tree incident tonight (facts 1453, 1460, 1476) and the only one caught before it did damage -- by accident, while planning something else. **Optical facts keep; tree facts rot, and the corpus does not distinguish them unless the author does.**
755. **A search that finds nothing and a search that ran nowhere are the same picture.** Before reporting a zero match as evidence of absence, prove the search had reach: `Test-Path` the target, or assert a non-zero hit count for a pattern known to be present in the same file. Prefer `git grep <pattern> HEAD -- <path>`, which fails loudly on a bad path and pins the revision, over `Select-String` with a relative path. ORCH gated a fleet-wide lane redistribution on a zero it never measured (fact 1477).
756. **Attribute an uncommitted edit by reading its diff, never by asking git who owns the file.** In a shared working tree `git status` has no author column and `git log -1` answers a question about the past. Both will name the wrong agent with total confidence at exactly the moment a file is changing hands, which is the moment attribution matters (fact 1478).
757. **When an agent reports that the site you sent it to was the wrong one, update every grant that depended on your model of that site.** ORCH told M107 the gather was in `warpmap.rs`, M107 found it in `align_cmd.rs`, and ORCH then granted `align_cmd.rs` to a second agent — because the grant was made against the instruction, not against the discovery (fact 1479).
758. **Prove a fix reaches the render by tracing the call chain to the CLI dispatch, not by grepping for the symbol.** Walk it in the direction that can fail: from the changed line outward to its callers, and stop only at the subcommand match arm the operator actually types. Count the callers at each hop — a function with zero callers is the failure this discipline exists to catch, and a function with several may reach the render on only one of them. This was the dominant failure mode of the 2026-08-24 build night: three diagnosed defects had finished, measured fixes, and the worst of them reached no render at all (facts 1481, 1482).
759. **A fix ported to a second code path inherits none of the first path's evidence.** Porting is cheap and usually harmless; the claim that travels with it is neither. Re-measure the defect on the destination path before asserting the port fixes anything there, and state which path each number came from every time it is quoted. ORCH took an `argmax-baseline` measurement and broadcast it to three agents as a property of `strehl stack` — the fourth instance of this error class in one night, and roughly an hour after folding discipline 758 against it (facts 1483, 1484). **AMENDED 2026-08-24 -- THE PRINCIPLE STANDS; THIS INSTANTIATION DOES NOT.** ORCH did **not** commit this error: the broadcast figures were `strehl stack` figures quoted as `strehl stack` figures, and argmax-only numbers stayed labelled argmax. The real error was different and is recorded as discipline **763**. Keep this discipline for the general rule, which remains sound; strike the example.
760. **An instrument that can only fail in one direction cannot audit a fix for overshoot.** Before a readout is used as the acceptance gate for a change, plant the defect in **both** signs and report the recovered magnitude for each, not a pass/fail; and report the statistic's headroom in each direction as a number. A quantity measured after its value has been pinned at full scale has no room left to express an excess (fact 1486).
761. **Never build corpus text in a PowerShell double-quoted here-string.** `@"..."@` treats backtick as an escape introducer, so every markdown inline-code span is a mutation site and the corruption is invisible in a renderer. Write the text to a file with a Python script, or use the single-quoted `@'...'@` form, which does not interpret escapes. When repairing, **restore the letter the escape ate** rather than deleting the byte — deletion silently shortens an identifier into a plausible-looking different one (fact 1488).
762. **A stale `$LASTEXITCODE` can read as either a false pass or a false failure, so a correct-looking code does not clear a truncated pipeline.** M87 attempted to refute the effect and its probe returned a correct `1` — because the *previous* command had also failed. Capture the code immediately after the process, on its own line, before any filtering; and when auditing past gates, re-run them rather than reasoning about which direction the error would have taken (fact 1490).
763. **When several instruments agree there is no effect, verify each one is *able* to see the effect's domain before treating the agreement as corroboration.** Concurring nulls feel like independent confirmation and are the most persuasive evidence available; two blind instruments agreeing is not evidence at all, it is manufactured confidence, and it is more dangerous than a single wrong number because it comes with a corroboration story attached. ORCH declared a shipped fix inert on three signals: a byte-freeze that renders a different pipeline by design (fact 1493), four subjects none of which exhibited the defect (fact 1494), and a mechanism invented afterwards to explain both (fact 1487, refuted). For each null, state the domain it samples and show the effect would have been in range.
764. **A test built to be insensitive to a change cannot later be cited as evidence the change did nothing.** The byte-freeze was specified to hold across this fix; when it held, that was the specification being met, not a measurement. Whenever a guarantee and an observation are the same artefact, the observation has no evidential content -- record which one you are invoking (fact 1493).
765. **A build that exits 0 has not been shown to have built anything.** `cargo check` on a warm cache, on an empty target set, or on a workspace whose members failed to resolve can all return 0 with no `error` line to grep. Before citing a green build, show it did work: artifact count in a cold `target/`, wall-clock, or a re-run whose sub-second `Finished` proves the previous run was the cold one. This is disciplines 763-764 applied to the compiler -- a green result is a claim about your instrument until the instrument is shown to have been running.
766. **Lane discipline manufactures unreachable code, and the orchestrator must count *reachable* fixes, not *specified* ones.** Forbidding two agents from one file is correct and prevents silent clobbering, but its consequence is that an agent diagnosing a defect owned by another lane can only deliver a **spec**. M111 produced a tested module and a line-numbered integration table for the waxy-blob defect and correctly stopped at `merge.rs`'s boundary; ORCH briefly recorded the defect as addressed because a commit existed. A commit is not a code path (cf. discipline 758). Track *specified* and *reachable* as separate columns, and treat a hand-off as an open defect until a second agent has applied it and proved the flag's null with a hash.
767. **When a correction is radial and its fit has empty outer annuli, stratify every headline statistic at the support boundary before believing it.** A whole-frame aggregate silently mixes the fitted zone with the extrapolated one, and for a defect that grows monotonically with radius the **top decile is dominated by precisely the extrapolated pixels** -- so the most impressive number in the report is the one least supported by data. M107's -54.08 % top-decile improvement on `bee-3-cpl` is a materially weaker claim if produced mostly past r = 0.788 than the same number produced inside the fit, and the two cases are indistinguishable in the aggregate. Cost of the split: one mask (facts 1499, 1501).
768. **Anchor an edit on a complete line, never on a sentence prefix.** A prefix-anchored replacement silently grafts the unmatched remainder of the line onto the end of the new text: **no error, no failed match, no lint violation**, and the result reads as plausible prose. M111 did it three times in one file -- twice grafting a bullet's tail onto a new bullet, once deleting four words -- and found all three only by reading the joined lines afterwards. Its repair commit showing **0 deletions** is what proved the fixes byte-exact. Same family as the rule against building `old_str` from truncated output, and it bites even when the text you can see is complete.
769. **A rate measured against the wrong denominator is not a weaker result, it is a different quantity.** M109's B15 predicted ~74.7 % and measured 21.02 % because it divided by all sampled frames while the merge averages ~55 focus-gated contributors. The temptation is to treat the gap as noise or as a partially confirmed hypothesis; it is neither, and the honest move -- which M109 made -- is to report the bar as failed, name the suspected denominator error, and **refuse to assert the corrected figure until it is measured** (fact 1503).
770. **When issuing a fleet-wide remediation order, measure its boundary before you send it.** ORCH told seven agents to re-run any gate built through a truncated pipeline. M113 spent two minutes on a positive control (reproducing the defect) plus a negative control on its own construct, and converted that into *re-run any gate that used `Select-Object -First`* -- provably excluding `Select-String` and `Out-String -Stream`, which the original order would have sent every agent to re-check for nothing. **An over-broad correction costs the fleet more than the defect did** (fact 1507).
771. **Scope a read-only constraint to the whole volume, not to named subtrees.** ORCH wrote '`D:\personal\macro` and `D:\macro-dark-frames` are STRICTLY READ-ONLY'. Agents obeyed it exactly and then wrote **16.9 GB** of scratch elsewhere on the same personal drive, which no one had forbidden and no one had intended to permit. A constraint enumerated as a list of protected paths grants everything not enumerated. State the permitted **write** location instead -- outputs go to `C:\dev\strehl-out\` -- because an allowlist cannot be under-enumerated in the dangerous direction (fact 1509).
772. **A null is not validation. A metric that always returns zero passes a null.** ORCH's first CA metric had a textbook null -- median change -0.06 %, worse in 46 % of windows, at the one radius where the effect is zero by construction -- and was nonetheless blind to the effect it was built to measure (fact 1516). A null shows the instrument is **quiet**; only a planted effect of known size shows it can **respond**. Register both, and register the positive control's pass bar before running it.
773. **Plant a geometric effect with an INTEGER shift.** A plant that resamples also blurs, so a metric with any sharpness sensitivity will answer about the blur rather than the geometry -- which is exactly how ORCH's bilinear CA plant produced a wrong-signed, non-monotonic response (fact 1516). An integer roll moves data without touching its spectrum. This is the same principle as registering paired crops by integer-only shifts, applied to the plant rather than to the measurement.
774. **Read an estimator's sign convention off its control; never assume it.** ORCH's phase-correlation estimator recovered `-planted` on first run. The magnitude was excellent (0.045 px) and every downstream number would have been perfectly precise and exactly backwards -- reporting a correction that works as a correction that causes the defect. A control that plants a **signed** quantity detects this; one that plants only a magnitude does not (fact 1511).
775. **Measure the physical quantity, not a proxy for it -- and disqualify any proxy that is non-zero where the quantity is zero by construction.** Lateral CA *is* a radial displacement between channels, measurable in pixels; scoring it by chroma residual correlation was a proxy that read -0.778 at the optical centre. That single number was sufficient to disqualify the metric and it was visible in the very first run, before any comparison was made (fact 1516).
776. **Separate a scalar gain error from a shape error by asking whether the error is flat in the independent variable.** ORCH assumed a radial-shape failure past the fit support; the gain measured 1.453 inside and 1.381 outside, which is flat, which means a coefficient is wrong rather than a model (fact 1513). The two diagnoses lead to entirely different work -- a new capture campaign versus a one-line rescale -- so the test is worth running before either is scheduled.
777. **Build the noise floor into the instrument from a component the physics forbids.** Lateral CA is radial, so the **tangential** displacement the same estimator returns is a direct, in-band, same-window measurement of the estimator's own error -- no separate null capture, no synthetic noise model, and it travels with every measurement automatically. Any radial number that fails to clear it is not signal, which is how fact 1515 refused a tempting blue-channel claim from the same table that supported the red one.
778. **Do not read a defect's magnitude off its apparent extent.** A fringe, a halo and a seam all have a width set by the local blur and an amplitude set by the underlying error; the eye reports width and the fix needs amplitude (fact 1518). The failure mode is not mis-seeing -- ORCH's 2-4 px observation was accurate -- it is the silent inference from extent to magnitude, which here would have been wrong by 25x. Measure the quantity the fix is parameterised in, in the units the fix is parameterised in.
779. **A strength-zero arm is not a placebo for a correction that resamples.** If the implementation short-circuits at zero strength -- which is good engineering and is provable here, since `zero` is byte-identical to `off` (fact 1517) -- then the zero arm omits the resampling too, and any improvement attributable to interpolation blur rather than to the correction itself remains **completely invisible to the arm set**. The placebo must preserve the operation and destroy only the hypothesis: apply the same magnitude in a direction the physics forbids (here, tangentially), so the blur is identical and the correction is nil.
780. **A table that mixes measured rows with inferred ones launders the inference into a measurement.** M113 labelled `-Last` as *not separately tested* in its report; ORCH folded it into fact 1507 as a row in a table of measurements, and the label did not survive the fold. Nothing was misquoted -- the provenance was simply carried by prose that the table format discarded. **Mark provenance per row, or measure the row before it joins the table.** The risk is highest exactly where the inference is reasonable, because then nothing looks wrong (facts 1507, 1520).
781. **An agent-ID-shaped substring in a path is not provenance.** `Recovered_113MSDCF` sat on the owner's drive during an audit for agent-created scratch, and reads unmistakably as M113's. It is a Sony DCIM folder predating the fleet by three and a half months (fact 1522). **Check the timestamp against the agent's lifetime before attributing anything to it** -- one cheap comparison, and the alternative is accusing an agent of violating a constraint it obeyed, or worse, deleting the owner's data because its name matched a pattern.
782. **Numerator and denominator must carry the same weights.** M109's B15 bar predicted ~74.7 % and measured 21.02 % because it counted over all sampled frames while the merge averages ~55 focus-gated contributors (facts 1502, 1503). The same error is now forbidden by construction in the shipped accumulator: the clip-state count uses **the identical `w_i` the value accumulator uses**. An unweighted count over a gate-weighted merge is not a noisier rate, it is **a different quantity** -- and inside shipped code that is far harder to notice than it was in a report.
783. **A producer exposes its sufficient statistics, never their ratio.** The merge accumulator returns `w_pinned` and `sum_w` separately rather than the fraction, because publishing the ratio silently moves the threshold policy from the consumer, which must defend it, into the producer, which cannot. The general form: **emit what was measured, not what a decision needs**, so that a later change of policy does not require a change of instrument.
784. **Prefer a known, bounded, directional bias over an epsilon's unknown one.** Facing an interpolation-induced under-count at edges, the tempting fix is a small tolerance on the saturation test. That converts a bias whose sign, cause and magnitude are all understood into one whose behaviour depends on an unjustified constant -- exactly the class Section 4.1 demolished. **Take the conservative test and write the limitation down** (fact 1525), so it can be measured later rather than discovered later.
785. **A spread of point estimates is not a confidence interval on their mean, and quoting one as the other manufactures agreement.** ORCH reported a CA gain range of 1.381-1.505 and concluded that sqrt(2) = 1.4142 was 'inside the measured spread'. The standard error of the mean was roughly **4x narrower**, and against it sqrt(2) is excluded (fact 1526). **The scatter of estimates answers 'how variable is a single ring', not 'where is the mean'** -- and it is the second question that a hypothesis about a single global constant is asking. Before declaring a round number compatible with data, state which of the two you computed.
786. **Weight binned statistics by their support before reading anything off the extremes, because the extreme bins are usually the least-supported ones.** In the CA gain table the highest (1.505) and lowest (1.381) rings carried 52 and 33 windows against up to 240 elsewhere -- **7.4 % of the data defining 100 % of the range**. Unweighted, they set the apparent uncertainty and rescued a hypothesis; weighted, they nearly vanish. This is the same failure mode as fact 1526 seen from the other side, and the general rule is: **the tails of a binned summary are where n is smallest, so they are exactly where a conclusion is least affordable.**
787. **A correction cannot be validated on the data it was fitted to; the residual nulls by construction.** ORCH came within one command of synthesising a 0.692-scaled correction from the *same* image pair the 1.444 gain was measured on, and reporting that it nulled the residual. It would have nulled exactly, it would have looked decisive, and it would have carried **zero** information -- the scale factor was defined as the thing that makes that residual vanish. **Any validation of a fitted correction must use data the fit has never seen.**
788. **Read a fitted artifact's provenance BEFORE interpreting any discrepancy against it.** ORCH measured a 44 % over-correction and concluded 'the coefficient is wrong' without checking which captures the coefficient was fitted from or under what conditions. The profile records both fields, and one of them is explicitly `None` **as information** (fact 1530). **The fitting conditions decide whether a discrepancy means a wrong number or a correctly-fitted number applied out of range** -- and those two diagnoses call for opposite code changes, one of which is a regression.
789. **Locate a discrepancy in the fit or in the application before shipping a corrective scalar, because a scalar that silently compensates an application bug will break the moment anyone fixes the bug.** A fitted fudge factor absorbs whatever is wrong upstream of it and leaves no trace of what that was. When the reported fit quality is inconsistent with the observed error (fact 1531), the application path is the first suspect, not the last.
790. **A render log that does not name its input is not reproducible.** M114's `r1.log` records the arm, the environment value, the exit code, the wall time and an output hash -- everything except **which stack was rendered**. ORCH could not recover it from the log, the filenames or the directory, and had to interrupt the agent to ask. The output hash pins *that* the run is reproducible without recording *what* it reproduces.
791. **Run the arithmetic before telling anyone it supports your hypothesis.** ORCH sent M107 a ranked list of convention bugs to hunt, headed 'check 1 first', on the strength of unrun mental arithmetic that a radius-convention error 'lands in this numeric neighbourhood'. Enumerated properly it lands in the **gap between** the two candidates (fact 1532). The cost of being wrong here is not the orchestrator's -- it is a subordinate spending hours hunting a bug in the wrong place, on authority.
792. **A statistical interval is not an exclusion when the systematics are unquantified and plausibly larger.** The same interval was used to exclude sqrt(2) (fact 1526) and then to exclude every convention ratio (fact 1532) -- but it describes ring-to-ring scatter, not instrument bias, and the instrument has three known unquantified biases (fact 1533). **State which errors an interval contains before using it to rule anything out**, and prefer a decisive cheap observation -- read the code, measure on the fitting data -- over a tighter version of an interval that was never measuring the right error in the first place.
793. **A test that cannot express a direction cannot fail on one.** M107b's L1 (zero correction is bitwise identity), L5 (green untouched) and L6 (exact composition) are all **sign-symmetric** -- every one holds identically for `+eps` and `-eps`. Three more tests **hardcoded the implementation's own expression** `1.0 / (1.0 + p.eps_r)`, and a test that restates the code cannot disagree with it. A seventh asserted against `displacement_at()`, **built from the same convention as the code under test**, so it agreed because it was derived from it. **Nine green tests, and not one had the power to catch a global sign inversion.**
794. **A mutation that stays inside the defect's own convention cannot reveal the defect.** The independent verifier's mutation testing changed `1/(1+eps)` to `1-eps` -- **both are the same wrong direction**, so the mutant died against tests that were themselves wrong, and the matrix reported health. Mutation testing measures whether tests detect *perturbations of the written code*; it says nothing about a convention error shared by the code and its tests. **Mutation coverage is not a substitute for one measurement in the output domain.**
795. **Verify a correction where its pixels land, not only where its coefficients are fitted.** M107b's sign inversion was caught in a **render-domain preview** after the unit suite was 9/9 green (fact 1536); ORCH's 1.444 scale discrepancy is visible only in the render domain and invisible to a fit reporting `r_squared = 0.9969` (fact 1535). **The same correction has now produced two distinct application-path defects that fit-domain evidence could not see.** Any geometric correction needs at least one end-to-end measurement of the quantity it claims to remove, taken on output pixels.
