796. **Check a report's citation count before assuming its findings are in the corpus.** `M107b-lateral-correction.md` is 82 KB, contains a shipped sign inversion, a registered bar reported as failed, and a refutation of a claim ORCH had put in the user-facing brief -- and had **zero** citations in `SYNTHESIS.md` for hours while ORCH re-derived part of it independently. **A written report is not a folded finding.** Sweep `docs/research/*.md` against the corpus periodically; the cost of the check is one command.
797. **A detector needs a TRAP it must not fire on, not only a plant it must fire on.** M97r's decisive arm is `defocus` -- the same scene at a different focus -- which a focus-stack robustness mask **must** ignore because that disagreement is the signal. The naive port passed every plant and fired on 100 % of the trap (fact 1541); the obvious fix made the trap ten times worse (fact 1542). **Neither failure is visible without an arm designed to stay silent.** A placebo shows the instrument is quiet on nothing; a trap shows it is quiet on something that looks exactly like the target and is not.
798. **When a nuisance effect is collinear with your signal, enter it as an explicit parameter and project it out; do not filter it and do not tune around it.** Filtering failed because it rescaled signal and noise together (fact 1542), and thresholding failed because a 0.027 px defocus bias is **10 sigma** significant when gradients are large. Adding the Laplacian as a third fitted parameter and taking the Schur complement made the statistic **structurally unable** to express the nuisance direction (fact 1544). **Blindness by construction survives a change of scene; blindness by threshold does not.**
799. **Debias any information matrix estimated from noisy measurements, and validate the debias against known ground truth rather than against plausibility.** `E[g2_meas] = g2_true + Var(g_noise)` inflated M97r's matrix by 48x on a low-contrast tile and shrank the estimate to half the null (fact 1545). The correction is credible **because it moved a planted 1.0 px translation to 1.0000 px**, not because it improved a score. A correction that merely improves a number is indistinguishable from a tuned one; a correction that lands on a known truth to four decimals is not.
800. **Verify the CALL SITE, never the test suite, when asking whether a capability is live.** `pub` suppresses `dead_code` in a lib crate, so 1365 lines and 24 green tests coexisted with zero callers (fact 1547) -- and this corpus folded its results as MEASURED while the render never ran it. The check is one command: `git grep <symbol> HEAD -- crates/` and read the hits that are **not** the module or its own harness. Do this before folding any milestone that claims a product effect.
801. **Before believing a multi-pass pipeline is invariant under a change, establish WHICH PASS computes the quantity you are measuring.** M97q's election map was immune to photometric gain for a **structural** reason (pass one runs before the gains exist) and not for the physical reason the design document asserted (fact 1549). Both explanations predict the same null. Only the line numbers distinguish them -- and the structural one is the stronger guarantee, so the distinction is worth the five minutes.
802. **A region-based estimator must be eroded, and the proof is a flux-conserving sweep whose true answer is exactly zero.** An un-eroded mask read **3.63 % where the truth was 0.0000 %**, 168x over its own bar, because blur transports light across the mask perimeter (fact 1551). Any statistic accumulated inside a boundary that the physics can cross is measuring the boundary. Erosion is the cheapest available control and its absence inflated a shipped headline number.
803. **Run a reachability audit over `pub mod` on a schedule, and treat unreachable line count as a first-class health metric of this project.** Discipline 800 says verify the call site for one capability; this is its standing form. The audit is one script and one minute (`experiments/ORCH-drift-check/reachability.py`), and its first run found 1638 lines of tested, measured, folded capability that the binary cannot reach (fact 1553) -- including the cure for a defect the corpus had already diagnosed and priced (fact 1554). **This project's characteristic failure is not building the wrong thing; it is building the right thing and not connecting it.**
804. **Price the STAGE before you price the ALGORITHM.** Fact 1189 measured the same defect at two intervention points and found a **16.7x** difference between them (100 % of offending pixels removed at the election, 6.0 % of the benefit recovered at the average). No amount of sophistication in the average-stage estimator closes that gap, because the wrong frame has already been elected. **When a fix underperforms its registered bar, ask whether it is aimed at the right stage before improving it** -- M89's mask failed at -5.21 % against a +10 % bar, and the stage, not the statistic, was the reason.
805. **To prove an instrument is connected, cross-check it against a quantity computed by a DIFFERENT code path, at TWO settings that give clearly different answers.** An 'export exists and looks plausible' check cannot distinguish a live probe from a constant, a stale buffer or an off-by-one field; agreement to ~3e-4 with an independently-computed scalar at **both** gate 4 (4.563) and gate 2 (2.829) can (fact 1558). This is the direct antidote to the dead-code failure of fact 1547: **one agreement is a coincidence budget, two that differ is a measurement.**
806. **Report a guard that never fired as UNEXERCISED, never as PASS.** Two milestones reached this independently on the same night (fact 1560). A guard reported PASS on the strength of never having been reached is the disconnected-probe error in its purest form -- the same error that made a bar and its own plant both read exactly 0 px and nearly shipped as a headline null (fact 1548). **The honest status of an unfired guard is 'live path, no real-data evidence'.**
807. **A cache key must cover every input that can change the cached artefact, and the only honest test is adversarial poisoning: run the identical command after different histories and compare hashes.** Keying on the capture path alone let one bracket's two configurations share an entry and produced two different renders from one command line (fact 1561). A knob added an hour before was already poisoning it (fact 1563). **Every new tuning knob is a cache-key change until proven otherwise** -- bind it to the key in the same commit that adds it, and when running measurement arms, give each arm a private cache path.
808. **Derive a bar's premise from the SOURCE, never from a binary's `--help` -- the binary may be stale.** M97n's C4 failed for exactly this reason (fact 1565). The companion rule is the response: **when a pre-registered bar fails, first ask whether the prediction was wrong**, and if it was, report the bar as failed and correct the premise in the open. Silently restating the bar to match the observed behaviour destroys the entire value of pre-registration.
809. **Before measuring a cross-channel quantity, enumerate every cross-channel operator between the sensor and the file.** A colour matrix and a guided demosaic are both cross-channel, both were present, and both were in a file whose own `--help` says *'For looking at, NOT for measuring'* (fact 1568). The general form: **a measurement space is part of the instrument.** Establish that the quantity survives the space before trusting any number taken in it -- and read the tool's own warnings, which in this case were correct and ignored.
810. **When a pipeline applies a known compile-time constant, that constant is a free end-to-end calibration of the measurement chain -- use it to test the instrument before trusting the instrument's other numbers.** `applied / eps_r` separated three measurement spaces that no internal consistency check could distinguish, and revealed two contaminations of **+31 % and -30 %** (fact 1569). Look for such a constant in any pipeline you are about to measure; if one exists, running it is nearly free and it is the difference between an instrument and a hope.
811. **An estimator that returns a surprising number is not necessarily broken -- re-run it in a clean space before indicting it.** ORCH's estimator was accused of being 'blind to 94 % of the field'; unmodified, in the uncontaminated space, it agreed with an independent method to **0.4 %** (fact 1572). A whitening step that weights all frequencies equally will **maximally amplify a zero-lag contaminant**, so the very design choice that made it look broken is what made it a sensitive detector of the contamination.
812. **Rank your own weaknesses, publish the ranking, and expect it to be inverted.** ORCH listed five weaknesses and named the first as most likely real; the verifier **refuted that one at 0.0004 px and confirmed the fourth** (fact 1574). The ranking was still worth publishing -- it directed the verifier's effort and it is what made the inversion legible. **Author-supplied uncertainty is useful precisely because it is checkable, not because it is accurate.**
813. **A dead-code audit that excludes a symbol's own file measures a visibility smell, not reachability -- and the two differ by 15x here.** Local helpers are called by their siblings; excluding the file hides exactly those calls, so every locally-used helper reports as dead (fact 1578). Both quantities are worth knowing, but they are different questions with different remedies: unreachable code should be **wired or deleted**, over-`pub` code should be **narrowed**. State which one the instrument computes, and check a handful of its hits by hand before believing the total.
814. **Audit DEFAULTS, not just reachability -- reachable-but-off is the same defect as unreachable, and a dead-code audit cannot see it.** `halo.rs` is called, compiles, is tested, and returns immediately because its gate reads `Err(_) => false` (facts 1579-1580). Every static tool the language provides was satisfied. The audit that finds this is a different one: enumerate every gate on the product path and print its **default**, then diff that list against the wins the corpus claims. **A measured win behind a default-off flag has not shipped**, and the corpus should not describe it as though it has.
815. **Ask which way your control's residual bias points -- a control biased toward your hypothesis is worse than no control, because it converts a confound into a confirmation.** The tangential placebo under-blurs on oriented content (fact 1584), so *'the artifact vanished in the placebo arm'* was partly guaranteed by construction and would have been read as *'the treatment earned it'*. **The disqualifying property is that the bias is uncontrolled, not that it is large**: the same control is fine at 0.28 % on isotropic content and fatal at 93.41 % on hairs, and nothing in the design tells you which regime you are in.
816. **Prefer a negative-dose arm to a null arm: it holds the nuisance exactly constant and yields a monotone ladder instead of a single contrast.** Running the treatment at negative strength matched interpolation blur to **1.11e-16** where a direction change failed by up to 93 % (facts 1584-1585). A null arm answers *'is the effect there?'*; a dose ladder answers *'does the effect scale with the treatment?'*, which is much harder for a confound to imitate. **And check that your null arm actually executes the nuisance** -- a zero-strength path that short-circuits omits it (fact 1586).
817. **The dispersion of k sub-estimates is not the standard error of their mean, and sub-estimates from one capture sharing one estimator are not k independent draws.** ORCH read a range as an interval and a mechanism hunt was dispatched on it (fact 1582). Two habits follow: **state which interval you are quoting**, and when the sub-estimates are correlated, note that the honest interval is **wider** -- then check which of your conclusions that direction weakens (fact 1583). Correlation always degrades an **exclusion** and always leaves a **compatibility** finding intact, so the asymmetry is knowable without computing the correlation.
818. **Score the compound claim, not the component that is easy to count.** *Overshoot* means a sign flip **and** a magnitude increase; counting flips alone conflated a working correction with a broken one and reported **62.9 %** where the real rate was **9-19 %** (facts 1587-1588). The general trap: a statistic that captures **one** of the conjuncts will fire on the benign case, and it fires *hardest* exactly when the treatment works best, because a correction that lands near zero flips the most signs. **Before believing a bar, ask what a perfect treatment would score on it** -- here, a perfect correction scores near-total failure.
819. **Every component of a detection rule must be a quantity the mechanism actually changes -- a plausible-looking one that does not discriminate licenses a false clear.** ORCH's rule paired byte-identity, which discriminates perfectly, with runtime, which does not: a live correction arm ran **faster** than its own control (fact 1590). This is the same error shape as clearing an exit-code gate because the code looked right (fact 1508). **Ask of each clause: what values does it take under the defect, and under its absence?** If those overlap, the clause is not evidence and belongs out of the rule rather than in it as reassurance.
820. **A plugin system needs the data AND the dispatch that selects it; shipping the data alone leaves the capability un-defaultable and silently misapplicable.** strehl has a measured optical profile and no way to recognise the gear it describes (facts 1592-1593), so its best-measured correction must stay off and can be pointed at the wrong glass by hand. **When a profile is keyed to physical hardware, the identification of that hardware is part of the plugin, not a convenience on top of it** -- and until it exists, every claim of the form 'the tool corrects X' is really 'the tool corrects X if the operator knows to ask'.
821. **Read the source section, not the headline -- and read the report's own conclusion before promoting its number.** ORCH twice directed the fleet on the halo correction using a figure that the report qualifies as an unshipped pipeline (fact 1596), from a section *titled* with the opposite recommendation (fact 1597). Nothing was hidden; ORCH did not look. **A headline is written to be quotable and a conclusion is written to be acted on**, and when a corpus grows past the point where any one reader holds it, quoting the first without checking the second becomes the default failure rather than an unusual one.
822. **Prove that every arm of a multi-arm check fires, individually, or you do not know which arm produced your green.** M111's guard reported 7/7 caught with half of itself inert, because the cheap arm short-circuited ahead of the expensive one (fact 1602). **An arm that never fires is indistinguishable from one that cannot.** The commissioning test is per-arm, not per-suite: plant a defect that **only** arm N can see, and require arm N to be the one that reports it.
823. **Before commissioning an experiment, search the corpus for whether it has already been run.** ORCH designed a blur control for the halo correction that M87 had already built, matched **1000x more precisely** than ORCH specified, and **pre-registered against its own author's expectation** before measuring the opposite (fact 1595). The cost was two misdirected messages and nearly a wasted measurement campaign. **In a corpus this size the prior-art search is cheaper than the experiment**, and the search that matters is for the *question*, not for the milestone that happened to ask it.
824. **Look at the output.** This project ran 119 milestones, wrote 156 research reports and recorded 1602 facts before its orchestrator viewed a single rendered pixel, and ten minutes of looking **reordered the defect priority list** (facts 1603, 1607). The largest visible defect had no milestone, no fact and no name in the corpus, because every instrument the project built was pointed at a defect somebody had already thought of. **A metric can only answer the question it encodes; an image answers questions nobody asked.** Looking is not a substitute for measurement -- fact 1603 is labelled OBSERVED for that reason -- but it is how you find out which measurement is worth making.
825. **Withdrawing a cure is not withdrawing the diagnosis, and the corpus must say which one it means.** ORCH withdrew the halo correction on strong evidence (facts 1596-1601) and the next reader could reasonably have concluded the halo was not a real problem. It is a severe one (fact 1607), and the project now has **no** fix for it (fact 1606). **A negative result about a treatment is silent about the disease**, and in a corpus where facts are read out of order by agents who were not there, the two have to be stated as separate rows or the refutation will be mistaken for a dismissal.
826. **Before citing a passing suite as reassurance about a specific hazard, check that the suite's coverage intersects the hazard.** strehl's 449-test byte-freeze registry is green and covers **none** of the cache-poisoning path (fact 1613). Quoting it in that context would have been literally true and materially misleading, which is the most dangerous shape a claim can take because nothing in the output flags it. **A test result reports its verdict but never its scope**, so the scope has to be supplied by the person citing it -- and the citation is worthless without it.
827. **Date a defect from when its read path first existed, not from when the bug was written -- and if it caches, treat exposure as cumulative rather than per-run.** Fact 1562 put the cache-poisoning window at 48 hours by dating it from the write; the read path did not exist for most of that, and the true window is **10 h 26 m** (fact 1609). The two errors pull opposite ways and both matter: dating from the write **inflates** the blast radius and wastes an audit, while ignoring persistence **deflates** it, because a file-backed cache lets a single bad invocation contaminate runs made long after the fix shipped (fact 1611).
828. **Assert the dtype and range you expect on the line after you load, because a reader that silently narrows your data is worse than one that fails.** PIL returns `uint8` for a 16-bit RGB TIFF and says nothing (fact 1615); the failure arrives as a **plausible number**, not an error, and nothing downstream can recover it. The hazard generalises past this library: **any loader that has a lossy fallback will take it silently**, and the cost of the guard is one line while the cost of its absence is every measurement built on top. Prefer a loader that raises over one that copes.
829. **When your comparison has a set of possible references, use the one that argues against you.** ORCH measured the merge against the **quietest** of five input frames -- the choice that most flatters the finding -- and only after switching to the **noisiest** was the result worth reporting (fact 1620). This is the fourth instance tonight of the same error shape and it is worth naming precisely: **the bias is not in the metric, it is in the selection of the reference**, so no amount of validating the metric can catch it. The check is to ask, before running, which choice of reference would make the answer come out the way you expect -- and then not make that choice.
830. **An arm's name is not its semantics: look up what a harness arm IS before you build a conclusion on it.** ORCH measured `armM-gate0-binlin` for an entire session believing it was the shipped merge; `merge.rs:3341` calls gate 0 a **negative control** and `merge.rs:299` sets the shipped default to 4.0 (fact 1621). The measurement was correct, the instrument was commissioned, the conservative reference was chosen -- and the conclusion was still about the wrong thing, because **no amount of rigour downstream of a mis-identified input can recover it**. One grep for the arm name would have cost thirty seconds. Make identifying the arm part of loading it, not part of writing it up. **ORCH's citation in this entry was itself wrong** -- it read line **3027** for the negative control and line **298** for the default gate; the lines are **3341** and **299**, corrected by M121 and re-verified against the source. An entry about looking a thing up before building on it cited the wrong line while saying so; the *claim*, checked again, holds.
831. **A detector must be run on an instance that CANNOT contain the defect, and if it fires there the counting statistic is dead.** ORCH's patchwork detector fired on 3 of 12 windows of an unmerged photograph with a worst case *higher* than the merge's (fact 1627). The nulls it had passed were synthetic -- iid noise and a smooth ramp -- and synthetic nulls only prove the metric is quiet on things nobody was going to measure. **The null that matters is a real instance of the population you are scoring, minus the mechanism under test**: here, a real photograph of a real defocused background, with real noise, that simply never went through a merge.
832. **Before comparing two images, state what is held constant between them; if the answer is 'nothing', it is not a comparison.** ORCH put a render of one subject against a frame of a different subject and read a 390x ratio off it (fact 1629). Two images of different scenes differ for any reason at all, and no amount of rigour in the metric recovers that. This is the same failure shape as discipline 830 -- **six of ORCH's errors tonight were in what was being compared, none in how it was measured** (fact 1632) -- so make identifying the controlled variable a written step, not an assumption.
833. **Say 'sufficient' when you have shown sufficiency, and do not let it drift into 'the cause'.** Fact 1635 shows level drift is large enough to account for about half the merge's spatial swing. That is a real and useful result -- a mechanism too small to produce the artifact is dead on arrival, and this one is not -- but **it is one-directional**. The test that converts sufficiency into attribution is removing the mechanism and re-measuring the artifact, and until someone runs it the honest word is 'candidate'. The corpus has a bad history here: fact 1580 promoted a correction on a headline number, and facts 1595-1602 took it back.
834. **A promotion bar is defined on an axis, and it silently rejects wins on every other axis.** M116 built a careful campaign, pre-registered a threshold, ran 12 arm-subject pairs, and correctly reported that none cleared it (fact 1639). The same files, scored with a statistic shaped like the defect actually complained of, contain a 29% effect and an obvious visual one (facts 1637, 1638). **Nothing was done wrong** -- and that is the point, because no amount of rigour inside the bar detects that the bar points elsewhere. **Before accepting a null, state what the metric would have to be blind to for the null to be false, and check.**
835. **When an effect is real but confined to one subject, report the covariate before reporting the average.** The cross-subject median for photometric is 1.013, which reads as 'no effect' and is how a summary row would have recorded it. The per-window table shows the effect tracks background smoothness within `tweezers-cpl` and that `bee-3-cpl` starts below the floor the fix converges to (fact 1637). **The median destroyed the finding; the covariate explained it.** Aggregate last.
836. **A defect statistic ranks only the candidates that already passed the control; ranking first and controlling afterwards promotes the blur.** The arm with the best number on every subject was disqualified by a window it was never supposed to change (facts 1641, 1643). The general form: **any metric that rewards removing something can be maximised by removing everything**, so it must be paired with a region where removal is forbidden, and that pairing must gate the ranking rather than annotate it.
837. **Anchor a fold on a unique full line, inside the section you mean, and walk to the end of the wrapped entry.** Two folds in one session inserted into the wrong place: `fold138` matched question 138 in an early part of the list rather than its end, and `fold139` matched **discipline** 202 in section 5 instead of **question** 202 in section 10 -- then split that discipline's bold span, because section-5 entries wrap onto indented continuation lines and the anchor was only the first of them. Both were caught by `corpus_lint`, which is the reason to run it after every fold rather than after a batch. `fold140` carries `insert_after_entry(number, section_pattern, block)`, which confines the search to one section and walks past continuations; use it.
838. **Take the worst subject, not the median: a candidate that blurs anywhere is not rescued by scoring well elsewhere.** All three soft-gate variants pass their texture control on `tweezers-cpl` and post the best removal numbers measured, and all three are blurs -- only `bee-3-cpl` shows it, and `foam` is silent (fact 1645). Discipline 835 said aggregate last; this is the sharper form. **A subject on which a defect does not appear is not evidence that the defect is absent, and averaging it in actively conceals the one subject that saw it.** `switch_gate.py` therefore reports OVERALL REJECT when any single subject rejects, and never reports a cross-subject mean of the two axes.
839. **Commission a ranking instrument by making it reject a known-BAD candidate, not merely detect a known-good effect.** Every plant used here until now proved sensitivity -- can the statistic see the thing we hope it sees. None proved specificity -- can it decline the thing we hope it declines. The gap is exactly where tonight's near-miss lived: the old instrument's controls all passed, and it still ranked a blur first. **Feed the instrument a candidate that is nothing but the failure mode, and require it to be rejected before any real verdict is printed** (fact 1646). An instrument that has never rejected anything is not known to be able to.
840. **Triage a silently-narrowing reader by the shape of the statistic, not only by the dtype of the input.** The question `was my input 16-bit RGB?` is necessary and not sufficient: two statistics computed from the same pixels in the same script diverged by 8.7% against 0.0% (fact 1649). The sharper question is **`does my statistic divide a small quantity by a large one?`** -- if so it compresses toward 1 under quantisation and fails toward a clean null (fact 1648). Two practical riders from the same audit: **grep for `Image.open(` call sites, not for `PIL`**, because a case-insensitive search false-positives on `compiling`; and when asked whether you are exposed, **re-run both readers rather than reasoning from having avoided the API** -- `I did not use PIL` is exactly the class of argument the hazard notice warns against.
841. **Report sharpness as SNR at matched contrast, never as contrast.** Any operator that multiplies high frequencies raises a contrast metric, so a contrast-shaped number cannot distinguish sharpening from information gain and cannot be falsified. Measured: a gain-invariance control moved `R_SNR` by <=0.54% while a naive gradient metric moved **8.25x** on the same arms (fact 1654). **If a candidate's headline can be manufactured by a post-filter, it is not a measurement of the candidate.**
842. **Two independent milestones hit the same failure on the same night: a scoring rule that rewards removing or adding structure, with no term forbidding it.** M115 reported its registered decision rule defective because `R_SNR` alone **rewards blur**, so a `MEAN` arm scored highest; ORCH's background statistic ranked a soft gate first for the same reason (facts 1641-1645). **This is not a coincidence of two careless authors -- it is the default shape of a single-axis quality metric**, and it is why disciplines 836 and 839 are structural requirements rather than advice. Every scoring rule in this project must name, in advance, the thing it would reward that nobody wants.
843. **Triage a narrowed reader by asking whether the statistic is a ratio of two arms on the same data or an absolute quantity.** Measured: ratio-of-arms moved **-1.0%** under a planted narrowing, while absolute noise power moved **3.5x** and band SNR fell to **0.438x** of truth (fact 1655). Combined with fact 1649's small-over-large compression, this gives a two-question triage that needs no re-run: **is it absolute (suspect), and does it divide a small quantity by a large one (suspect)?** Note also that damage scales with the **occupied** range, so a low-contrast ROI can be left with single-digit levels where the full-range figure suggests 256.
844. **A new instrument must pass a replicate control before any of its readings are admitted -- run the replicate before the bar, not after.** M113 withdrew its own post-hoc bar S8 because the instrument's bee-triplet repeatability is **116 ppm** against a **145 ppm** effect, so its clean `spread survives` verdict was inside its own noise. It had run the bar first and the replicate second. **The order is not cosmetic: a bar run before a replicate cannot be interpreted even if it passes**, and the temptation to keep the result is strongest exactly then.
845. **When a pipeline test fails, suspect the test, and look for a subject where the confound is absent by construction rather than corrected for.** M113's first alignment answer -- 64% of the effect attributable to the pipeline -- was an artefact of defocused windows diluting a global fit. It was not fixed by a better estimator but by choosing a **flat** subject, on which the merge is a measured **4.8 ppm no-op** (fact 1659). **A confound removed by the choice of subject needs no model and cannot be mis-specified**; a confound removed by a correction term is only as good as the term.
846. **A triage list distributed to a fleet needs its own negative control, because a false positive costs more than a miss.** ORCH generated the PIL exposure list with a grep and broadcast it without reading a single entry. A missed leaf script leaves one number wrong; **a false positive on a *shared* reader invites several agents to replace working, validated code and to re-run correct work** (fact 1661). The specific error was greping for the API call rather than for what happens to its return value: `Image.open` for TIFF **tags** is safe, `np.asarray(Image.open(p))` on the **pixels** is not. Commission the list before broadcasting it.
847. **When one effect admits several numbers, the honest headline is the one whose qualifier fits in the sentence -- and quoting the largest without it is a misdescription even when every number is correctly measured.** ORCH's CA headline was the largest of five (fact 1662); ORCH's halo headline was likewise the most flattering member of a family (fact 1596). **Twice in one night, and both times an auditing agent caught it rather than the author.** The rule: **state the denominator in the same breath as the number**, or quote the plainest member of the family. `-29.4 % of edge chroma` needs no qualifier; `-61.0 % of edge-localised chroma excess against a 5 px baseline` cannot survive without one, and will be repeated without it.
848. **A recommendation with no author is a recommendation nobody checked -- scan for its source before shipping it.** V-CA's `v4_absence_check.py` did a whitespace-collapsed sentence scan of every document in the corpus and found that **not one author recommended enabling the CA correction by default; two recommended against, and so did the code and ORCH's own fact 1593** (fact 1663). The recommendation had accreted in the orchestrator's summarising rather than arriving from any measurement. **The check is mechanical and should precede any default change**: grep the corpus for a sentence that actually recommends the thing, and if the only source is the summary, there is no source.
849. **THE ORCHESTRATOR'S FOLD IS AN UNAUDITED TRANSFORMATION, AND ON THE NIGHT IT WAS FIRST AUDITED, EVERY ERROR IN IT RAN THE SAME WAY.** The corpus verifies milestones. It has never verified **the step that turns a milestone's report into a fact**, and that step is performed by the one participant nobody checks. Audited on 2026-08-24/25, six ORCH errors surfaced in a single night: a **synthetic plant's** number folded as *the real occluding scene* (fact 1598); two experiments **spliced**, M86's worst-case half-pixel shift borrowed into M87's warp (fact 1595); a mechanism its own author **explicitly labelled ARGUED** folded as MEASURED (fact 1599); a **700 x 1100 ROI window** folded as *the shipped frame* (fact 1601); **the largest of five numbers** for one effect quoted without the qualifier that gives it meaning (fact 1662); and a default-on recommendation that, on a scan of every document in the corpus, **had no author at all** and had accreted purely in ORCH's summarising (fact 1663). **Not one of the six ran toward weakening a claim. All six ran toward strengthening it.** That is a bias, not a scatter, and its mechanism is plain: summarising drops qualifiers, and a qualifier is almost always what makes a finding smaller. **Consequences.** Fold from the milestone's own primary artefacts rather than from its prose wherever a number is load-bearing; carry the author's own epistemic label (MEASURED / ARGUED) across unchanged, because downgrading it is a finding and upgrading it is a fabrication; name the scene, the space and the window in the same sentence as the number; and **treat the fold as a workstream that requires an independent verifier exactly like any other**, because the rule that an author must not verify their own work has no exemption for the person writing it down.
850. **BEFORE COMMISSIONING, SEARCH `docs/research/` FOR THE QUESTION AND NAME THE PRIOR REPORTS IN THE BRIEF -- ORCH BROKE THIS AND IT COST A WHOLE MILESTONE.** Rule 40 already required it. ORCH's M123 brief named **no** prior report; **four existed** (M28, M60, M89, M97r) and **three had already used real captures**. Worse, ORCH handed the agent M89's 4.78 % figure as *a measured prior to reproduce* **without saying it was M89's** -- passing along a number from the very milestone that had written *the mask, as specified, should not ship*. The agent found all four in twenty minutes and declined to re-ask the closed question. **The check is mechanical and takes minutes; skipping it spends an entire agent re-deriving a known no.** Corollary: **search the source too** -- `outlier.rs` carried a regression test whose *name* was the answer.
851. **A MODULE HEADER IS DOCUMENTATION THAT DRIFTS FROM THE CODE BENEATH IT, AND IT IS WHAT EVERY READER AND EVERY DISPATCHER HITS FIRST.** `outlier.rs`'s header describes **two** discriminators where its enum, forty lines below, documents **four** and marks one of them a measured failure (fact 1668). ORCH read the header, briefed from it, and commissioned an agent to test an arm the file itself already recorded as dead. **The nearer documentation is to the top of a file, the more load it bears and the less often it is re-read when the code changes.** When a header and an enum disagree, the enum is the code and the header is a claim about it -- and the claim is the one that was never tested.
852. **BEFORE A METRIC IS ALLOWED TO JUSTIFY A DEFAULT, ASK WHAT IT READS WITH NO DATA IN IT.** M118 derived a closed form from `align.rs`'s filter weights alone and predicted its own headline to within **12 %** of the effect, **with no photograph involved** (fact 1670). A metric that can be computed from the algorithm's coefficients is measuring **the algorithm's datasheet**, not the images -- and it will rank kernels in the order their frequency responses predict no matter what the subject is, which is why `nearest` tops it. **The test is cheap and general: compute the metric analytically, or on a blank/random field, and subtract. What remains is the part that is about the photographs.** Same family as fact 1444's circular mask and M115's scene-free SNR of 84.9: **an instrument that cannot tell you it has no data will happily report a result.**
853. **WHEN A CHANGE IS BLOCKED ON A MISSING FLAG, LAND THE FLAG BEFORE THE CHANGE, AND HAND OVER THE DIFF RATHER THAN APPLYING IT ACROSS AN OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY.** M118 measured a real by-eye improvement and still **declined to promote it**, because the cost is **2.91x-3.92x** and there is no way for an operator to say no (fact 1674). It then wrote the enabling `align_cmd.rs` diff and **handed it to the milestone that owns that file instead of applying it**, in a tree where several agents edit concurrently. **A quality change that cannot be declined is not a default, it is a tax**; and a correct patch applied across an ownership boundary is still a clobber.
854. **A confirmed mechanism and a shippable fix are two different verdicts, and conflating them is how a correlation gets promoted into a default.** M122 established the blotch's cause at **rho = +0.70, p = 0.0035**, with the confound refuted and the code's own fitted gain corroborating it -- and still returned **KEEP-OFF**, because one pre-registered no-harm criterion failed on two stacks. *Why does this defect happen* is answered by a correlation; *should this correction be on for everyone* is answered by the worst stack, not the average one. **Report both, and never let the strength of the first argue for the second.**
855. **When a confound is registered in advance, report the partial correlation even when the raw one already passes -- and read its direction.** M122's partial came back **+0.7550 against a raw +0.7011**: the confound was *suppressing* the effect, not creating it. That is information a bare 'confound refuted' would have destroyed, and it is only available because the worry was written down before the numbers existed. **A confound that shrinks the effect and a confound that hides it look identical until you compute the partial.**
856. **In a two-arm image comparison, choose the scored pixels from the symmetric mean of both arms, so neither arm selects the region it is judged on.** M122 pooled windows on `(A0+A1)/2`; the variant that selected per arm produced a different verdict on `tweezers-cpl`. Selecting on one arm lets the metric find that arm's quietest pixels, which is a search for a favourable ROI dressed as a measurement -- the same family as fact 1601's 700x1100 window and discipline 849's systematic sign.
857. **Turn an aesthetic complaint into a proof by deriving what the estimator is *incapable* of producing, then showing the output exceeds it.** M120 did not argue that the patchwork looks wrong; it computed that **any spatially constant convex weighting is bounded above by Q = 1.284** and measured the shipped render at **4.337**. That converts *I do not like this background* into *no fixed set of frame weights can have produced this background*, which cannot be answered by taste, and which localises the cause to the spatial variation of the weights. **Where a bound is derivable from the estimator's own form, derive it -- it is worth more than another ratio.**
858. **A refuted `ARGUED` fact is the labelling system working; do not file it with the folding errors.** Fact 1604 was wrong in two limbs and was folded as `ARGUED` with 'Unverified' written into its own text, so it misled nobody and cost one milestone's dispatch. Discipline 849's subject is different and narrower: findings folded **stronger than the source supports** -- a synthetic plant folded as a real scene, `ARGUED` folded as `MEASURED`, a qualifier dropped. **Counting honest refuted hypotheses as orchestrator errors inflates the error rate in the pessimistic direction, which is the same bias with the sign flipped, and it would make the one discipline that measures my reliability useless.**
859. **When a reader may have narrowed your data, the number that predicts the damage is the occupied range of the LOCAL WINDOW your statistic integrates over -- not the file's, and not the ROI's.** M103's ROI kept 93 of 11 542 levels, which reads as survivable; the 5x5 windows its denominator actually came from held **1.26 levels against a quantisation step of 1.0**. Compute the ratio *your smallest integration window's spread : the quantisation step*. Below about 10 the statistic is measuring the truncation.
860. **A quantisation floor compresses ANY ratio of unequal quantities toward 1, whichever way up it is written.** Small-over-large fails toward a clean null; large-over-small understates the effect (M103: 3.7324 published against 4.8411 true). **So 'my statistic is a ratio, so it cancels' is only true when the two terms are comparable in size** -- a two-arm ratio on the same data is protected (-1.2% measured against a -1.0% plant), a ratio across scales is not. Ask which two numbers are being divided before claiming cancellation.
861. **A hardware-keyed profile must ship its identification alongside its data, and the identifier must denote the composed system, not the lens.** M119's `a7c2-fe100gm-2xtc-x4cpl` is four claims in a string, of which the file evidences two and one (`a7c2`) appears nowhere in any field. **An identifier that cannot be checked against the file is a label, and a label that looks like a key invites the software to assert what it cannot verify.**
862. **A gear-match predicate must be three-valued, and `unknown` must be un-collapsible at the type level.** Matching wrongly applies a correction measured on other glass; failing to match silently declines a correction the user asked for. Both are bad and they are different, so `bool` is the wrong return type. This is the same class as `STREHL_FIX_CA`'s silent no-op under `STREHL_ALIGN=0` -- **byte-identical output with no warning is `unknown` collapsed into `no`.**
863. **Derive a vendor's obfuscation as a formula with a test, not as a copied table.** Five lines of `const fn` with a stated derivation is licence-clean where a transcribed lookup table is not, and -- the part that matters for correctness -- **a formula is falsifiable**: it can be shown wrong on a new body, whereas a table can only be found to be missing a row. M119 flagged its own single-body verification as `ARGUED` because of exactly this.
864. **A single-band sharpness statistic cannot adjudicate selection against estimation, because it rewards retained noise.** V-M116's `D` ranked `--gate 0` patchwork above the gate-4 merge on all three subjects. **Score the flat band and the detail band separately and report both**; `Q = D - N` reversed the ranking on one subject and confirmed it on another. Any future 'sharper' claim in this project must carry its flat-band number beside it or it is not a claim about picture quality.
865. **A non-default configuration must appear in the sentence that travels, not only in the section that explains.** M116 disclosed `STREHL_ALIGN=0` in its section 7 and in the claim body, and still shipped a headline saying 'the default merge'. **Headlines are what get folded, quoted and told to the owner** -- an accurate body does not repair an inaccurate headline, because the two travel separately. Put the flag in the noun phrase.
866. **Report the dispersion of any pooled contrast, and state what fraction of the field carries it.** V-M116 found per-tile sd of **1.5x to 1.9x the headline**, and that the bee headline was carried by **25.8% of tiles**. A pooled mean with a robust sign reads as a uniform improvement and can be a minority effect with a confident sign -- the two are indistinguishable without the spread. Both were true here, on the same number.
867. **Before reading a null, count how many members of the class could have expressed the effect.** M121's bright-object row read a flat +0.0009 and superficially refuted its own prediction; only **5 of those 18 edges straddle a depth discontinuity**, and under *every* mechanism on the table a same-depth edge shows nothing. **A class that cannot express the prediction is not evidence against it, it is a sample that cannot address it** -- and it will look exactly like a refutation.
868. **Require a claimed localised feature to END.** M121's most exciting reading (+0.1326, n=96, 100% positive) died because its profile was still +0.0884 at 18-24 px, while the genuine rim went negative by 12 px. A gradient, a vignette and a lighting falloff all produce large, consistently-signed, high-n readings near an edge. **The discriminator is not amplitude or significance, it is spatial support** -- measure the profile out to several times the expected width and require it to return to zero.
869. **Third triage question for a narrowed reader, after 'is my statistic absolute' and 'does it divide small by large': is anything about WHERE I measure decided from the narrowed pixels?** M121 measured the same class twice through the same defect: **+0.4% with the band pinned, -31% under free re-detection**. A milestone that scored at fixed coordinates is far less exposed than one that found its own features, *with an identical statistic*. Amplitude did not predict which classes moved; re-detection did.
870. **Index maps are pixels, and their failure mode is worse than quantisation.** A narrowed intensity image gives you a wrong *value*; a narrowed index map gives you the **wrong frame** -- `bee-3-cpl`'s 299 frames wrap silently in uint8. Assert `uint16` on index maps, and read them **nearest-neighbour only**: interpolating an index map invents frames nobody elected.
871. **To triage a statistic against a narrowed reader, ask whether it reads pixel *value* or feature *position* -- not whether it is absolute or a ratio.** Location statistics (displacements, centroids, peak positions) dither and average out; dispersion statistics (noise power, sd, SNR, band energy) absorb the quantisation variance directly. This **replaces** ORCH's absolute/ratio rule, which false-positived on a location estimator and would have caused correct work to be re-run.
872. **Immunity claims must carry the level count at which they expire.** M113's location estimator is immune down to roughly **12 distinct levels per fitted window** and then fails hard -- **-43% at 4 levels, sign inverted at 2** -- while still returning confident, plausible numbers. An unqualified 'location statistics are safe' is a licence to trust the regime where it is most wrong. **State the boundary or do not state the immunity.**
873. **Watch for a control whose sampling saturates: a count that stops changing while its parameter keeps moving means the control is testing nothing, and it will report a clean negative.** M113's floor sweep admitted the whole 693-window grid at every setting and printed 'NOT CONFIRMED'. **Log the sample count of every control at every level and require it to vary** -- this is the same class as a plant the harness cannot express, and it is cheaper to detect.
874. **Ask about the ratio of the *terms*, not the form of the expression.** 'It is a ratio, so quantisation cancels' is true only when the two terms are comparable: measured shift rises monotonically from **0.68%** at `D` < 1.25 to **8.04%** at `D` >= 8. Report `D` = max/min of the terms alongside any cancellation claim. **A defect-detection contrast is a strong term over a weak one by construction**, so it is never in the protected regime, however it is written.
875. **When a pre-registered gate fails, register your explanation of the failure as the next gate before acting on it.** M111's account of why run 1 failed was itself wrong -- the heavy tail was real but innocent, and the true cause was the gate's own bin boundary. Switching statistic at that point would have produced the right answer for a reason that was false, and nothing would have caught it. **A failed gate tells you *that* it failed, not *why*, and the why is what you carry into the next design.**
876. **Check exposure at both ends: what your scripts read, and what produced the files they read.** M111 is the only milestone that audited its *inputs'* provenance rather than only its own call sites, and confirmed the baseline independently by counting levels in the control file (**49 028**). A clean reader on a file that was already narrowed upstream is still a narrowed measurement.


877. **AUDIT THE FOLD BY RE-DERIVATION, NEVER BY RE-READING LABELS.** MEASURED against ARGUED is the wrong axis: fact 1722 measured **zero** mislabelled rows among 8 defects. The errors live in the **scope of the sentence** -- one window presented as six, a control presented as a null, a tolerance borrowed from the experiment next door. All four are invisible to a reader who trusts the label and only visible to one who reopens the artefact. Budget the expensive check: **25 facts re-derived beats 105 skimmed**, and V-FOLD chose exactly that trade deliberately.
878. **WHEN A CORPUS FACT QUOTES A DERIVED CONSTANT, THE SHIPPED CODE'S OWN DOC COMMENT IS THE CHECK.** Fact 1568's matrix was wrong for six files' worth of propagation while `color.rs:221` documented the correct green row **from 4 h 26 m before the wrong value was folded** (fact 1725). The cross-check cost ORCH **one `view` call and one script run**, and the script's output matched the doc comment to 3 d.p. If a fact quotes a matrix, a coefficient or a threshold that the code also computes, **read the code's own statement of it before folding** -- and if the two disagree, the code wins until proven otherwise.
879. **A SCRIPT THAT PRINTS A DISAGREEMENT AND IS NEVER FOLDED IS WORSE THAN ONE THAT WAS NEVER RUN**, because it creates a false record of having checked. `ca_matrix_prereg.py` (fact 1725) is the case. A pre-registration whose output is not read back into the corpus has performed the ceremony of falsification without its substance.
880. **BEFORE QUOTING A TOLERANCE, CONFIRM THE EXPERIMENT THAT PRODUCED IT.** `+/-X ppm` reads like a property of the finding and is in fact a property of **one run** (fact 1723). The splice was undetectable by reading the sentence, and trivially detectable by grepping the cited report for the number -- which is exactly what `fold_check.py` rule 31b does, and rule 31b **postdates** the defect. Extend it: a tolerance must be found in the cited report, not merely somewhere in the corpus.
881. **PROVE BYTE-INERTNESS AGAINST A FIXTURE COMMITTED BEFORE THE WORK, NOT AGAINST YOUR OWN BEFORE/AFTER.** M124's default hash `119936E6...D709` was already in `byte-freezes.tsv` as `coffee-bean-20-gate2-sidecar` (fact 1726). A self-comparison proves only that the agent did not change its mind mid-run; matching a **pre-existing committed hash** proves the output is where the corpus says it should be. When a fixture for your surface already exists, quoting it costs nothing and upgrades the claim's class.
882. **A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS WORSE THAN A MISSING CHECK, BECAUSE IT REPORTS AS COVERAGE.** Fact 1728 is the model disposition: M124 worked out that every admissible freeze mode was one in which its flag provably could not act, and **declined to add the row**, stating the structural reason. Compare fact 1725, where a script that printed a real disagreement was never folded and created a false record of having checked. **Both failures are about the gap between performing a check and the check meaning something** -- one adds ceremony, the other discards substance.
883. **WHEN THE SAME MAPPING EXISTS TWICE, THE BUG IS NOT IN EITHER COPY.** `lanczos2` was unreachable because a name table lived in two places and drifted (fact 1727). The repair that ends with **one** mapping is worth crossing a crate boundary for; the repair that ends with two or three is not a repair. Add the test that the duplication defeated -- here, that every listed name resolves to a **distinct** variant.
884. **A TIMING TAKEN ON A SHARED HOST IS A BOUND; LABEL IT AS ONE AND REPORT THE READING THAT DOES NOT FIT.** M124's bilinear cost ran outside the prior milestone's range and it published the disagreement unresolved (fact 1729). The temptation is to quote the half that agrees. **An unreconciled out-of-range reading is information; a silently dropped one is a defect that will be rediscovered later at higher cost.**
885. **THE SYNTACTIC SHAPE OF A STATISTIC PREDICTS NOTHING ABOUT ITS EXPOSURE. THIS IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT REFUTATION AND THE RULE IS WITHDRAWN ENTIRELY.** ORCH broadcast a two-question triage -- *is it absolute?* and *does it divide small by large?* -- to the whole fleet. It has now been refuted on three separate axes by three milestones that did not consult each other: **V-M113** (what matters is whether the statistic reads pixel VALUE or feature POSITION -- location statistics dither, dispersion statistics absorb); **M111** (protection depends on the **term disparity** `D`, and a defect-detection contrast is a strong term over a weak one *by construction*, so the rule false-cleared exactly the statistics the fleet was writing); and **M115** (fact 1732 -- a common floor drives a power ratio to the **signal-power ratio**, which can be a sign reversal with *widened* spread). **Do not triage by the form of the expression. Derive what the perturbation does to your specific estimator, or measure it with a dose-response control.**
886. **A SHARED DEGRADATION IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN AN INDEPENDENT ONE, BECAUSE IT SURVIVES THE CANCELLATION YOU ARE RELYING ON.** The intuition that a two-arm ratio on the same data is self-protecting assumes the degradation is common **and cancels**. Fact 1732 shows a common floor does not cancel out of a power ratio -- it cancels out of the *signal* factor and concentrates in the *noise* factor, which is the one carrying the answer. **When you argue cancellation, expand the expression algebraically and see which factor the perturbation actually lands in** (this is the same medicine as the `|B-Y|` control that carried an explicit `R` term).
887. **BEFORE TRUSTING A NOISE ESTIMATOR, ASK WHETHER YOUR CONTAMINANT IS CORRELATED ACROSS THE SAMPLES IT DIFFERENCES.** Fact 1733 is the general case: split-half, frame-difference and paired estimators all measure noise **as the part that differs between samples**, so any contaminant that is *deterministic in the signal* is invisible to them and is booked as signal. Quantisation is the instance the fleet met; fixed-pattern noise, dust, hot pixels and a stuck warp are others. **Injecting equal-power random dither is NOT a valid model of quantisation** -- measured, the two differ 16x in the quantity being estimated.
888. **A POSITIVE CONTROL MUST BE MONOTONE-DOSED, NOT BINARY.** M115 tested a claimed law by sweeping the dose across **six** levels plus the analytic asymptote (fact 1732), which is why it could report the *shape* -- monotone approach to a sign reversal -- rather than merely `effect / no effect`. A single-dose control cannot distinguish `no effect` from `an effect my estimator saturates on`, and it cannot recover a law. **When you are testing a proposed general rule rather than a single hypothesis, the control has to have an axis.**
889. **A FLEET BROADCAST IS A WRITE TO EVERY AGENT'S CRITICAL PATH; PRICE IT THAT WAY.** Fact 1739 measures the bill: six broadcasts, hours of a top agent's time, and the agent could not opt out because auditing rather than asserting immunity is exactly what it had been told to do. **Address broadcasts explicitly, exempt agents that have filed, and batch corrections.** And note the multiplier -- a broadcast that is *wrong* costs the fleet the audit AND the rework, so the bar for sending one must be higher than the bar for believing one.
890. **`CHEAPER TO DO` AND `JUSTIFIED TO DO` ARE DIFFERENT GATES, AND A REPORT SHOULD SAY WHICH ONE IT MOVED.** M124 lowered the cost of changing the resampler default (a flag now exists, the default is pinned to a committed fixture) and correctly said only that. M85 then withdrew the evidence that a change would help (fact 1736). **A decision record that tracks only feasibility will read `G3 met` and go.** When you retract a measurement that supports a pending decision, name the decision document in the retraction -- the retraction is the thing that must travel, and it does not travel by itself.
891. **A PLACEBO THAT CONTAINS NO SUBJECT AT ALL IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THIS CONTROL.** M85 killed its own headline by scoring a **dark frame** -- no photograph in it -- through the identical channel and reading essentially the same gain (1.0006 against the claimed effect). No argument about scene content, ROI choice or tuning survives that. **When a metric's band may be noise-dominated, run the metric on data with no signal in it before you run it on a rival method.**
892. **PROSE ABOUT CODE IS THE ONLY ARTEFACT IN THIS PROJECT WITH NO STALENESS CHECK, AND IT IS THE ARTEFACT THE OWNER READS.** Fact 1740: a correct sentence about which modules were reachable decayed into a false one within hours of being written, and every automated gate stayed green because none of them reads prose. Facts get folded, code gets tested, numbers get `fold_check`ed; **a claim of the form `X is not wired up` has no owner and no expiry.** Treat every code-state assertion in an owner-facing document as perishable: re-derive it from `crates/` before each delivery, and prefer claims that are dated (`as of <commit>`) over claims that are timeless, because a dated claim that goes stale is still true and an undated one is simply wrong.
893. **`BUILT AND MEASURED` IS NOT `ON`, AND THE GAP IS INVISIBLE FROM EVERY GREEN SIGNAL THE PROJECT PRODUCES.** Fact 1741: five measured improvements sit behind unset environment variables, so the test suite, the byte-freezes and the milestone reports were all truthfully green about a render that contains none of them. **A default is a decision, and an unset `env::var` is a decision nobody wrote down.** Any project that gates work behind flags must audit the resolved default set as its own deliverable -- and must distinguish a gate that is *structurally inert* (no-op unless a second gate is on) from one that is *measurably useless*, because the two produce the identical number and mean opposite things. Only reading the code separates them.
894. **PREFER AN INVARIANT WITH A PROVEN BOUND OVER A TUNED THRESHOLD, AND COMMISSION IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** INV-PATCHWORK (fact 1742) is worth more than any measured number in M120's report because `Q <= 1.284` is a **theorem about constant weights**, not a level someone chose: a violation is a proof that the weighting varies spatially, and it cannot be argued down. It is also commissioned **both** ways -- a placebo that must pass (0.3085) and a plant that must fail (6.694) -- so a green means the instrument is quiet AND awake. **When a quantity admits an analytic bound under the null you care about, build the check on the bound; you get sensitivity, a failure direction and interpretability for free.**
895. **`SURVIVES AVERAGING` IS A DIAGNOSTIC, NOT AN ANOMALY: IT SEPARATES BIAS FROM NOISE AND SHOULD BE THE FIRST QUESTION ASKED OF ANY PERSISTENT ARTEFACT.** Fact 1743's artefact is visible after averaging **166.8 frames per pixel**, which alone refutes every noise-driven explanation without any further measurement -- 167-fold averaging would have removed it. ORCH's fact 1604 had proposed exactly such an explanation (a flat response giving a random argmax) and it was refuted at **15.0x** the noise ceiling. **Before theorising about a persistent structure, ask what `n_eff` it survived; the answer usually deletes half the candidate mechanisms for free.**
896. **WHEN YOU BROADCAST A HAZARD, STATE ITS DIRECTION AS A HYPOTHESIS AND ASK TO BE CORRECTED -- BECAUSE THE DIRECTION IS THE PART YOU ARE MOST LIKELY TO GET WRONG.** Fact 1746: ORCH broadcast the PIL hazard fleet-wide as a false-null risk, and the first agent to *measure* it found the opposite sign on band-pass statistics. The existence of the hazard was right; the sign was wrong; and a fleet acting on the sign would have dismissed inflated alarms as safe. **A hazard notice carries two claims -- that the mechanism exists, and what it does to your number -- and only the first is usually established when the notice goes out. Label the second ARGUED and invite the measurement.**
897. **TRANSCRIBE THE OPERATION, NOT THE CONSTANT -- IT IS FREE AND IT IS IMMUNE TO THE CORPUS GOING STALE.** M109 survived the colour-matrix error (fact 1749) for one reason: its script recomputes the matrix by the crate's own algorithm instead of copying the number the corpus quoted. Five other files copied the number and all five were wrong. **A copied constant is a snapshot with no link back to its source; a transcribed operation re-derives itself every run and fails loudly if the source changes.** Where a value is computed by shipped code, compute it the same way rather than quoting it, and say in the docstring which function you are mirroring.
898. **A FIX WHOSE NO-OP CASE IS THE IDENTITY *BY CONSTRUCTION* NEEDS NO REGRESSION ARGUMENT, AND THAT IS WORTH DESIGNING FOR DELIBERATELY.** Fact 1748: `clip_highlights` takes an early return on every unpinned pixel, so `never worse` is a property of the control flow rather than a claim requiring a measured null on every stack. Contrast the switchable improvements, none of which can make that claim and all of which therefore need an audit before promotion. **When designing a correction, prefer the form that is exactly inert outside its trigger condition** -- it converts an open-ended empirical burden into a one-line reading of the code, and it is the reason this fix could ship ungated while better-measured ones could not.
899. **A CORRECTION NOTICE SHOULD STATE WHICH DESIGN DECISIONS IT STRENGTHENS, NOT ONLY WHICH NUMBERS IT INVALIDATES.** ORCH broadcast the matrix correction as a list of contaminated files and numbers to re-run. M109 replied with the consequence ORCH had missed: because the green-to-red coefficient is **negative** and green is the suppressed channel, the corrected leak makes the defect **2.6x stronger**, which is an argument *for* the fix's placement (fact 1749). **A correction changes the weight of evidence in both directions; a notice that only lists damage invites every recipient to check for damage and nobody to check for support.** Ask explicitly: does this make any existing decision better justified?
900. **A TRAP BEATS A NULL, BECAUSE A NULL CAN ONLY FAIL TO FIND AN EFFECT WHILE A TRAP CAN CONVICT.** Fact 1752: M97e's gate was *null-proven* and still wrong. A null asks `does it do nothing where nothing should happen?`; a **trap** asks `does it do something where doing anything is definitionally an error?` -- and only the second can distinguish a statistic aimed at the right quantity from one aimed at a correlated wrong quantity. Here the trap is a **stationary** stack in which a frame legitimately disagrees because it is the only frame resolving that pixel, so any firing is a false positive by construction. **Register the trap before you build, name what firing on it would prove, and accept that a gate can pass every null you own and still be aimed at the wrong thing.**
901. **IN A SHARED WORKING TREE, PAIR AN IN-PROCESS INSTRUMENT WITH A CROSS-PROCESS ONE AND REQUIRE THEM TO AGREE.** Fact 1751. The two are blind to different confounds -- the in-process counter cannot see between-run drift because it never leaves the process, and the cross-process image diff sees the shipped artefact including every dependency that moved. **Agreement between them is a positive measurement that nothing drifted**, which is stronger than any hash-based drift check and far stronger than an assertion that the tree was quiet. This is the cheap alternative when pinning a private copy of the dependency tree is impractical: not one instrument plus vigilance, but two instruments whose failure modes do not overlap.
902. **`LANDED BEHIND A FLAG` IS A COMPLETE AND HONOURABLE OUTCOME; SAY SO IN THE HEADER.** M97e's status line reads `LANDED BEHIND A FLAG, DEFAULT OFF, AND THE FLAG SHOULD STAY OFF` -- the build succeeded, the measurement refused it, and both facts are in the first line a reader sees. **A milestone that ships working code it then recommends against is not a failed milestone**, and a report that buries that recommendation under the engineering is how an unjustified default gets promoted later by someone reading only the summary. Lead with the recommendation, not the deliverable.
903. **BEFORE TRUSTING A CLEARANCE, ASK WHAT THE CHECK WOULD HAVE READ HAD THE DEFECT BEEN PRESENT.** Fact 1754: a census that reads a header field can only ever clear an axis the header records. M117's sidecar header had no smoothing field, so its smoothing clearance was structurally incapable of failing -- and this happened *inside* the audit commissioned to find exactly that class of blindness. **The test is not `did it pass` but `could it have failed`**, and the repair is to re-clear against an artefact that carries the perturbed quantity by construction: whole-file identity over coefficients, not agreement over summaries. This is the same medicine as commissioning a checker with planted defects, applied to a check that was never commissioned at all.
904. **A PRESENCE TEST CANNOT AUDIT A CORPUS THAT DOCUMENTS ITS NEGATIVES.** Fact 1755. Rule 47 makes reports declare unset variables, so searching for a variable name finds the proofs of absence alongside the instances of use; a `PIL` grep finds `compiling`, hazard warnings, and probes written to demonstrate the hazard. **Four distinct false-positive classes were observed in one night, and every one reads as a hit.** Any hazard sweep must therefore (a) resolve what happens to the matched token -- is it used, declared unused, warned about, or demonstrated? -- and (b) **report its false-positive count alongside its hit count**, because a sweep whose precision is unstated cannot be acted on.
905. **A VERIFIER THAT REPORTS A DEFECT IN ITS OWN INSTRUMENT IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE THAT REPORTS A CLEAN CORPUS.** M117 delivered an all-clear (fact 1753) and led instead with X19, a flaw in its own method, then volunteered the residual gap its strongest null cannot close (fact 1756). It also chased `the number that does not fit` -- a sharper claim it liked, that refusals would make CA apply partially -- and reported it **empty**, because M97o measured zero refused frames corpus-wide; recorded as dormant rather than live. **Grade a verification by how hard it tried to invalidate itself, not by the verdict it returned**, and treat a verifier that never finds a defect in its own instrument as unaudited rather than as lucky.
906. **TRIAGE A STATISTIC BY THE QUANTITY IT LOCATES, NOT BY THE TYPE IT RETURNS.** Fact 1757: ORCH's own replacement rule -- position immune, value fragile -- graded strehl's merge election immune, and the election is an argmax over **gradient energy**, a quantity the same rule calls destroyed. An argmax inherits the fragility of the field it searches. **Every triage rule ORCH has issued has been refuted by the next milestone that planted the perturbation instead of consulting the rule** (three times now: absolute-vs-ratio, small-over-large, position-vs-value). The standing instruction is therefore not a better rule but the absence of one: **expand the estimator algebraically, or plant a dose-response control, and never classify by shape.**
907. **PUBLISH THE DISPERSION OF THE TERMS ALONGSIDE ANY STABILITY FIGURE, OR EXPECT THE CENTRE TO BE READ AS A BOUND.** Fact 1761. A band-mean of -1.0 % over bins spanning -5.62 % to +10.93 % is an honest average and a misleading protection claim, and ORCH turned it into a fleet-wide rule within hours. Fact 1759 is the same failure in a different costume: a bias of +0.014 frames beside a MAD of 0.622. **A single-number stability result is only actionable with its spread attached**, and the author is better placed to attach it than the reader is to ask.
908. **REPLICATION EARNS THE RIGHT TO STATE SCOPE LIMITS, AND THE LIMITS ARE THE VALUABLE PART.** Fact 1760: M115 confirmed M111's `D` law and, in the same breath, showed it disagrees by **8.5x** on magnitude within a shared bin and has **zero support** in the two most alarming bins. A replication reported as `confirmed` alone would have hardened a ranking heuristic into a lookup table. **A confirming milestone should be asked what its confirmation does NOT cover**, and that answer folded with the same weight as the agreement.
909. **CHECK WHETHER A SUSPECTED BIAS POINTS TOWARD OR AWAY FROM YOUR CONCLUSION BEFORE SPENDING A DAY BOUNDING ITS MAGNITUDE.** Fact 1762: M112 was genuinely exposed, and the exposure was harmless because it pushes toward `ship` while M112 concluded `no-go`. **A bias aligned against your verdict is a strengthening, not a threat**, and establishing the *direction* is usually one cheap dose-response ladder where bounding the *size* is a campaign. State the direction explicitly in the clearance, because a reader who sees only `exposed but small` cannot tell a lucky escape from a structural one.
910. **ALGEBRAIC EXPANSION IS NOT ENOUGH IF THE PERTURBATION LANDS IN A WEIGHT.** Fact 1763. ORCH's replacement guidance -- expand the estimator and see which factor the perturbation enters -- was followed correctly and still produced the wrong sign, because substituting a scalar for a transfer function silently assumes **the perturbation shares the signal's spectral shape**, and quantisation is the case where that assumption is worst. Any statistic that is a **mean over a band, an average over windows, or a weighted combination** hides a weighting the scalar form does not show. **Expand it, then ask what the perturbation's spectrum is relative to the signal's** -- and if you cannot answer that, the dose-response ladder is not optional.
911. **AUDIT THE PROVENANCE OF SHARED HELPERS, NOT ONLY YOUR OWN CALL SITES.** Fact 1764: a tile-ranking helper used across milestones embeds a differencing dispersion statistic, so a milestone whose published statistic is provably immune can still inherit the defect through **which data it selected**. M111 reached the same place from the other direction by auditing the provenance of its *inputs* rather than its code. **The hazard surface of a measurement includes every library it calls and every file it reads**, and both are outside the region a self-audit naturally inspects.
912. **A CORRECT PREDICTION LICENSES THE ORDERING, NOT THE MECHANISM -- STATE WHICH ONE YOU TESTED.** Fact 1766: M105b's registered direction was right and its registered *reason* was wrong, and only checking the reason separately revealed it. **A pre-registration that binds only the outcome will certify a false mechanism as confirmed**, and that mechanism then propagates as though it had been measured. Register the expected *reason* alongside the expected result, and when the result lands, ask explicitly whether the mechanism it landed by is the one you named.
913. **DO NOT QUOTE A RATIO WITHOUT ASKING WHAT ITS DENOMINATOR IS MADE OF.** Fact 1768: a **336x** under-report was set by float32 representation, because its null arm measured **0.2 ulp** -- the denominator was an absence, not a quantity. The check is arithmetic and takes seconds: **express the denominator in ulps of its own dtype**, and if it is order-unity, the ratio is reporting your number format. The same sweep's identical answers at two doses came from a **grid collision** (`21/63` and `5/15` are both exactly 1/3), which a second subject exposed -- **so a repeated value across doses is a coincidence to rule out, not a plateau to report.**
914. **A GATE BUILT TO HONOUR A DISCIPLINE CAN INVERT IT, SO COMMISSION THE GATE ON THE FAILURE IT EXISTS TO CATCH.** Fact 1767: a citation checker's first run reported **TOOL** for a real **SUBJECT** failure, because `ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` promotes a subprocess's stderr into a terminating error -- turning a successful detection into an apparent malfunction of the detector. **Every checker must be run once against a planted instance of its target failure and required to name that failure correctly**, not merely to be non-green. And the defect that prompted it is worth its own note: **six of seven cited hashes were right, and the wrong one was the most recent** -- recency feels like verification and is not.
915. **WHEN A GATE'S RESPONSE TO A PLANTED EFFECT IS SMALLER THAN ITS RESPONSE TO NOTHING, STOP TUNING AND KILL IT.** Fact 1770: **24.51 %** at zero planted displacement against **34.57 %** at six times the detection bar is not a threshold that needs adjusting -- it is a statistic that is mostly reading something other than displacement. **The diagnostic is the zero-dose arm, and it is cheap:** run the positive control at dose zero *first*, and if it fires substantially, no amount of ladder above it can rescue the instrument. Every earlier attempt on this direction tuned the bar; the zero-dose arm is what ended it.
916. **ASK WHETHER A DETECTOR'S FAILURE MODE IS CORRELATED OR ANTI-CORRELATED WITH ITS TARGET.** Fact 1771: both displacement gates abstained hardest on the stack with the most motion, because large motion destroys the correspondence they measure. **An anti-correlated failure is categorically worse than a noisy one** -- it does not merely add variance, it systematically inverts the ranking, so aggregate performance looks acceptable while every individual verdict is backwards. Where a detector needs local correspondence, large signal can be self-defeating, and that must be tested with a *large*-amplitude plant rather than a marginal one.
917. **A DOCSTRING CAN COMMISSION WORK, SO IT MUST BE MAINTAINED AS THOUGH IT WERE THE REPORT.** Fact 1773: three propagation failures in one night, and the third caused a milestone to be commissioned against a claim the same file had already refuted forty lines lower. **Correct knowledge sitting in the tree is not the same as correct knowledge in the corpus**, and the direction of the error is not symmetric -- a stale header is read by whoever opens the file next, which is precisely the person about to act on it. When a finding lands, fix the docstring **and** fold it; and when writing a brief, **quote the file's authoritative declaration rather than its prose summary.**
918. **TO TEST WHETHER A SWITCH REACHES PIXELS, HASH THE OUTPUT -- DO NOT REASON ABOUT THE CALL GRAPH.** Fact 1775: ORCH spent the night warning the fleet about a silently inert gate and prescribed a remedy (read the source) that **most agents cannot apply, because the file belongs to another lane.** The byte-hash A/B answers the same question from outside, in one command, with no ownership required. **Prefer a black-box discriminator over a white-box argument whenever both are available** -- the black-box version survives lane boundaries, stale docstrings, and an author's belief about their own code, all three of which failed somewhere in this project tonight.
919. **PUT THE KNOWN-INERT ARMS IN THE SAME TABLE AS THE RESULT.** Fact 1776: including `0`, `off` and unset arms costs one run each and converts an A/B from a claim into a commissioned instrument, because arms **proved** inert by the same measurement demonstrate that the discriminator is capable of returning the inert verdict. **A switch A/B without inert arms cannot distinguish `the switch works` from `my test cannot fail`** -- and the four-way agreement additionally proves the off-path is insensitive to *how* the switch is spelled, which is its own class of bug.
920. **A FEATURE WHOSE MEASURED SCALE MATCHES A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT IS AN ARTEFACT YOU OWN, SO CHECK THE CONSTANTS BEFORE BLAMING THE PHYSICS.** Fact 1778: the halo's width matched `WINDOW_RADIUS` and matched no optical quantity -- defocus radius, object size and focus step were all excluded. **The discriminating test is cheap and should be routine:** derive the predicted extent from the source constants, then check whether the measurement tracks *those* or the physical alternatives. A defect attributed to the lens is a capture problem; the same defect attributed to a window radius is a one-line change.
921. **AN APPARENT EFFECT THAT NEVER ENDS IS A GRADIENT, AND A SINGLE UNMERGED FRAME IS THE CONTROL THAT SAYS SO.** Fact 1779: M121's largest and most exciting rim measurement (**+0.1326**) failed two checks it applied to itself -- it **did not terminate within 30 px**, and **one unmerged frame reproduced its shape**, which no merge artefact can do. Both checks cost minutes. **Require every claimed local artefact to demonstrate a spatial extent that ends, and to be absent from a single input frame**, because a background gradient, a vignette and an illumination falloff all masquerade as a rim when the profile window is too short to see them close.
922. **A VERDICT THAT SURVIVES THE WITHDRAWAL OF ITS OWN SUPPORTING ARGUMENTS IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE THAT NEVER LOST ANY.** Fact 1783: V-CA entered with five objections, **destroyed four of them itself** -- including the one it had been commissioned to press, which was refuted *in sign* -- and reached the same conclusion on the remainder. **Record which arguments fell alongside the verdict they failed to change**, because a conclusion re-derived from a smaller base is better evidenced than the original, and because the withdrawn arguments are exactly the ones a future reader would otherwise re-litigate. The inverse is the warning: a case whose every limb still stands has usually not been pressed.
923. **A SIGN ERROR IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY TEST THAT CHECKS MAGNITUDE, SO IT NEEDS ITS OWN ARM.** Fact 1784: an inverted correction shipped past **9/9 unit tests and mutation testing**, and was caught only by looking at a render. Magnitude-based assertions -- tolerances, ratios, error norms, even mutation coverage -- are **symmetric in the quantity's sign** and cannot express the failure. **Any correction with a direction must carry an explicit `anti` arm** that applies the deliberately inverted profile and requires the metric to get *worse*; if it does not, the sign is untested no matter how green the suite is.
924. **REPORT THE RAW STATISTIC BESIDE EVERY EXCESS-OVER-CONTROL, IN THE SAME TABLE.** Fact 1785: the excess said *step up*, the raw statistic said *falling*, and **they disagreed in sign** -- so the direction of the reported effect was entirely the control's. One extra column would have caught the withdrawn item before it was sent, and the same column showed the surviving item was **stronger** than its author had claimed. A control is a subtrahend, and **a subtrahend with structure of its own is indistinguishable from a result** unless the minuend is printed next to it.
925. **A CONTROL THAT VARIES SYSTEMATICALLY ALONG THE AXIS YOU ARE BINNING ON IS NOT A CONTROL ON THAT AXIS.** Fact 1785: the null's efficacy decayed with radius, and the finding was reported *per radial decile*. The control was strongest where the claim was weakest and collapsed where the claim was made. **Before binning an excess along any axis, plot the control alone against that axis**; if it has a trend there, the excess inherits it and the binned result measures the control. This is the structural analogue of expanding a control **algebraically** in the terms it combines -- **expand it geometrically in the coordinate you are about to slice.**
## 6. Novelty — verified gaps, labelled as bets

Recorded with their queries; **all are UNVERIFIED as wins, and none is on the v1 default path.**

- **SR from focus-breathing sub-pixel diversity.** 4 arXiv queries, 0 relevant results. Breathing
